The WorkSource names Chrome, also when the page runs inside an installed WebAPK, and `ACQ` says how long ago the page took it.

**해결:**
- Find the site's WebAPK without pulling APKs: `for p in $(adb shell pm list packages | grep webapk | cut -d: -f2); do echo "$p $(adb shell dumpsys package $p | grep -o '<host>' | head -1)"; done`. The one that prints the host is the site's app (one of 25 here).
- Open the installed app at any page: `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d https://<host>/<path> -p <webapk package>`. It opens in `SameTaskWebApkActivity` (standalone, no URL bar), so `display-mode: standalone` code paths run.
- Then `adb shell dumpsys power | grep SCREEN_BRIGHT_WAKE_LOCK` shows whether the wake lock is held.

## OPS-369 — safaridriver "Some devices were found, but could not be used" names the cause on the next line; for a paired iPad it was `device is locked`

`측정 2026-10-07 · /usr/bin/safaridriver (macOS 27) → iPad mini 5 (iPad11,1) · iPadOS 26.7.1 · paired over the local network, not USB`

**증상:** `POST /session` with `{"browserName":"safari","platformName":"iOS","safari:deviceUDID":"<udid>"}` returned `session not created: Could not create a session: Some devices were found, but could not be used`. The same capabilities had opened sessions on this iPad two days earlier (OPS-351), so the capabilities were suspected first. Tools that print only the first line of the error hide the reason.

The full `message` carries a list after a newline: `- iPad mini (00008020-…): device is locked`. `xcrun devicectl device info lockState --device <udid>` showed `passcodeRequired: true` at the same moment. Web Inspector and Remote Automation were still on.

**해결:** read the whole `message`, not its first line. For `device is locked`, unlock the device by hand (a passcode cannot be entered by a session) and set Settings > Display & Brightness > Auto-Lock to Never for the test run. Check `devicectl device info lockState` before opening a session. The device was also listed as `connected (no DDI)` with `Transport Type: localNetwork`; the working sessions in OPS-351 were over USB.

## OPS-370 — 무료 개발자 팀(Personal Team)으로 서명한 XCUITest 러너는 실기기에 이미 무료 프로필 앱이 3개 있으면 설치되지 않는다

`측정 2026-10-07 · Xcode 27 xcodebuild test-without-building · iPad mini 5(iPad11,1) · iPadOS 26.7.1 · 팀 "Ricky Cho (Personal Team)" UXJJ94BPC2`

**증상:** UI 테스트 번들 하나뿐인 프로젝트(OPS-239 방식, `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED = YES`, `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = UXJJ94BPC2`, `-allowProvisioningUpdates`)는 `build-for-testing`까지 성공한다. 그런데 `test-without-building`이 `Failed to install or launch the test runner … 'SimRotateUITests-Runner'을(를) 설치할 수 없음. This device has reached the maximum number of installed apps using a free developer profile`(`MIInstallerErrorDomain` 13)로 끝난다. 그때 기기에는 다른 프로젝트 세션의 개발 빌드 3개(`com.mnori.cobramission.dev`, `com.mnori.monsterworld.dev`, `com.mnori.button.dev`)가 있었다. 러너도 앱 하나로 센다.

**해결:** `xcrun devicectl device info apps --device <udid>`로 무료 프로필 앱을 먼저 센다. 3개면 진짜 탭 검사를 위해 하나를 지워야 하는데, 다른 세션의 빌드이므로 지우기 전에 운영자에게 묻는다. 유료 개발자 팀으로 서명하면 이 한도가 없다.
- 자리를 비운 뒤에도 첫 실행은 `Failed to initialize for UI testing … Timed out while enabling automation mode.`로 끝났다. 그때 기기 화면(`xcrun devicectl device capture screenshot --device <udid> --destination x.png`)에는 "'XCTest'의 Touch ID · Enable UI Automation" 창이 떠 있었다. 실기기 UI 자동화는 처음 켤 때 기기 주인의 지문이나 암호가 필요하다. 세션이 할 수 없는 단계이므로 이 화면을 띄워 둔 채 운영자에게 알린다.
- 그 뒤 실제로 돌릴 때의 함정 둘(같은 날): ① Safari 웹 콘텐츠 버튼은 `safari.buttons["음성으로 듣기"]`(identifier 일치)로 찾지 못한다. `buttons.matching(NSPredicate(format: "label == %@", "음성으로 듣기"))`로 찾는다. ② safaridriver 세션을 끝내지 않고 드라이버를 죽이면 Safari가 주황 주소창의 자동화 창에 남는다. URL을 열 때마다 "Safari가 자동 테스트를 실행 중입니다" 창이 다시 뜨고, XCUITest가 "테스트 세션 중단"을 눌러도 되풀이된다. `xcrun devicectl device info processes --device <udid> | grep MobileSafari`로 pid를 찾아 `xcrun devicectl device process terminate --device <udid> --pid <pid>`로 Safari를 끝내면 평소 창으로 돌아온다. "자동화 끄기"는 누르지 않는다. 원격 자동화 설정이 꺼져 safaridriver를 다시 켜려면 기기에서 사람이 손대야 한다.
- 지운 다른 세션의 앱은 그 프로젝트의 `build/ios/*.ipa`를 풀어 `xcrun devicectl device install app --device <udid> Payload/<name>.app`으로 다시 넣을 수 있다(무료 프로필 만료일 안에서만). 앱 데이터는 지울 때 사라진다.

## OPS-371 — 위키백과 조회수로 인기순을 매길 때: 조회수 API는 리다이렉트를 따라가지 않고, 한국어 문서 제목은 개역개정 표기가 아니다

`측정 2026-10-08 · Wikimedia REST pageviews per-article · MediaWiki action=query · ko/en Wikipedia · 성경 인물 171명`

**증상:** `https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/metrics/pageviews/per-article/ko.wikipedia/all-access/user/<제목>/monthly/<시작>/<끝>`에 흔히 쓰는 이름을 넣으면 수치가 0에 가깝거나 404가 난다. 이 API는 리다이렉트 문서의 조회수를 그 문서 몫으로 따로 센다. 정식 문서로 넘겨 주지 않는다. 조회가 한 번도 없는 기간은 오류가 아니라 404로 온다. 한국어 위키백과 성경 인물 문서는 공동번역·가톨릭 표기가 정식 제목이다(`사도 바울로`, `폰티우스 필라투스`, `유다 이스카리옷`, `히즈키야`). 같은 이름의 다른 인물이 정식 문서를 차지한 경우도 있었다(ko `호세아`는 북이스라엘 왕, en `Micah`는 인명 안내 문서).

**해결:** 제목은 먼저 `https://<lang>.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&format=json&formatversion=2&redirects=1&prop=pageprops&titles=A|B|…`(50개씩)로 확인한다. `redirects`에 잡히면 정식 제목으로 고치고, `pageprops.disambiguation`이 있으면 동음이의 문서이므로 다른 제목을 찾는다. 조회수의 404는 0회로 센다. User-Agent에 연락처가 든 이름을 붙이고 동시 요청 4개로 171명 × 2개 언어가 47초 걸렸다. 화면에 보이는 이름은 독자에게 익숙한 표기로 따로 둔다. 구현: who.withthebible.com `scripts/build-people.mjs`.

## OPS-372 — Census Data API는 이제 키 없는 요청을 302로 돌려보낸다; 키 없이 ACS를 읽으려면 Census Reporter API를 쓴다

`측정 2026-10-07 · api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs1 · api.censusreporter.org/1.0 · ACS 2020–2024 5-year`

**증상:** `curl "https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs1?get=NAME,B02015_005E&for=state:06"`이 본문 없이 끝나고, JSON 파싱이 `Expecting value: line 1 column 1`로 실패한다. 응답은 `HTTP 302`, `Location: https://api.census.gov/data/missing_key.html`, 헤더 `X-DataWebAPI-KeyError: 1`이다. 첫 요청부터 막힌다. 변수 목록(`/variables/<id>.json`, `/groups/<table>.json`)은 키 없이 읽힌다.

**해결:** 키를 받으려면 `https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html`에서 이메일로 받아 `&key=`를 붙인다. 키 없이 바로 읽어야 하면 Census Reporter가 같은 ACS 표를 준다: `https://api.censusreporter.org/1.0/data/show/latest?table_ids=B02015,B02018&geo_ids=31000US19740,05000US34003,04000US08`. 응답의 `release`가 실제 연도를 알려 준다(이날은 `acs2024_5yr`, 1년치가 아니라 5년치). geo id는 메트로 `31000US<CBSA>`, 카운티 `05000US<주FIPS><카운티FIPS>`, 주 `04000US<FIPS>`이고, 값은 `data[geo][table].estimate["B02015005"]`처럼 변수 이름에서 밑줄과 `E`를 뺀 키로 온다. 예: 한국계 단독 `B02015_005`, 단독 또는 혼합 `B02018_005`.

## OPS-373 — Dokploy compose deploy fails with "pull access denied" when a locally built image lost its tag, even though the running container still uses that image

`측정 2026-10-07 · Dokploy compose (raw source), Docker on the host, locally built images (no registry)`

**증상:** a web-only redeploy kept the other service's release in `.env`
(`LANDGRAB_SPACETIME_RELEASE=20261005-harder`). `docker compose up -d --build` stopped with
`Image landgrab-spacetime:20261005-harder Error pull access denied for landgrab-spacetime, repository does not exist or may require 'docker login'`
and Dokploy reported the compose as `error`. `docker inspect` on the running container still showed
`Config.Image = landgrab-spacetime:20261005-harder`, but `docker images` listed that image ID
(`07700a907c82`) only under another tag (`20261005-reports`). A container keeps running on an image
whose tag has moved or been removed; compose resolves the tag again on the next `up` and, finding no
local image and no registry, tries to pull.

**해결:** re-tag the image the container is running (`docker tag <repo>:<tag-that-exists> <repo>:<tag-in-.env>`,
same image ID, no rebuild and no data touched) and deploy again. Before a partial deploy that reuses
another service's tag, check `docker image inspect <repo>:<tag>` exists.

## OPS-374 — 실기기 iPad의 XCUITest는 xcodebuild를 돌릴 때마다 Touch ID "Enable UI Automation"을 다시 요구했다. 사람 손이 올 때까지 1분 간격으로 다시 돌리면 된다

`측정 2026-10-08 · Xcode 27 xcodebuild test-without-building · iPad mini 5(iPad11,1) · iPadOS 26.7.1 · Personal Team 서명 UI 테스트 번들`

**증상:** 한 번 지문으로 UI 자동화를 켜고 테스트가 끝까지 돈 뒤, 몇 분 뒤 같은 러너로 `test-without-building`을 다시 돌리자 또 `Failed to initialize for UI testing … Timed out while enabling automation mode.`(약 60초 대기)로 끝났다. 기기 화면에는 다시 "'XCTest'의 Touch ID · Enable UI Automation" 창이 떠 있었다(OPS-370은 처음 켤 때만 필요하다고 적었지만, 이날은 실행마다 필요했다). 실패한 실행은 테스트가 실패한 뒤에도 xcodebuild가 진단 수집에서 몇 분 동안 끝나지 않기도 했다.

**해결:** 루프로 `test-without-building`을 다시 돌리고, 로그에 `Timed out while enabling automation mode`가 없을 때 멈춘다(이날 5번째 시도에서 지문이 와서 통과). 그동안 운영자에게 지문 한 번을 부탁한다. 결과 확인은 `-resultBundlePath`로 받은 xcresult에서 `xcrun xcresulttool export attachments --path … --output-path …`로 `XCTAttachment(screenshot:)` 화면과 화면 녹화(mp4)를 꺼내 본다. 진단에서 멈춘 xcodebuild는 결과 번들이 이미 쓰였으면 죽여도 된다.

## OPS-375 — Cloudflare: an origin that sends no `Cache-Control` gets its .js/.css held at the edge for the zone's browser TTL (4 h) after a deploy; `no-cache` fixes the edge, but browsers still receive `max-age=14400`. POST to `/api/v4` from the dashboard session is blocked, the 「사용자 지정 제거」 dialog is not

`측정 2026-10-08 · Cloudflare free plan, zone browser cache TTL 4시간 · FastAPI StaticFiles origin behind a Cloudflare Tunnel · Brave 1.96 Playwright persistent profile · Speak Out`

**증상:** after two deploys 13 minutes apart, `audio.js` came back `cf-cache-status: HIT`, `age: 925`, with the first deploy's content, while `?v=<random>` returned the new file. Starlette `StaticFiles` sends `ETag` and `Last-Modified` but no `Cache-Control`, so the edge kept the file for the zone's 4 h TTL. One page can then load scripts from two different commits.

- With the origin sending `Cache-Control: no-cache`, the edge answers `cf-cache-status: REVALIDATED` and serves the new file at once. **But the response to the browser still says `cache-control: max-age=14400`**: the zone's browser cache TTL overrides the origin's `no-cache`. A plain `fetch()` in a service worker, or a returning visitor without one, can still reuse a 4 h old file from the browser's HTTP cache.
- Purging by URL: `POST /api/v4/zones/<id>/purge_cache` from the dashboard page (headers `x-cross-site-security: dash` and `x-atok: window.bootstrap.atok`) returned `403` with an HTML block page; GET `/zones?name=…` worked with the same headers (same as OPS-111). The UI path works: `…/<account>/<zone>/caching/configuration` → button 「사용자 지정 제거」 → in the `[role=dialog]` choose 「URL」, fill its `textarea` with one URL per line, press 「제거」. The next request was `MISS` with the new content.
- Files the edge cached **before** the origin started sending `no-cache` did not pick it up: after the next deploy `sw.js` came back `cf-cache-status: STALE` with the old content on three requests in a row. One more purge by URL, then `MISS` and `REVALIDATED` from there on.

**해결:** send `Cache-Control: no-cache` for every static file, then purge those URLs once (in Starlette, subclass `StaticFiles` and set the header in `file_response`). In the service worker, fetch with `{cache: 'no-cache'}` so the browser revalidates by ETag instead of trusting the rewritten `max-age`. To stop the rewrite itself, set a cache rule for the hostname with browser TTL `respect_origin` (OPS-301); changing the zone-wide browser TTL also changes every other site on the zone.

## OPS-376 — Android WebView app on `WebViewAssetLoader`: a link to `/` shows an error page, and `dumpsys vibrator_manager` shows whether a `performHapticFeedback` from the JS bridge actually played

`측정 2026-10-08 · Pixel 7 Pro, Android 16, WebView 154.0.8037.106 · androidx.webkit WebViewAssetLoader (AssetsPathHandler on "/") · Speak Out release build`

**증상:** the page loads as `https://appassets.androidplatform.net/index.html`. Following a plain `<a href="/">` (here the logo, reached by Enter on the focused link) asked the loader for the asset path "", which logs `E WebViewAssetLoader: Error opening asset path: … FileNotFoundException`. The app showed 「웹페이지를 사용할 수 없음」 with `net::ERR_INVALID_RESPONSE`. The same link works on the website.

- Haptics through a `@JavascriptInterface` method that calls `webView.performHapticFeedback(…)` need no VIBRATE permission. To verify them on the device, `adb shell dumpsys vibrator_manager` lists each one with the app's package, `reason: performHapticFeedback(constant=17)` and the outcome: `finished` (`Prebaked=DOUBLE_CLICK` for REJECT, `TEXTURE_TICK` for CLOCK_TICK) while the app is in front, and `ignored_background` (nothing felt) once another app has the focus.
- A release build with WebView debugging off can still be driven: build the same release once with `setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true)`, `adb install -r` it (same upload key, the app's data is kept), `adb forward tcp:9333 localabstract:webview_devtools_remote_<pid>` and send `Runtime.evaluate` to the page's `webSocketDebuggerUrl`. Reinstall the normal build afterwards.

**해결:** never navigate to `/` inside the asset origin. Handle the logo in script, or link to `/index.html`. Check haptics in `dumpsys vibrator_manager` with the app in front.

## OPS-377 — macOS Safari WebDriver over ssh: writing `AllowRemoteAutomation` to the plist does not enable it, and a locked console leaves GUI scripting with no windows

`측정 2026-10-08 · macOS 27.0.1, Safari 27.0.1 · ssh session without sudo · MacBook Air (M1)`

**증상:** a browser test needed real Safari on a shared test Mac. `safaridriver -p <port>` started, but `POST /session` with `{"capabilities":{"alwaysMatch":{"browserName":"safari"}}}` answered 500 `session not created`: "You must enable 'Allow remote automation' in the Developer section of Safari Settings to control Safari via WebDriver." It still answered that after `defaults write com.apple.Safari AllowRemoteAutomation 1`, with the same key already `1` in `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari/Data/Library/Preferences/com.apple.Safari.plist` and `IncludeDevelopMenu` `1`. The setting is not read from those keys; `safaridriver --enable` needs an administrator password.

GUI scripting was the next attempt. `osascript` over ssh could list processes through System Events and click the Safari menu's "설정…" item without an error, but `count of windows` of process Safari stayed 0. The console was locked: `ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` showed `"CGSSessionScreenIsLocked"=Yes`. Headed Godot and Chromium runs still render on a locked console, so the lock does not show up until a GUI step finds no windows.

**해결:** check the lock before planning any Safari GUI step (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep -o 'CGSSessionScreenIsLocked"=[A-Za-z]*'`). Enable remote automation once, on an unlocked console, through Safari Settings > Developer or `safaridriver --enable` with an admin password; plist writes do not do it. Without WebDriver, real Safari still runs a page test on an unlocked Mac: serve a local copy of the page on `http://localhost:<port>` (a secure context) with the measuring script injected at the top of `<head>` and a `setInterval` that `fetch`es its results to a small POST handler on the same server; open it with `open -a Safari <url>`; give the user gesture with `osascript` System Events `click at {x, y}` inside the front window (measured 2026-10-08, Safari 27.0.1: the click resumed the page's `AudioContext` to `running`, and sound reached the destination in 242 of 246 100 ms windows). Close only that tab afterwards (loop Safari's tabs and close those whose `URL` starts with the test address).

## OPS-378 — `codex exec` as an unattended text and research worker on a ChatGPT login: old CLIs reject newer models, `--output-schema` must be strict, and opened pages show up as `view` results

`measured 2026-10-08 · codex-cli 0.154.0 → 0.162.0 (Homebrew), ChatGPT login, macOS`

**Symptom 1:** `codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol` fails at once with `The 'gpt-6.1-sol' model is not supported when using Codex
with a ChatGPT account.` (preceded by `Model metadata for 'gpt-6.1-sol' not found`). The same login runs `gpt-6-astra`, and
the ChatGPT app's bundled CLI (0.160.1) runs both. The model list is served per client version: `brew upgrade codex` to 0.162.0
fixed it. `~/.codex/models_cache.json` shows the slugs and the `client_version` the list was fetched for.

**Symptom 2:** `--output-schema` with a loose schema (an object property typed only `{"type":["object","null"]}`) fails the
turn: `Invalid schema for response_format 'codex_output_schema': 'schema.additionalProperties' is required to be supplied and
to be false when strict is true.` Every object needs `additionalProperties: false` and all its properties in `required`.
`minItems`/`maxItems`, `minimum`/`maximum` and `enum` are accepted. For a free-form result, drop `--output-schema`, ask for
"one JSON object, no code fences" and parse the last `agent_message` (strip fences, take first `{` to last `}`).

**Facts for an isolated worker:**
- `codex login status` prints to **stderr**, not stdout (`Logged in using ChatGPT` / `Logged in using an API key ...`).
- `--ignore-user-config` skips `~/.codex/config.toml` (MCP servers, plugins, `service_tier`), but auth still comes from
  `CODEX_HOME`. Add `--ephemeral --ignore-rules --sandbox read-only -c approval_policy="never"`, and turn tools off with
  `--disable shell_tool --disable unified_exec --disable apps --disable plugins --disable image_generation --disable multi_agent`
  (names from `codex features list`). A run like that made zero `command_execution` items.
- `-c web_search="live"` turns on web search; `"disabled"` turns it off.
- With `--json`, each search is an `item.completed` of type `web_search`. `action.type` is `search` (with `queries`) or
  `open_page` (with one `url`), sometimes `other`. **One open item can carry several opened pages**: the results list each
  with a `ref_id` like `turn2view1` and the snippet `Total lines: N`. Search hits have `turnNsearchM` (also `youtube`,
  `reddit`, `academia`). Failed opens come back as `view` results with an empty `url` and `Total lines: 1`. So "pages the model
  actually read" = results whose `ref_id` ends in `view<N>` with a non-empty URL.
- bible.com range pages such as `/ko/bible/86/NUM.27.1-11.KLB` came back empty three times; chapter pages
  (`/ko/bible/86/NUM.27.KLB`) opened.
- One research-and-write job (study prompt of about 15k characters, gpt-6.1-sol, effort high) took 725 s and opened 11 pages
  on 7 domains.

**Fix:** keep Codex current; write strict schemas or parse JSON text; count `view` results with a URL as read sources.

## OPS-379 — Putting a large binary on Google Drive with a public link, unattended: Drive's web UI in Brave on the Air, the new-file button is `신규`, and the share dialog lives in a frame

`측정 2026-10-09 · drive.google.com web UI (Korean) · Brave 1.96 · playwright-core · air.local (~/kc-test/profile)`

**증상:** a 71 MB `.dmg` had to be shared by link. The Drive connector takes file content as one base64 string in a
tool call, which is not a way to move tens of megabytes. Scripting the web UI failed twice on details: a
`getByRole("button", { name: /새로 만들기|New/ })` waited 20 s for a file chooser and timed out, because the Korean
UI labels the button **`신규`**; and after the share dialog opened, `page.getByText("링크가 있는 모든 사용자")` on the
top frame found nothing.

**해결:**
- Open the signed-in profile (`~/kc-test/kc-browser.mjs` `open()`), go to `https://drive.google.com/drive/my-drive`,
  start `page.waitForEvent("filechooser")`, click the button named `/신규|새로 만들기|^New$/`, then the menuitem
  `/파일 업로드|File upload/`, and `setFiles(path)`. Poll the page text for `업로드 완료`; 71 MB from the Air took under a
  minute. Script: `~/kc-test/drive-upload.mjs <file>`.
- Share: click the file's name in the list (it selects the row), click the button named `/공유|Share/`, then click the
  `제한됨` dropdown under 일반 액세스 (by position worked) and search **every frame** (`page.frames()`) for the exact text
  `링크가 있는 모든 사용자`; then the frame's `완료` button. The toast says `액세스 권한이 업데이트됨`. Script:
  `~/kc-test/drive-share.mjs <file name>`.
- Verify without a browser: the Drive connector's `get_file_permissions` lists `{"role":"reader","type":"anyone"}`,
  and an anonymous `curl -sL "https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=<id>&export=download"` returns Google's
  **Virus scan warning** page for a file this size. That page is normal: a person clicks through it to download.

## OPS-380 — SpacetimeDB 2.8 Rust module: `#[default(-1i32)]` does not compile; a named constant does, and migrates existing rows to -1

`측정 2026-10-09 · spacetimedb crate =2.8.0 · SpacetimeDB server 2.8.0 (local standalone) · Rust 1.97.1 · wasm32`

**증상:** appending `#[default(-1i32)] pub play_day: i32` to a live table failed to build, with the error pointing at the
table attribute rather than the column:

```
error[E0600]: cannot apply unary operator `-` to type `AlgebraicValue`
   --> server/src/lib.rs:281:1
    | #[table(accessor = game, public)]
```

The macro expands a default as `#val.serialize(ValueSerializer)`. With `val` = `-1i32` that is `-1i32.serialize(..)`,
which Rust parses as `-(1i32.serialize(..))`: a negation of the serialised value. `#[default((-1i32))]` compiles, but
rustc then warns `unnecessary parentheses around assigned value` and its suggested fix is the form that does not
build. Positive literals (`#[default(0u32)]`, `#[default(1250i32)]`) are unaffected.

**해결:** name the value: `const NO_DAY: i32 = -1;` and `#[default(NO_DAY)]`. No warning, and a data-keeping publish
(`spacetime publish … -y`, no `-c`) migrated the table in place: all 189 existing rows read `-1` in the new column.

## OPS-381 — `rsync -a` to a build host keeps old source mtimes, cargo skips the rebuild, and `spacetime publish` reports "Updated database" with the old module

`측정 2026-10-09 · rsync 2.6.9 (macOS) · cargo 1.97.1 · spacetime CLI 2.8.0 · MacBook Air test host`

**증상:** a tree was copied to `~/work/<copy>` on the test host with `rsync -az --exclude target`, built and published
once, then later refreshed with newer Rust sources (edited earlier in the day on another machine) and published again.
`spacetime publish --module-path server --server local mydb -y` printed `Updated database with name: mydb`, but
`curl http://127.0.0.1:3002/v1/database/mydb/schema?version=9` still listed the old tables. Clients then failed with
`subscription refused: no such table: mission`.

`rsync -a` preserves each file's modification time. The new sources had been *edited* at 08:10–08:17, while the
`target/` on the host (kept, because `target` was excluded from the copy) had been built at 09:30 from the older
sources. Cargo compares mtimes, saw every source older than its artifact, and reused the old wasm. Nothing in the
publish output says the module was not rebuilt.

**해결:** after refreshing sources with `rsync -a` into a tree whose `target/` survives, `touch` the crate sources (or
`cargo clean -p <crate>`) before building, then verify the published schema, not the CLI's word:
`touch server/src/*.rs shared/src/*.rs && spacetime publish … -y && curl -s …/schema?version=9 | jq '.tables[].name'`.
Alternatively copy with `rsync -rlz` (no `-t`) so the copies take the time they arrive.

## OPS-382 — Eclipse links: NASA's per-eclipse Google map pages no longer draw a map, and timeanddate.com answers 403 to curl but loads in Brave

`측정 2026-10-10 · eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov SEgoogle pages · timeanddate.com · Brave 1.96 on the MacBook Air test host`

**증상:** NASA GSFC's interactive path maps (`https://eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov/SEgoogle/SEgoogle2001/SE2027Aug02Tgoogle.html`
and the same pattern for every eclipse) answer 200 to curl and still show their text, controls and "Greatest Duration"
paragraphs, but the map area is blank in Brave: the page loads Google Maps with a retired v2 `key=ABQIAAAA…`, and no
`.gm-style` element ever appears. A status-code link check passes while the reader sees no map.

The obvious replacement, `https://www.timeanddate.com/eclipse/solar/<year>-<month name>-<day>` (e.g. `2027-august-2`,
`2035-september-2`), returns **403 to curl** even with a desktop browser User-Agent and `Accept` headers, so a curl
link check wrongly reports it dead. In headed Brave through Playwright all eight pages 2027–2038 returned 200 with
the path map, a 3D globe and local times. The NASA decade tables (`/SEdecade/SEdecade2021.html`) and
`https://science.nasa.gov/eclipses/future-eclipses/` answer 200 to curl and render.

**해결:** link eclipse paths to timeanddate.com, and check such links with a real browser rather than curl. Treat a
200 from curl as proof only that the server answered, not that a JavaScript map drew.

## OPS-383 — Android FPS without an in-game probe: SurfaceFlinger timestats, but one layer is split into a block per refresh rate

`측정 2026-10-10 · Pixel 7 Pro (Android 16) · adb 1.0.41 · Godot 4.7.2 debug APK (Vulkan SurfaceView)`

**증상:** a release-style export leaves `tools/*` out, so an in-game FPS probe is not in the APK, and
`dumpsys gfxinfo` sees only HWUI views, not a Godot/Unity `SurfaceView`. SurfaceFlinger's timestats measure any app:
`adb shell dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --timestats -clear` then `-enable`, play, `-dump`, `-disable`. Each layer block has
`totalFrames`, `averageFPS` and a `present2present histogram` (`16ms=…  33ms=…  50ms=…`), which gives the share of
frames over a budget directly. The trap: when the panel switches between 60 and 120 Hz during the window, **the same
`layerName` appears in several blocks**, one per `displayRefreshRate`/`renderRate` pair, and reading the first block
shows only part of the run (a 28 s walk read as 564 frames over 14.5 s). Blocks from another app's layer (the
launcher) in the same dump mean something else took the screen mid-run.

**해결:** sum every block whose `layerName` contains the package, and take FPS as intervals over the histogram's summed
time (Σ bucket × count), not any single `averageFPS`. Check the foreground before and during the run on a shared phone
(AGT-044). Record `dumpsys thermalservice` status at the end: a 3-minute walk took the Pixel from status 0 to 2.

## OPS-384 — Real shape models of Phobos, Itokawa, Ryugu and Bennu for the web: where they are, and their frames match the USGS feature coordinates

`측정 2026-10-10 · PDS SBN Gaskell 64q · JAXA DARTS SFM 49k · NASA SVS 5069 OLA v20 · USGS nomenclature KMZ · three.js 0.186`

**증상:** NASA's 3D Resources repo has no Phobos, Itokawa or Ryugu model, and its "1999 RQ36" Bennu is the pre-mission radar shape. Searching for "glb" finds only that, a 840 KB Bennu with an unknown frame and 300 MB+ files.

Sources that work, all in the bodies' own fixed frame (x toward 0°E, z north, km), so feature coordinates land on the right spot:
- Itokawa: `https://sbnarchive.psi.edu/pds3/hayabusa/HAY_A_AMICA_5_ITOKAWASHAPE_V1_0/data/vertex/ver64q.tab` (4.2 MB text, 25,350 vertices, 49,152 plates; line 1 = counts, then `id x y z`, then `id a b c` 1-based).
- Phobos: `https://sbnarchive.psi.edu/pds4/non_mission/gaskell.phobos.shape-model/data/phobos_ver64q.tab` (same layout).
- Ryugu: `https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/hayabusa2/paper/Watanabe_2019/SHAPE_SFM_49k_v20180804.obj` (2.6 MB OBJ; README says "as is", credit JAXA / Watanabe et al. 2019).
- Bennu: `https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/vis/a000000/a005000/a005069/g_00880mm_alt_ptm_0000n00000_v020.glb` (60.6 MB, 3.4 M triangles, positions in km, uint32 indices; the node matrix only turns z-up into y-up). The TAG-site model on the same page is named `l_00050mm_alt_ptm_5595n04217_v020`, i.e. Nightingale at 55.95°N 42.17°E.
- Feature names and centres: `https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/images/<TARGET>_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz` (PHOBOS, ITOKAWA, RYUGU, BENNU). The KML's `center_lon` is **east-positive 0–360** (Stickney 311), even though the website shows Phobos in west longitude (Stickney "49").

Check: with Gaskell's Phobos rendered in three.js, a marker at 1°N 311°E sits exactly in Stickney's bowl.

**해결:** quantise to int16 positions + uint16 indices (25 k vertices fit) — about 450 KB per body, ~40 % smaller gzipped; vertex clustering cut Bennu from 3.4 M to 44 k triangles. Converter: `parklab/scripts/convert-shape-model.py`.

## OPS-385 — AdMob "스토어 추가" finds a newly published Play app only by its full store URL, not by package name

`측정 2026-10-10 · AdMob web (ko UI) · Play app com.mnori.landgrab live since 2026-10-05 · Brave on the Air with the owner's profile`

**증상:** an AdMob app created before its Play listing went live shows 「검토 필요 · 광고 게재가 제한됨 · 스토어를 추가하여 한도 해제」. In 「스토어 추가」 → Google Play, searching the package name `com.mnori.landgrab` returned no row ("앱을 찾을 수 없는 경우 앱 스토어 세부사항을 확인한 후 다시 시도해 보세요"), and searching the Korean title returned only other developers' apps. The listing was public (HTTP 200) for five days.

**해결:** paste the full listing URL `https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=<package>` into the same search box. It returned the app at once (under its English listing name). Then 추가 → 계속 → 패키지 이름 확인 → 저장. The app turns to 「준비 중 · 검토 중」; Google's ad-serving review takes 2–3 days. The other MNORI apps on the same AdMob account (버튼, 곰 사냥꾼) were still unlinked on 2026-10-10.

## OPS-386 — The Air test host cleans itself under 32 GB free: idle folders lose `node_modules`/`target`/`.godot`, week-idle `~/work` copies are deleted; protect one with `.air-keep`

`측정 2026-10-10 · MacBook Air M1 (192.168.0.123), macOS, LaunchAgent com.mnori.air-clean`

**증상:** the Air's data volume was down to 13 GB free (owner, 2026-10-10). 100 GB of the 142 GB home
was `~/work`: 143 project copies nobody had touched for a day held 29 GB of `node_modules`,
`target` and `.godot`, and 24 copies of repositories that also live on the Mac held 20 GB more.
`/private/var/folders/*/*/X/com.brave.Browser.code_sign_clone` showed 13 GB (24 clones, one per
Brave launched by a test and killed), but they are APFS clones: deleting all 24 freed about 1 GB.

Owner's standing rule: when less than 32 GB is free, delete what is not needed. Implemented as
`~/.local/bin/air-clean.sh`, run by the LaunchAgent `com.mnori.air-clean` every 30 minutes and at
login; a run with 32 GB or more free does nothing. Under the limit it deletes, in order:

1. Brave `code_sign_clone` copies no process has open;
2. the uv, npm and pip caches (unless that tool is running);
3. `node_modules`, `target`, `.godot` and `android/build` in every `~/work/*`, `~/codex-runs/*`
   and `~/.codex-landgrab-checks/*` folder with no file changed in 24 hours;
4. this user's `/tmp` entries older than 2 days;
5. only if still under 32 GB: whole `~/work/*` folders with no file changed in 7 days, oldest
   first, until 40 GB is free.

Never: anything a process has open (files or working directory), a folder named by a LaunchAgent
or `~/srv` script, `~/kc-test`, SDKs, models, browsers. Each deletion is logged with its size in
`~/Library/Logs/air-clean.log`. Staleness is judged by **file** times only: deleting a
`node_modules` changes its parent directory's mtime, so a directory-time test calls every
cleaned folder fresh.

**해결:** after syncing to the Air, install dependencies again if `node_modules` (or a Godot
project's `.godot` import cache) is gone; rsync the whole tree if the folder is gone. To keep a
folder through step 5 (an Air-only database or results not yet copied back), `touch
~/work/<folder>/.air-keep`. `AIR_CLEAN_DRY=1 ~/.local/bin/air-clean.sh --force` logs what a run
would delete without deleting.

## OPS-387 — Homebrew `codex` 0.162.0 runs `codex exec` image generation again with a ChatGPT login (OPS-264 no longer applies to it)

`측정 2026-10-10 · codex-cli 0.162.0 (/opt/homebrew/bin/codex) · model gpt-6.1-sol · macOS 27 · ChatGPT login`

**증상:** OPS-264 says the Homebrew CLI fails every `codex exec` once the shared config names a newer model, and to use the ChatGPT app's bundled CLI instead.
After a `brew upgrade` to 0.162.0, the Homebrew binary follows the config's current model: five unattended image generations in a row (OPS-076 wrapper, one empty folder each) all wrote a 1024x1536 PNG, no 400 error.

**해결:** check `codex --version` first. At 0.162.0 or later the Homebrew `codex` on `PATH` works; below it, use the app-bundled CLI as OPS-264 says.

## OPS-388 — Waist-up portraits from image generation: a "belt at the bottom edge" lands near 85 % of a 1536-px canvas, and Vision's foreground mask breaks thin wire props into dashes

`측정 2026-10-10 · codex-cli 0.162.0 image generation (1024x1536) · macOS Vision VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest · Pillow + numpy + scipy`

**증상:** two traps when generating dialogue portraits that are cropped to the top 1024x1280:
1. A prompt that says the bottom edge crosses the waist at the belt line still draws the belt at rows ~1280-1380 of 1536, so a 1280 crop cuts away anything shown at the belt (two generations lost this way).
2. The Vision instance mask, tightened by a plain threshold, turns thin props (bent wire, coat hangers, chains) into dotted lines, and the generator paints a pale grey halo just outside ink lines that a mask-only cut leaves as a grey fringe.

**해결:**
1. Put the position in the character paragraph as a fraction of the image height ("the belt at three quarters of the image height") when the crop must show it; the third generation then kept the belt above row 1280.
2. Inside the mask's soft edge, compute alpha from the colour distance to the flat grey background and project the pixel to the nearest solid foreground colour, then remove grey pockets enclosed between wires and the outermost 1-px blended ring. Light details not connected to the outer background (studs, highlights) survive.

## OPS-389 — `rsync --delete` to a test host's Godot copy deletes the `.import` and `.uid` files Godot wrote there: new fonts then fail with "has no resource loaders"

`측정 2026-10-10 · rsync 3.x · Godot 4.7.2 · macOS 27 (MacBook Air M1 test host)`

**증상:** a sync script mirrored the working tree to the test host with `rsync -az --delete` (excluding `.godot`) and ran `godot --headless --import` there. New `.woff2` fonts and scripts were added locally without their generated `.import` / `.uid` files. The first import on the host wrote them, the next sync deleted them again, and the following test run failed at compile time: `Parse Error: Preload file "res://assets/fonts/Jua-korean.woff2" has no resource loaders (unrecognized file extension)` for every new font. The import log even ended mid-way, so it looked like an import crash.

**해결:** protect generated files on the receiving side: `rsync -az --delete --filter='P *.import' --filter='P *.uid' ...`, import once on the host, then copy the generated files back into the repository (`rsync -az --ignore-existing --include='*/' --include='*.import' --include='*.uid' --exclude='*' host:copy/client/ client/`) so they are committed with the asset, as Godot expects.

## OPS-390 — Frame-time A/B on a shared test host: whole runs swing 14 → 35 ms; alternate the switch in 0.4 s windows and compare the fastest window of each side

`측정 2026-10-10 · Godot 4.7.2 · macOS 27 (MacBook Air M1 test host, other sessions rendering)`

**증상:** two back-to-back runs of the same build measured 14.7 and 24.0 ms a frame on a test host where another session's Godot test was rendering; switching one feature off between runs gave "savings" from −1.9 to +6.4 ms for the same switch. Averaging three on/off pairs of 2 s still swung by several ms, because the other session's load starts and stops mid-run.

**해결:** toggle the feature inside one run and compare in short alternating windows. Two estimates held steady: the median of seven paired 1.2 s differences, and, better, the minimum over sixteen 0.4 s windows on each side (other work only ever adds time, so the fastest window is the uncontended one). The same switch then read 2.05 / 2.19 ms in two runs and 0.24 / 0.29 ms after a fix. Find the CPU floor the same way with `RenderingServer.render_loop_enabled = false` (the scripts kept running at 0.26 ms a frame: the frame was all rendering). Log `uptime` with each run.

## OPS-391 — `dd` to a USB stick from an agent session fails with "Operation not permitted" even as root; run it from a Terminal `.command` file

`측정 2026-10-10 · macOS 27 (Darwin 27.0.0) · Claude Code in VS Code · SanDisk Cruzer Glide 32 GB`

**증상:** writing an ISO to a USB stick from a Claude Code (VS Code) Bash session. `/dev/rdisk6` is `root:operator 640`, so root is needed; `osascript -e 'do shell script "dd if=… of=/dev/rdisk6 bs=4m" with administrator privileges'` showed the password dialog and ran as root, yet failed twice:
1. `dd: /Users/<user>/Downloads/<file>.iso: Operation not permitted` — the root process could not read `~/Downloads`, although the same session's own `cp` could.
2. After copying the ISO to `/private/tmp`: `dd: /dev/rdisk6: Operation not permitted`. Same result with the command sandbox disabled. TCC attributes the process to the agent's app, which has no raw-disk access.

`osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to do script …'` timed out (`AppleEvent 시간이 초과되었습니다 (-1712)`) waiting on the Automation permission prompt.

**해결:** put the commands in an executable `.command` file and run `open -a Terminal flash.command` (no Automation permission needed). The file runs `diskutil unmountDisk /dev/diskN` then `sudo dd if=/private/tmp/…iso of=/dev/rdiskN bs=4m` and writes a log the session waits on. Terminal's TCC attribution allowed the raw write: 2,927,861,760 bytes in 184 s (15.9 MB/s). Keep the ISO outside `~/Downloads`. For a verify read, take exactly the ISO's length: the block size must divide it (`bs=8k count=<size/8192>`). A rounded-up count reads trailing old bytes, and the hash then looks like a failed write.

## OPS-392 — Main Mac off the home network: the MacBook Air test host has no route at all — not by IP, not by `air.local`, not through Tailscale

`측정 2026-10-10 · macOS 27 (main Mac, en0 172.31.185.121) · Tailscale 1.10x, exit node jupiter`

**증상:** `ssh 192.168.0.123` → `Operation timed out`, `ping` 100 % loss (even `192.168.0.1` fails). `ssh air.local` →
`Could not resolve hostname air.local`, and `dscacheutil -q host -a name air.local` / `dns-sd -G v4v6 air.local` return
nothing. Unlike OPS-347 there is no shared link, so mDNS's IPv6 link-local path is gone too.

Bringing Tailscale up (`tailscale up --accept-routes --exit-node-allow-lan-access --exit-node=100.102.194.77`, the
command `tailscale up` itself prints to keep the saved flags) does not help: `tailscale status` lists only
`m1max64` (this Mac), `jupiter` (the exit node, a Mac in Busan), an iPad and a phone — **the Air is not in the
tailnet**, and the exit node does not forward `192.168.0.0/24` (`route -n get 192.168.0.123` → `utun5`, still
timing out). Hopping through jupiter is no use either: it sits on a different LAN.

**해결:** first check `ipconfig getifaddr en0`. If it is neither `192.168.0.x` (use the IP) nor a subnet that
shares the Air's link (use `air.local`, OPS-347), the Air is unreachable from this Mac until it returns to the
home network or the Air joins the tailnet. Do not leave Tailscale changed: `tailscale down` restores the
stopped state. Run the suite locally only as a stated fallback and run it on the Air once it is reachable.

## OPS-393 — Dokploy `install.sh` pins Docker 28.5.0, which Docker's apt repo does not carry for Ubuntu 26.04 (resolute); install Docker 29.x first, then re-run

`측정 2026-10-11 · Dokploy v0.30.8 install.sh, Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (resolute) amd64, Docker CE repo`

**증상:** `curl -sSL https://dokploy.com/install.sh | sudo sh` on a fresh Ubuntu 26.04 box fails:
the bundled get.docker.com step adds the Docker apt repo for `resolute`, then dies with
`ERROR: '28.5.0' not found amongst apt-cache madison results`, leaving Docker uninstalled, so the
next step fails `docker: not found` / `Failed to initialize Docker Swarm`. The installer hardcodes
`DOCKER_VERSION="28.5.0"` (install.sh line 4) and calls `get.docker.com | sh -s -- --version
$DOCKER_VERSION`. The `resolute` component of the Docker repo only publishes docker-ce 29.x
(`apt-cache madison docker-ce` → 5:29.6.0 … 5:29.9.0-1~ubuntu.26.04~resolute); there is no 28.x
build for 26.04, so the pinned version can never resolve.

**해결:** Install Docker from the already-configured repo at whatever version it carries, then
re-run the Dokploy installer — it skips Docker when `command -v docker` succeeds (prints
`Docker already installed`, install.sh line 139) and goes straight to swarm init + stack deploy.

```bash
sudo apt-mark unhold docker-ce docker-ce-cli docker-ce-rootless-extras
sudo apt-get install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
sudo systemctl enable --now docker
sudo sh /tmp/dokploy-install.sh    # Docker 29.9.0 ran Dokploy v0.30.8 fine
```

## OPS-394 — Ubuntu 26.04 subiquity writes a netplan with no `dhcp4`, so a wired box comes up IPv6-only (RA works, no IPv4 lease)

`측정 2026-10-11 · Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS server install, systemd-networkd, Verizon CR1000A (OpenWrt) router`

**증상:** A freshly installed server reachable only over IPv6 link-local — `ip -4 addr` empty,
`ip route` empty — while `ip -6 route` shows a working RA default via the router and a global
SLAAC address. Docker Hub and other IPv4-only mirrors are then unreachable. The installer-written
`/etc/netplan/00-installer-config.yaml` has only `match`/`set-name` for the interface and no
`dhcp4`/`dhcp6` key, so networkd brings nothing up on v4 (IPv6 still works via kernel RA). Seen on
a wired install; the box had a live link the whole time.

**해결:** Add `dhcp4: true` (and `dhcp6: true`) under the interface and `sudo netplan apply`; the
IPv4 DHCP lease and default route appear within seconds. Reach the box first over IPv6 link-local:
`ssh user@'fe80::...%<local-iface>'` (the `%scope` is the *local* machine's interface). Find it
without IPv4 via `ndp -an`/`ping6 -c2 ff02::1%en0` on macOS.

## OPS-395 — Ubuntu subiquity LVM install caps the root LV at 100 GB regardless of disk size; the rest of the volume group sits unused

`측정 2026-10-11 · Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, subiquity guided LVM, 931 GB SATA SSD`

**증상:** `df -h /` shows ~98 GB on a 1 TB disk. `lsblk`: `sda` 931.5 G, `sda3` 928 G as
`LVM2_member`, but `ubuntu--vg-ubuntu--lv` only 100 G. `vgs` shows ~828 G `VFree` left unallocated.
This is subiquity's default for the guided-LVM layout — it provisions a 100 GB root LV and leaves
the remainder free in the VG, not an error. Easy to miss: a Docker host then fills up at 100 GB
while 800 GB sits idle.

**해결:** Extend the LV into the free extents and grow the filesystem online (ext4 grows while
mounted):

```bash
sudo lvextend -l +100%FREE /dev/ubuntu-vg/ubuntu-lv
sudo resize2fs /dev/ubuntu-vg/ubuntu-lv    # xfs: xfs_growfs /
```

## OPS-396 — Cloudflare Email Routing on a zone with no mail yet: the dashboard-session API refused the writes, the UI did it in four clicks, and direct SMTP is only good for an RCPT check

`측정 2026-10-11 · Cloudflare dashboard (ko UI) · zone already on Cloudflare Registrar, no MX · Chrome for Testing (ms-playwright chromium-1243) on the main Mac with a copy of ~/.gstack/chromium-profile`

**증상:**
- From a signed-in dashboard page, `fetch('/api/v4/zones/<id>/email/routing/enable', {method:'POST', headers:{'x-cross-site-security':'dash'}})` and `POST …/email/routing/rules` both answered **403** (HTML, not JSON), unlike OPS-339. GETs on the same paths answered 200. `GET …/email/routing/dns` lists the five required records even before they exist.
- The wrangler OAuth token has the `email_routing:write` scope, but an expired token was not refreshed in a non-interactive shell ("could not be refreshed, and the environment is non-interactive"), so wrangler was no way round it.
- Right after the rule was saved (`enabled: true, status: ready, synced: false`), `RCPT TO:<contact@…>` on `route1.mx.cloudflare.net:25` still answered `550 5.1.1 Address does not exist`; about 1 minute later it answered `250`, while unknown addresses kept getting 550.
- A test message sent straight to the MX from a home IP with an `@<zone>` sender was refused: `550 5.7.26 Cannot forward emails that are not authenticated`. The activity log shows it as 「인증되지 않음」.

**해결:**
- Do it in the UI: 설정 tab → **누락된 레코드 추가** (MX ×3, DKIM, SPF; OPS-101), then 라우팅 규칙 → 라우팅 규칙 생성. The pickers are custom: click `button[aria-label="도메인 선택"]`, `button[aria-label="동작"]`, `button[aria-label="Show options"]` (destination) and pick `[role=option]` by text; `getByRole('button', {name})` did not find them inside the dialog. A destination verified for another zone is offered at once (account-wide, OPS-101).
- Check reception without sending mail: SMTP `MAIL FROM` + `RCPT TO` + `RSET` against the route MX; 250 for the routed address and 550 for a made-up one means the rule is live.
- End-to-end: send from Gmail (`mail.google.com/mail/u/0/?view=cm&fs=1&to=…&su=…&body=…`, then click 「보내기」). Even from the destination account itself the activity log shows 「전달됨」 within about a minute (the copy will not show in that inbox, OPS-097).
- With the Air unreachable, a Cloudflare session on the main Mac: copy `~/.gstack/chromium-profile` (Google signed in) to a temp dir and open it headed with Chrome for Testing from `~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium-*`, `--remote-debugging-port` so later scripts can `connectOverCDP`. The Cloudflare login page offered the last-used Google account; one click signed in. Delete the copy afterwards.

## OPS-397 — On a fresh Ubuntu server, `get.docker.com` fails on the dpkg lock held by unattended-upgrades and exits without installing Docker; a script that continues then fails later with `docker: not found`

`측정 2026-10-11 · Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS server, get.docker.com commit 2b32480, Dokploy v0.30.8 install.sh`

**증상:** The first minutes after a new server gets internet (here right after fixing IPv4, OPS-394),
`unattended-upgrades` runs and holds `/var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend`. `sh get-docker.sh` prints
`E: Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend. It is held by process NNNN (unattended-upgr)`
during its `apt-get install ca-certificates curl` step and stops. Docker is not installed, but a
wrapper script without `set -e` keeps going: `systemctl enable --now docker` →
`Unit docker.service does not exist`, and Dokploy's installer → `docker: not found` /
`Error: Failed to initialize Docker Swarm`. The Docker apt repo is already configured at that point.

**해결:** Make apt wait for the lock instead of failing, then run the Dokploy installer again:

```bash
sudo apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=900 install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
```

Or wait first: `while fuser /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 5; done`.

## OPS-398 — Gmail asks for a passkey re-auth before it creates any filter, through the UI or through "필터 가져오기"; the session cannot pass it alone, but the owner can finish it in the automation window

`측정 2026-10-11 · Gmail web (ko UI) · Chrome for Testing (ms-playwright chromium-1243) with a copy of ~/.gstack/chromium-profile · account protected by a passkey`

**증상:** the account was signed in and Gmail worked (compose, send, search, new label). Creating a filter stopped at a dialog 「계속하려면 본인 인증이 필요합니다」 both from 「필터 가져오기」 (XML, OPS-102) and from 검색 옵션 → 필터 만들기. 「계속」 opens a popup at `accounts.google.com/v3/signin/challenge/pk` that says 「패스키를 사용하여 로그인을 완료합니다」; 「인증 방법 더보기」 did not offer anything else in that window. Creating a label did not ask for re-auth. OPS-102 (2026-09-20) did not meet this step.

Also measured in the same run: in the 검색 옵션 panel the text inputs' DOM order does not follow the visible rows, so filling an input picked by id put `@mnori.com` into 제목 (`subject:(@mnori.com)`). Typing `to:(@domain)` in the search box first, then opening 검색 옵션, fills 받는사람 correctly. The action checkboxes are hidden inputs at x = -9743; click their `label[for=<id>]`.

**해결:** a session cannot pass the passkey step alone. Set the filter up fully (label, `to:(@domain)` search, actions ticked), click 「필터 만들기」 and 「계속」, bring the popup to the front, and tell the owner to authenticate in that window. The owner's passkey worked in the Chrome for Testing window with the copied profile; the popup closed by itself and the filter appeared in 설정 → 필터 at once (measured: poll every 10 s for the popup to close, then read the filter list). Close the browser and delete the profile copy afterwards.

## OPS-399 — Brave on macOS: System Events `click at` and `AXPress` on a web-page button do nothing; setting `AXFocused` and sending Return presses it

`측정 2026-10-11 · Brave Browser (Chromium) on macOS 27, System Events with Accessibility granted, dash.cloudflare.com login page`

**증상:** With JavaScript from Apple Events off (and the menu toggle not taking, OPS-366 note), a web button found in
Brave's accessibility tree — e.g. `button "chowooick@gmail.com 계정으로 Google 사용하여 계속"` — returns its element path
from `tell application "System Events" to click at {x, y}` and from `perform action "AXPress"`, without an error, but the
page does not react: no navigation, no popup, the URL stays the same.

**해결:** focus the element and type Return:

```applescript
tell application "Brave Browser" to activate
tell application "System Events" to tell process "Brave Browser"
  set b to button "<name>" of … -- path as returned by `click at`
  set value of attribute "AXFocused" of b to true
  delay 0.3
  keystroke return
end tell
```

For targets that are not focusable (table rows, divs with click handlers) post a real `CGEvent` mouse-down/up from a
small Swift binary at the point mapped from a `screencapture` (Retina: screenshot pixels ÷ 2 = points).

## OPS-400 — Renaming Dokploy's own panel domain without the UI: `webServerSettings.host` in Postgres plus the root-owned `dokploy.yml`, edited from inside the dokploy container
`측정 2026-10-12 · Dokploy v0.30.8 (misa) · Traefik file provider · Let's Encrypt HTTP-01`

**증상:** `sed -i` on `/etc/dokploy/traefik/dynamic/dokploy.yml` as a docker-group user fails with `sed: couldn't open temporary file /etc/dokploy/traefik/dynamic/sedXXXX: Permission denied` — the directory and file are `root:root 644`, and without sudo there is no host-side way to write them.

The panel domain lives in two places: the `host` column of the single row in `"webServerSettings"` (Postgres, `docker exec <dokploy-postgres> psql -U dokploy -d dokploy`), and the two router rules in `dokploy.yml`. The DB value is what Dokploy uses when it regenerates `dokploy.yml` (saving the domain in Settings → Web Server, or an update), so changing only the file is undone later.

**해결:** run the edit inside the dokploy container, which mounts `/etc/dokploy` as root: `docker exec $(docker ps -qf name=dokploy.1) sed -i 's/rule: Host(`old`)/rule: Host(`new`) || Host(`old`)/' /etc/dokploy/traefik/dynamic/dokploy.yml`, and `update "webServerSettings" set host='new'`. Traefik's file watcher picks it up and HTTP-01 issued one certificate with both names as SANs in under 30 s. Keeping `|| Host(old)` matters: GitLab push hooks (`https://<old>/api/deploy/<token>`) and deploy scripts in other repos still call the old name. better-auth sign-in from the new origin returned the normal `401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD`, not an origin error. A later regeneration from the DB will drop the old alias.

## OPS-401 — A single-node Docker Swarm (Dokploy) pins the LAN IP it was initialised on; move it to a netplan dummy address with `--force-new-cluster`, and expect the old address to stay in the raft member record

`측정 2026-10-12 · Docker 29.9.0, Dokploy v0.30.8, Ubuntu 26.04.1, netplan 1.2`

**증상:** Dokploy's installer runs `docker swarm init --advertise-addr <LAN IP>`. After the box got a different IP and rebooted, the swarm still elected itself leader and Dokploy came back (~2 min), but dockerd logged `agent: session failed … dial tcp 192.168.1.159:2377: connect: no route to host` before falling back to the local manager. Swarm ports 2377/7946 also listen on `0.0.0.0`, i.e. on whatever LAN the box is plugged into.

To make the swarm independent of the network, give it an address that never changes — a dummy interface in netplan — and re-anchor the existing cluster on it. `--force-new-cluster` keeps services, secrets and overlay networks:

```yaml
  dummy-devices:
    swarm0:
      addresses: [198.18.213.1/32]   # 198.18.0.0/15: benchmarking range, never a home LAN
      optional: true                 # see OPS-402
```
```bash
docker swarm init --force-new-cluster --advertise-addr 198.18.213.1 --listen-addr 198.18.213.1:2377
```

Afterwards `docker info` shows `NodeAddr 198.18.213.1` and 2377/7946 listen only on that address. But `docker node inspect self --format '{{.ManagerStatus.Addr}}'` still says the old `192.168.1.159:2377`: it lives in the encrypted raft WAL, is copied back into `/var/lib/docker/swarm/state.json`, and was not updated by the re-init or by two reboots. The agent still dials it once per start (8 failed dials in one boot) and then uses the local manager; tasks were created 3 s after dockerd started, so it costs nothing measurable. Only `docker swarm leave --force` + a fresh init clears it, and that drops Dokploy's services and secrets.

**해결:** Use the dummy address + `--force-new-cluster`; ignore the stale `ManagerStatus.Addr`. On a fresh install, create the dummy interface first and pass `--advertise-addr` to the installer's swarm init instead.

## OPS-402 — A netplan `dummy-devices` entry without `optional: true` makes every boot wait the full 120 s `systemd-networkd-wait-online` timeout

`측정 2026-10-12 · netplan 1.2, systemd-networkd, Ubuntu 26.04.1`

**증상:** After adding a dummy interface (OPS-401), boot became 2 minutes slower. Timeline from the journal: DHCPv4 lease at 24 s, but `docker.service` and `cloudflared.service` (both `After=network-online.target`) started at 142–151 s. A dummy link never gets carrier, so `systemd-networkd-wait-online` waits for it until its 120 s timeout. Nothing logs an error; the box just comes up late.

**해결:** Add `optional: true` to the dummy device. Measured on the next boot: DHCP 21 s, cloudflared connected 27 s, Docker 41 s, and the Dokploy site through its Cloudflare Tunnel answered 200 at 125 s after reboot (227 s before).

## OPS-403 — Laptop as a lid-closed Linux server: the internal panel stays lit at full brightness, RAPL `psys` is not a wall-power meter, and a Turing dGPU on nouveau already reaches D3cold

`측정 2026-10-12 · ASUS ROG Strix G712LU (i7-10750H, GTX 1660 Ti Mobile), Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-30, nouveau + i915`

**증상:** With `HandleLidSwitch=ignore` (so the server does not suspend), closing the lid does not turn the screen off.
`/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness` was 24000/24000, `card2-eDP-1/dpms` was `On`, and
`/sys/module/kernel/parameters/consoleblank` was `0` (Ubuntu server default). The panel burns power and heats the lid
around the clock. Two things looked like more waste but were not:
- `intel-rapl:1` (name `psys`) read 0.36–0.48 W while `intel-rapl:0` (package) read 2.2–2.3 W. On this board psys is
  not wired as platform power, so it cannot stand in for a wall meter.
- The dGPU showed `runtime_status=active` right after `lspci`, but that read woke it. `power_state` was `D3cold`, with
  `runtime_suspended_time` 8.7 h against 25 s active. Its USB-C/UCSI functions (01:00.2/.3) being `active` did not stop
  D3cold, so removing them is not needed.

**해결:** turn the panel off at boot with a oneshot unit that runs after `systemd-backlight` (that unit restores the
saved brightness), and add the kernel blank timeout:

```bash
for b in /sys/class/backlight/*/brightness; do echo 0 > "$b"; done
setterm --term linux --blank 1 --powerdown 1 --powersave powerdown </dev/tty1 >/dev/tty1
# /etc/default/grub: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="... consoleblank=60"; update-grub
```

Afterwards `eDP-1/dpms` reads `Off`, and it survives a reboot. On ASUS laptops also cap the battery for 24/7 AC use with
`echo 60 > /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/charge_control_end_threshold`, set from the same unit so it holds after every boot.

## OPS-404 — Swapping the names of two servers behind locally managed Cloudflare Tunnels: swap the tunnel credentials files, not DNS; restart avahi after `hostnamectl`

`측정 2026-10-12 · cloudflared (locally managed, /etc/cloudflared/config.yml), Ubuntu 26.04.1, avahi-daemon, Docker 29.9.0 swarm`

**증상:** Two home servers each ran their own locally managed tunnel (`nj1` → `nj1.mnori.com`, `nj2` → `nj2.mnori.com`) and the owner wanted the names swapped. Re-pointing the DNS CNAMEs would leave tunnel `nj1` running on the box now called nj2. After `hostnamectl set-hostname`, the new `<name>.local` did not resolve from a Mac on the LAN (`Could not resolve hostname nj2.local`), and `docker node ls` kept the old node name.

A locally managed tunnel is just its credentials JSON (`/etc/cloudflared/<tunnel-id>.json`, 175 bytes) plus `config.yml`. Copy each box's JSON to the other (base64 over ssh), rewrite `config.yml` with the other tunnel id and hostname, delete the old JSON, and restart cloudflared. The public hostnames then follow the names with no DNS or API call; each site was back at 200 within 6 s of the restart (while one box had no connector, its hostname returned 530).

**해결:** Swap the credentials and config as above. Then restart `avahi-daemon` so mDNS announces the new name, and restart `docker` (or reboot) so the swarm node takes the new hostname. On a Dokploy single-node install the Dokploy database holds no hostname (a `pg_dump --data-only` had 0 matches for the domain), so nothing in Dokploy needs changing. After the swap, drop the old `*.local` entries from the client's `known_hosts` (`ssh-keygen -R nj1.local`), because each name now belongs to a different host key.

## OPS-405 — Closing Dokploy's :3000 to the LAN while keeping it on a Cloudflare Tunnel needs two firewall paths: DOCKER-USER for IPv4, INPUT for IPv6

`측정 2026-10-12 · Dokploy v0.30.8, Docker 29.9.0 (iptables backend, userland proxy on), Ubuntu 26.04.1, cloudflared 2026.10`

**증상:** Dokploy publishes its panel as a swarm service port in **host** mode (`{"PublishedPort":3000,"PublishMode":"host"}`), so it listens on `0.0.0.0:3000` and `[::]:3000` on every interface. A server moved to another network serves the plain-HTTP login page to that whole LAN, and on IPv6 to its global address too. Swarm cannot bind a published port to one IP, and ufw rules do not apply to Docker's DNAT.

The two families arrive differently. IPv4 from the LAN is DNATed in `nat/DOCKER` (`! -i docker_gwbridge --dport 3000 -j DNAT --to 172.18.0.x:3000`) and crosses `FORWARD`, where `DOCKER-USER` sees it. IPv6 goes to `docker-proxy` on `[::]:3000` through `INPUT`. cloudflared's `http://localhost:3000` arrives on `lo`, so rules scoped to `en+`/`wl+` leave the tunnel alone.

**해결:** A oneshot unit with `After=docker.service`, `PartOf=docker.service` and `WantedBy=docker.service` that adds the rules idempotently (`iptables -C … || iptables -I …`), so they come back after every Docker restart and reboot:

```sh
for ifc in en+ wl+; do
  iptables  -I DOCKER-USER -i "$ifc" -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 3000 -j DROP
  iptables  -I INPUT       -i "$ifc" -p tcp --dport 3000 -j DROP
  ip6tables -I INPUT       -i "$ifc" -p tcp --dport 3000 -j DROP
done
```

Match `--ctorigdstport` in `DOCKER-USER`, because after DNAT the packet's `--dport` is the container port. Here the two are the same, but they differ for any `-p 8080:3000` mapping. Measured from another host on the LAN, IPv4 and IPv6 `:3000` both time out, and the tunnel hostname still returns 200.

For remote ssh through the same tunnel, add an ingress rule `hostname: <name>-ssh.<zone>` → `service: ssh://localhost:22` and `cloudflared tunnel route dns <id> <name>-ssh.<zone>`. On the client, set `ProxyCommand cloudflared access ssh --hostname %h`. Without a Cloudflare Access policy that hostname is open to anyone who has cloudflared, so set `PasswordAuthentication no` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-*.conf`. sshd keeps the first value it reads, and that file is read before Ubuntu's `50-cloud-init.conf` (`PasswordAuthentication yes`); confirm with `sshd -T`.

## OPS-406 — An old laptop HDD used as a server can be past its rated head-load count; `apm = 254` in `/etc/hdparm.conf` did not apply on Ubuntu 26.04, so set it from a systemd unit

`측정 2026-10-12 · Ubuntu 26.04.1, hdparm package, HGST HTS541010A9E680 (1 TB 5400 rpm laptop drive)`

**증상:** SMART on a repurposed 2016 laptop server read `Load_Cycle_Count` 661,055 (normalised 034) after 9,916 power-on hours, beyond the ~600k that laptop drives are rated for. SMART overall-health still said PASSED, with 0 pending or reallocated sectors, so nothing else warned. `hdparm -B` showed APM level 128, at which the drive unloads its heads when idle. Adding `/dev/disk/by-id/<disk> { apm = 254 }` to `/etc/hdparm.conf` changed nothing. Neither `udevadm trigger --action=add /dev/sda` nor running `/usr/lib/udev/hdparm` by hand applied it, and `hdparm -B` still read 128. The udev helper strips `-B` and leaves APM to `/usr/lib/pm-utils/power.d/95hdparm-apm`.

**해결:** Check `Load_Cycle_Count` and `hdparm -B` on any laptop HDD that becomes a server. To stop further head parking, use a oneshot unit, `WantedBy=multi-user.target`, with `ExecStart=/usr/sbin/hdparm -B 254 /dev/disk/by-id/<disk>`. Use the by-id path so the unit survives `sdX` renaming. It read 254 after a reboot.

## OPS-407 — A portable Docker Swarm host breaks on a LAN inside 172.18.0.0/16: the more specific LAN route hides `docker_gwbridge`, and host-mode published ports (Dokploy :3000) stop answering

`측정 2026-10-12 · Docker 29.9.0 swarm (Dokploy v0.30.8), Ubuntu 26.04.1, cloudflared tunnel → http://localhost:3000, userland proxy on`

**증상:** We checked a home server meant to work on any router by adding a second address to its NIC at runtime
(`ip addr add <addr>/24 dev eno2`), the same thing a router on that subnet would do, while probing the public tunnel
URL every 3 s:

| LAN added | `curl 127.0.0.1:3000` | tunnel URL |
|---|---|---|
| none (192.168.1.0/24), or the IP changed .160 → .201 | 200 | 200 throughout |
| 10.0.0.0/24 (Xfinity default; overlaps swarm `ingress` 10.0.0.0/24) | 200 | 200 |
| 172.17.0.0/24 (overlaps `docker0`, which is linkdown) | 200 | 200 |
| **172.18.0.0/24** (overlaps `docker_gwbridge` 172.18.0.0/16) | **000** | **502** for the whole 30 s |

Docker DNATs host-mode published ports to the container's `docker_gwbridge` address (172.18.0.x). A LAN `/24` route
inside 172.18.0.0/16 is more specific than the bridge's `/16`, so the host sends that traffic out of the NIC instead.
Overlay networks (`ingress`, `dokploy-network` 10.0.1.0/24) live in their own namespaces and did not clash. The tunnel
recovered as soon as the address was removed.

**해결:** if the box may land on such a LAN, move `docker_gwbridge` (and `docker0` via `"bip"` / `"default-address-pools"`
in daemon.json) to a range no router uses, e.g. 198.19.0.0/16 (benchmarking range). `docker_gwbridge` can only be
recreated with no swarm containers attached, so this takes the services down briefly. Otherwise accept the risk:
172.18.x home LANs are rare.

## OPS-408 — Moving Docker Swarm's `docker_gwbridge` and `docker0` off 172.17/172.18 on a live Dokploy host: about 40 s of downtime, nothing lost

`측정 2026-10-12 · Docker 29.9.0 swarm (Dokploy v0.30.8: services dokploy, dokploy-postgres + container dokploy-traefik), Ubuntu 26.04.1`

**증상:** A LAN inside `docker_gwbridge`'s 172.18.0.0/16 breaks host-mode published ports (OPS-407). Docker's default pools also hand out 172.17–31/16 and 192.168.x/20 to new bridge networks, such as Dokploy compose apps, which can collide with a home LAN. `docker_gwbridge` cannot be edited in place. It can be removed only with no swarm container attached, and `bip` only changes on a daemon restart.

**해결:** Run this as one detached script (`systemd-run`), because it restarts Docker:

```bash
cat > /etc/docker/daemon.json <<'J'
{ "bip": "198.18.0.1/24", "default-address-pools": [{ "base": "198.19.0.0/16", "size": 24 }] }
J
docker service scale -d dokploy=0 dokploy-postgres=0
docker stop dokploy-traefik            # standalone container on the attachable overlay also holds a gwbridge endpoint
for c in $(docker network inspect docker_gwbridge -f '{{range $k,$v := .Containers}}{{$v.Name}} {{end}}'); do
  docker network disconnect --force docker_gwbridge "$c"   # includes gateway_ingress-sbox
done
docker network rm docker_gwbridge
docker network create --subnet 198.18.1.0/24 --gateway 198.18.1.1 \
  -o com.docker.network.bridge.name=docker_gwbridge \
  -o com.docker.network.bridge.enable_icc=false \
  -o com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade=true docker_gwbridge
systemctl restart docker
docker service scale -d dokploy=1 dokploy-postgres=1 && docker start dokploy-traefik
```

The script ran in 32 s, and the panel answered 200 through its tunnel at 38 s. Services, database and secrets were intact, and the swarm overlays (`ingress` 10.0.0.0/24, `dokploy-network` 10.0.1.0/24) were untouched; OPS-407 showed they do not clash. A re-test then held 172.18.0.50/24, 172.17.0.50/24 and 198.51.100.50/24 on the NIC at once. During it, `127.0.0.1:3000` and the tunnel URL stayed 200 throughout, and `docker network create` handed out 198.19.0.0/24. 198.18.0.0/15 is the benchmarking range (RFC 2544), so no consumer router uses it. Do this before apps exist, because every app's bridge network would otherwise also need re-creating.

## OPS-409 — macOS 27 ignores the 80 % Charge Limit and charges to 100 % once 21 days pass without a full charge; location has nothing to do with it

`측정 2026-10-12 · macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), MacBookPro18,2, battery 436 cycles / 83 % health, Apple 140 W adapter`

**증상:** With Battery → Charge Limit set to 80 % (stored as a `manualChargeLimit` policy, `soclimit 80`, owner `PowerUIAgent`, in `/Library/Preferences/com.apple.powerd.charging.plist`), the Mac suddenly charges to 100 % on AC. It held 80 % for three weeks, so it looks tied to a place or a trip. No third-party tool (AlDente, `batt`, `bclm`) is installed.

`powerd` runs a battery-gauge calibration check every few hours. Once the last full charge is more than 21 days old, it overrides the limit:

```
[com.apple.powerd:batterygauging] Last full charge date was 20.6 days ago too recent
[com.apple.powerd:batterygauging] Last full charge date was 21.3 days ago, try and charge to full
[com.apple.powerd:batterygauging] Charge To Full System Level Request:1
[com.apple.powerd:charging] SOC limit disabled
[com.apple.powerd:charging] SOC limit policy suspend due to mitigation active:1
```

The 21-day count started on the day the limit was turned on, because that was the last full charge. The override is a timer, not a location rule: `PowerUIAgent` reads location for Optimized Charging, but the log line that disables the limit comes from `batterygauging`. The override stays active until the battery reports `FullyCharged = Yes`. Reaching 100 % in the menu bar and unplugging during "finishing charge" (`ioreg -rn AppleSmartBattery` still shows `FullyCharged = No`) does not reset the timer; the next check logs `21.8 days ago, try and charge to full` again. `pmset -g batt` and `/var/log/powermanagement/*.asl` show none of this. Read it with `/usr/bin/log`: in zsh, `log` is a shell builtin, so a bare `log show …` prints `too many arguments` or nothing.

```bash
/usr/bin/log show --last 8d --style compact \
  --predicate 'process == "powerd" AND eventMessage CONTAINS "Last full charge date"'
```

**해결:** This is designed behaviour, and no setting turns it off. Leave the Mac on AC until `ioreg` shows `FullyCharged = Yes`. The limit then comes back by itself for the next 21 days. To keep the forced 100 % from coming as a surprise, do a full charge on purpose every two to three weeks, for example the night before travelling.

## OPS-410 — Moving a whole Dokploy install to another host: restore its Postgres dump, then set `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, re-save application domains, and copy images and volumes yourself

`측정 2026-10-12 · Dokploy v0.30.8 → v0.30.8, Docker 29.9 swarm, 7 applications + 21 raw compose stacks + 1 Postgres service`

**증상:** After `pg_restore` of the old host's `dokploy` database into a fresh install, every service's env would not decrypt (`enc:v1:` values), application domains returned Traefik's 19-byte `404 page not found`, and compose stacks failed on `image: game-web:${RELEASE}` that existed only on the old host. Login asked for TOTP, because the old admin had 2FA.

Env values are encrypted with `sha256(ENCRYPTION_KEY ?? BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)`. An install without `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` uses the literal default `better-auth-secret-123456789`; a newer install has `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET_FILE`, so the keys differ. Dokploy writes an application's Traefik file (`/etc/dokploy/traefik/dynamic/<app>.yml`) only when a domain is saved, not on deploy; compose domains become labels at deploy, so those work.

**해결:** On the target: `docker service scale dokploy=0`, `drop database dokploy with (force)`, `pg_restore --no-owner`, copy the target admin's `account.password` hash back in, `delete from session`, then `docker service update --env-add ENCRYPTION_KEY=<old key or the default literal> dokploy` (it decrypts with the new key and the target's own secret) and scale to 1. The old host's API keys keep working, so scripts and GitLab hooks (`/api/deploy/<refreshToken>`) need only DNS. Call `domain.update` once per application domain to write the Traefik files. Move locally built images with one `docker save a b c … | zstd` (shared layers are sent once; 21 images were 2.17 GB, `docker load` 398 s over a 7 MB/s relay) and named volumes with `docker run --rm -v VOL:/v:ro … tar -cf - -C /v .` into a pre-created volume of the same name; compose then adopts it with only a warning. Per stateful stack: `compose.stop` on the old host, copy volumes, `compose.deploy` on the new one, check `curl -H 'Host: <domain>' http://<new-lan-ip>/`, then switch DNS. 18 stacks took 30-140 s of downtime each. Do not poll `composeStatus` for completion, it still reads `done` from the restored row; poll `deployment.allByCompose` for a deployment newer than your call.

Behind a tunnel that sends hostnames to `http://localhost:80`, set `forwardedHeaders.insecure: true` on Traefik's `web` entrypoint. cloudflared passes Cloudflare's `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, and Dokploy's `redirect-to-https` (`redirectScheme`) then does nothing. Measured through the tunnel: a `web` router with that middleware answered 200, not 301. Without that setting the same request loops. So a deploy script that flips a domain back to `https: true` does not break the site.

## OPS-411 — Cloudflare: creating `x.zone` turns off the `*.zone` wildcard for `a.x.zone`; two-level names go NXDOMAIN

`측정 2026-10-12 · Cloudflare DNS, mnori.com with an unproxied `*.mnori.com` A record`

**증상:** `admin.partners.mnori.com` and `api.farm.mnori.com` had always resolved through `*.mnori.com`. Minutes after explicit CNAMEs were created for `partners.mnori.com` and `farm.mnori.com`, both returned NXDOMAIN (`dig` empty, curl `000`).

This is RFC 4592: once `partners.mnori.com` exists, it is the closest encloser of `admin.partners.mnori.com`, and only a `*.partners.mnori.com` record could match. Resolvers then cache the NXDOMAIN, so the local machine kept failing after the fix while `dig @1.1.1.1` already answered.

**해결:** Before giving any name its own record, list deeper names that used the wildcard and create explicit records for them in the same step. A proxied two-level name also has no Universal SSL certificate, so keep such names DNS-only on a host with its own certificate (here misa's Traefik forwards them to the new host with `passHostHeader: false`).

## OPS-412 — Cloudflare Browser Integrity Check answers Python `urllib` with `403` / `error code: 1010`; deploy scripts on the origin host can bypass Cloudflare with `/etc/hosts` and a local Let's Encrypt certificate

`측정 2026-10-12 · Cloudflare proxied hostnames on mnori.com, Python 3 urllib, curl 8`

**증상:** A Dokploy API script that worked against a DNS-only host failed after the host went behind a Cloudflare Tunnel: `HTTP Error 403: Forbidden`, body `error code: 1010`. With curl, only the user agent `Python-urllib/3.12` was blocked; `node`, `undici`, `python-requests/2.32`, `Go-http-client/1.1` and an empty agent got 200. The tunnel's own cert.pem token cannot change zone settings (`/settings/browser_check` → 403 `Unauthorized`).

**해결:** For scripts that run on the server itself: `127.0.0.1 dokploy.<zone>` in `/etc/hosts`, plus a Traefik router for that host on `websecure` with `certResolver: letsencrypt`. HTTP-01 succeeds through the tunnel when the tunnel sends the hostname to `http://localhost:80` and the `web` router has no redirect-to-https. Python then reaches Dokploy locally with a valid certificate. From elsewhere, send a browser-like `User-Agent` or use a WAF skip rule in the dashboard.

## OPS-413 — A laptop server with its lid closed and `HandleLidSwitch=ignore` keeps its panel lit at full backlight; Ubuntu Server also ships `consoleblank=0` and no `rfkill`

`측정 2026-10-12 · Ubuntu 26.04.1 server, kernel 7.0, HP Pavilion (i7-6500U, Realtek RTL810xE r8169), powertop 2.15`

**증상:** A laptop server was set to ignore the lid switch so it keeps running when closed. Months later, with the lid shut, `/sys/class/backlight/intel_backlight/brightness` read 937/937 (100 %), `/sys/class/drm/card1-eDP-1/dpms` read `On`, and `/sys/module/kernel/parameters/consoleblank` read `0`. A closed lid does not switch the panel off. Nothing shows it, and the backlight is often the largest idle load on such a box. RAPL (`intel-rapl:0` package, core, uncore, dram) does not include the panel, so a RAPL before/after reading cannot see this saving. `rfkill` is not installed on Ubuntu Server, so a script line `rfkill block wlan bluetooth || true` fails silently.

**해결:** Use a oneshot unit (`After=multi-user.target`, `ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 20` so it runs after systemd-backlight restores its saved level). It sets every `/sys/class/backlight/*/brightness` to 0, then runs `setterm --term linux --blank 1 --powerdown 1 --powersave powerdown </dev/tty1 >/dev/tty1` and `setterm --blank force`, which together turn eDP dpms `Off`. Add `consoleblank=60` to `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT`, install `rfkill` for `rfkill block wlan bluetooth`, and turn off unused USB devices with `echo 0 > /sys/bus/usb/devices/<dev>/authorized` matched by idVendor:idProduct. Finish with `powertop --auto-tune`. Measured over 60 s at idle, package power fell 1.30 → 1.11 W and DRAM 1.21 → 0.97 W; the panel saving is extra and was not metered. powertop also put the Realtek NIC's PCI runtime PM on `auto`. Over the next 30 minutes there were 0 link drops (the one `Link is Down` was the driver's first link-up at boot, before the unit ran), and 60 of 60 tunnel probes returned 200. Every setting held after a reboot.

## OPS-414 — Typing into the owner's desktop Brave with CGEvent: a key event from the `.hidSystemState` source inherits a held Command and turns text into shortcuts

`측정 2026-10-12 · macOS 27, Brave (Chromium 154), Swift CGEvent, dash.cloudflare.com`

**증상:** After one `Cmd+A` (`CGEvent` with `.maskCommand`), typing a token name character by character with `keyboardSetUnicodeString` opened a private window, two new windows and replaced a tab's URL: every letter arrived as Cmd+letter (`n` new window, `Shift+Cmd+N` private, `t` new tab, `o` open file …).

Events built from `CGEventSource(stateID: .hidSystemState)` take their modifier flags from the combined system state, which still had Command down from the synthetic Cmd+A.

**해결:** Build key events from `CGEventSource(stateID: .privateState)` and set `flags = []` on every text event (only the shortcut events get `.maskCommand`). Work in a dedicated window (`open -na "Brave Browser" --args --new-window <url>`, then pick it by `id` in AppleScript, `set index of w to 1`) and list all windows/tabs before and after, so stray windows can be closed and a replaced tab restored. Cookie import into a headless browser is no alternative on this Mac: `cookie-import-browser brave` → `authorization denied` (TCC), and Brave's profile folder is `Operation not permitted` even outside the sandbox. To take a secret shown once (a new Cloudflare API token), click the page's copy button and run `pbpaste > file; printf '' | pbcopy`, so it never goes through a screenshot reader or the terminal.

## OPS-415 — Putting a GoDaddy- or hosting.kr-hosted domain behind a Cloudflare Tunnel: Cloudflare for SaaS on a free zone needs a billing checkout, so move the nameservers; GoDaddy and hosting.kr NS changes went live in minutes

`측정 2026-10-12 · Cloudflare free plan, GoDaddy (dcc.godaddy.com, ko UI), hosting.kr (Megazone, ko UI), cloudflared locally managed tunnel`

**증상:** A tunnel hostname must be a proxied record in a Cloudflare zone of the same account. For a name whose DNS lives at GoDaddy, the API answers `custom_hostnames` with `1404 No quota has been allocated` and `fallback_origin` with `1456 … available with SSL for SaaS`. The dashboard button 「Cloudflare for SaaS 사용」 leads to a checkout ($0/월, usage-based, card on file, terms checkbox), which is a billing agreement and not a setting.

**해결:** Create the zone by API (`POST /zones` with `account.id`, `jump_start: false`), import the registrar's records as a BIND file (`POST /zones/<id>/dns_records/import`, multipart `file` + `proxied=false`), add the tunnel CNAMEs (proxied), add the hostnames to the tunnel's `config.yml` ingress, then change the NS at the registrar. A user API token with Zone:Zone/DNS/SSL/Zone Settings Edit on "모든 영역" can create zones. GoDaddy: 도메인 → DNS → 네임서버 → 네임서버 변경 → 「내 고유 네임서버」, and a second dialog 「계속」. hosting.kr: 네임서버/DNS → pencil → delete rows and type the new ones → type `OK` → it warns that its own DNS record service is cancelled. The registry showed the new NS at once; `PUT /zones/<id>/activation_check` made the zones `active` within 2 minutes, and the edge certificate for the new zone took another ~2 minutes (curl `000` until then). For a stateful app, keep the old origin forwarding to the new one (Traefik file route, `passHostHeader: false`, to a hostname of the new server) while resolvers still hold the old delegation (.com NS TTL is 2 days).

## OPS-416 — Turning off a Dokploy admin's 2FA from the shell: delete the `two_factor` row and clear `user.two_factor_enabled`

`측정 2026-10-12 · Dokploy v0.30.8 (better-auth), postgres:16 service dokploy-postgres`

**증상:** The panel login asks for a TOTP code and the code is not accepted (or the authenticator is lost), so the 2FA screen cannot be passed and the UI path to disable 2FA is out of reach. The columns are snake_case: `select "twoFactorEnabled" from "user"` fails with `column "twoFactorEnabled" does not exist`.

2FA state lives in two places: table `two_factor` (`user_id`, `secret`, `backup_codes`, `verified`, `failed_verification_count`, `locked_until`) and column `user.two_factor_enabled`. Clearing both is enough; no Dokploy restart is needed.

**해결:**
```
P=$(sudo docker ps -qf name=dokploy-postgres)
sudo docker exec $P pg_dump -U dokploy -d dokploy -t two_factor -t '"user"' > user-2fa.sql   # keep a copy first
sudo docker exec $P psql -U dokploy -d dokploy -c \
  'begin; delete from two_factor where user_id=(select id from "user" where email=$$<email>$$);
   update "user" set two_factor_enabled=false where email=$$<email>$$; commit;'
```
Check without a browser: `POST https://<panel>/api/auth/sign-in/email` with `{"email","password"}` and an `origin` header returns `200` with a `token` and no `twoFactorRedirect`.

## OPS-417 — Installing the `cloudflared` .deb over a hand-copied binary restarts the running tunnel (~30 s outage) and turns `/usr/local/bin/cloudflared` into a symlink
