## OPS-526 — glab OAuth refresh can time out on DNS while Node reaches the same GitLab endpoint

`측정 2026-10-19 · glab 1.82.0 · Node 26.8.2 · MacBook Air M1 · gitlab.com OAuth`

**증상:** an existing OAuth access token returned HTTP 401 after expiry. A copied glab 1.82.0 executable on Air
failed its refresh with `lookup gitlab.com: i/o timeout`; Node fetch on that same Air reached GitLab. The cause
of the executable-specific DNS failure was not established; this does not prove a firewall rule.

**해결:** inspect the matching official glab release source for its OAuth client ID and refresh contract. From
Node on Air, POST the existing refresh token with `grant_type=refresh_token` and that public `client_id` to
`https://gitlab.com/oauth/token`. Verify the renewed access token with an authenticated API read before use.
Preserve the rotated refresh token and expiry too. When using an isolated copy of the CLI config, compare the
original file against its pre-refresh snapshot before updating it; otherwise concurrent credentials can be
overwritten or the original can retain an invalidated refresh token. This case passed the API read after
refresh and safely updated the unchanged original config. Keep token bodies out of logs and remove temporary
credential copies after the operation. No new login or account setting change was needed.

## OPS-527 — Astro on Workers: wrap the adapter's handler with `"main": "src/worker.ts"` to rewrite a request before Astro sees it (a cross-account relay that keeps `Astro.url` on the public host)

`측정 2026-10-19 · Astro 7.3.3 · @astrojs/cloudflare 14.3.2 · wrangler 4.135.0 · Workers Free`

**증상:** an OPS-510 relay Worker in the old account forwards the apex to the new account's `*.workers.dev`. Inside
Astro, `request.url`, `Astro.url` and every origin check then say `*.workers.dev`: same-origin POST checks reject the
browser's `Origin: https://<apex>`, generated links point at workers.dev, and a beacon gated on the public host is
left out. Astro middleware cannot replace the URL the pages see. `astro check` also fails on a global `Env` in the
entry (`ts(2304): Cannot find name 'Env'`) when the project has no `wrangler types` output.

**해결:** set `"main": "src/worker.ts"` in `wrangler.jsonc` (the adapter uses `config.main` and falls back to
`@astrojs/cloudflare/entrypoints/server`, which is only `{ fetch: handle }`) and wrap it:
`import { handle } from "@astrojs/cloudflare/handler"`, then `handle(rewritten, env as Parameters<typeof handle>[1], ctx)`.
Rewrite only when a shared-secret header matches (compare digests): `new Request(newUrl, request)` keeps method and
body, then delete the relay headers and set `cf-connecting-ip` / `cf-ipcountry` from the relay's copies; without the
secret just delete the relay headers. In the relay, drop `host`, `cf-*`, `x-forwarded-*`, `x-real-ip` before
`fetch(..., { redirect: "manual" })`, rewrite a `Location` that starts with the workers.dev origin, and answer `http://`
and `www` itself (OPS-498). Measured on the live apex: the cookie unlock (same-origin POST) 204, all pages 200, the
beacon only on the apex, a forged secret on workers.dev ignored, and a sign-up with the real Turnstile in Brave
returned a verification link on the apex. `dist/server/wrangler.json` still says `main: "entry.mjs"`; the wrapper is
bundled into it.

## OPS-528 — Cloudflare stopped account creation after three additional Free accounts (docs say five): 422 「생성할 수 있는 계정 수의 한도에 도달했습니다」

`측정 2026-10-19 · dash.cloudflare.com (ko UI), account switcher → 「+ 계정 만들기」 · one login with four accounts`

**증상:** a login that owned one account created three more the same day (two in the morning, two in the evening
minus one). The next 「계정 생성」 answered `POST /api/v4/accounts` → **422** and the dialog said 「생성할 수 있는 계정 수의
한도에 도달했습니다」. The official page "Create account" says a user "can create up to five additional Free accounts"
(user active and at least 7 days old, Super Administrator on an existing account) and gives "use an existing account
or contact your account team" as the remedy. A script looping over seven new names failed on all of them.

**해결:** count the slots before promising one account per project. Give the slots to the projects that use the most
account-wide Free quota (Workers requests, D1 rows, KV, AI neurons, Pages builds); zone features (WAF, cache, rules)
are per zone and gain nothing from a separate account. An account can be renamed (`PUT /accounts/:id {"name": …}`),
so a slot created for one project can be given to another.

## OPS-529 — Moving a Cloudflare Registrar domain to another account: the clicks, where the gaining account accepts, and how fast it switched

`측정 2026-10-19 · Cloudflare Registrar .com registered 2026-09-17 · dashboard (ko UI) in Brave via Playwright · gaining account created the same day, no payment method`

**증상:** the steps are spread over two accounts and the gaining side has no obvious page; the docs mention a mail.

- Losing account: 도메인 → 등록 → domain 「관리」 → 「다른 계정으로 이동」 → 「계속」 → `input[name=accountId]` and
  `input[name=confirmAccountId]` (type the target account ID into both) → 「계속」 → two acknowledgement checkboxes
  (getByRole checkbox, `check({force:true})`) → 「제출」. The page then shows 「계정 이동 취소」.
- Gaining account: `/{account}/domains/registrations` lists the domain as 「계정 가져오기 보류 중」 (the 전송 page is
  a 404). Its 「관리」 opens `/{account}/domains/registrations/action-center` (「작업 센터」) with 「동의」 / 「거부」;
  no mail click is needed. `GET /accounts/:id/registrar/domains` shows `actionable_metadata` type `domain_move`,
  `expires_at` 5 days out.
- Timings: accepted 02:19:56 UTC; `dig NS <domain> @a.gtld-servers.net +norec` showed the new zone's pair at
  02:23:55; `PUT /zones/:id/activation_check` then `status: active` at 02:24:08. The old zone in the losing account
  kept answering on the old nameservers (TTL 172800), so both accounts serve for up to two days.
- The gaining account warns 「청구 프로필에 결제 수단이 없습니다. 자동 갱신을 위해 결제 수단을 추가하세요」.
- Email Routing's MX and `cf2024-1._domainkey` records are read-only managed records; they are not copied to the
  new zone, and `POST …/email/routing/enable` recreates them. Rules to chowooick@gmail.com were refused with
  `2054 Destination address is not verified` until the address is verified again in the new account (one mail click
  per account).

**해결:** prepare the new zone (records, settings, rulesets, tunnel hostnames) and the Workers in the gaining account
first, deploy the Workers on workers.dev, then move. Run the custom-domain deploy and `activation_check` as soon as
the registry shows the new nameservers; clear the old Worker's crons (`PUT …/workers/scripts/<name>/schedules []`) so
the two copies do not both run them. Verify the Email Routing destination before the move, and add a card to the
gaining account before the registration's expiry.

## OPS-530 — Reading a Worker's secret values back for an account move: an undeployed version on a preview URL that returns them encrypted to an offline key

`측정 2026-10-19 · wrangler 4.151.2 versions upload · Workers preview URLs · Worker with 8 secrets and no other copy of them`

**증상:** Worker secrets are write-only (the API lists names only), and some must not change: a mail-signing secret
that derives subscriber IDs and every unsubscribe link already sent. Moving the Worker to another account needed the
exact values.

**해결:** `wrangler versions upload --config <tmp>/wrangler.json` with `name` = the Worker and a tiny `main` uploads a
version **without deploying it**; secrets are inherited by every version. The code answers only a request carrying a
one-time header and returns `{key, iv, ct}`: the JSON of the secret values encrypted with AES-GCM, the AES key wrapped
with RSA-OAEP-256 to a public key whose private half never left the Mac. Turn previews on
(`POST /accounts/:a/workers/scripts/<name>/subdomain {"enabled":false,"previews_enabled":true}`), call
`https://<first 8 of version id>-<name>.<account subdomain>.workers.dev/`, decrypt with Node
(`privateDecrypt` OAEP sha256, then `aes-256-gcm` with the last 16 bytes as the tag), write the values to a 0600
file, turn previews off (the URL then answers 404) and delete the key pair. Production stayed on its version at 100 %
the whole time. `wrangler secret bulk <json>` then sets them in the new account.

## OPS-531 — `wrangler d1 execute --file` of a `d1 export` dump fails with `SQLITE_TOOBIG` on rows above ~100 KB

`측정 2026-10-19 · wrangler 4.134.0 · D1 export 12.7 MB, 568 INSERT lines`

**증상:** importing a D1 export into a new database stopped at once with `statement too long: SQLITE_TOOBIG`. 19
`INSERT` lines for a table of image files were over 90 KB each (D1's statement limit is 100 KB).

**해결:** split the dump: lines over ~90 KB aside, the rest through `d1 execute --file` (598 queries in 0.38 s); load
the large rows another way (chunked updates, or keep the files in R2/KV) or skip them if the copy is only a fallback.

## OPS-532 — Korea Post's full postal-code DB downloads without a key; codes are 기초구역번호 per building, and 사서함 codes overlap ordinary ones

`측정 2026-10-19 · 우정사업본부 지역별 주소 DB (2026.10.08 기준, 고시 2026.10.13) · Python 3.9`

**증상:** a Korean service keyed by the 5-digit postal code needed every valid code with a readable neighborhood name.
The juso.go.kr dumps and data.go.kr APIs ask for an application or a key.

**해결:** `https://www.epost.go.kr/search/areacd/zipcode_DB.zip` (page `/search/zipcode/areacdAddressDown.jsp`) downloads
directly: 115 MB, 16 text files by 시도, 6,459,663 building rows, each with 우편번호, 법정동, 읍면, 리, 행정동 and 건물관리번호.
There are 34,403 distinct codes (01000–63644). Naming by 법정동 fits 79.7% of urban codes inside one 동 (행정동 only
48.3%); in 읍·면 areas use 면 + 리. 431 of 432 사서함 codes are also ordinary area codes, and 534 codes cover a single
building (mostly apartment complexes). A building-count split under-weights large apartment complexes (one address each).
One 동 is split across many codes (망원동: 04005–04018). data.go.kr 15000302 lists the service as "이용허락범위: 제한 없음",
but the 인터넷우체국 이용약관 §22② bars commercial reuse of its works without consent; confirm with 우정사업본부 before a
commercial launch. A 20-code random sample matched the public epost search 20/20.

## OPS-533 — A mail sent the minute Email Routing is enabled bounces "Recipient not found", and Resend then suppresses that address for good

`측정 2026-10-20 · Cloudflare Email Routing (zone with no MX before) · Resend free plan, ap-northeast-1`

**증상:** `POST /zones/:id/email/routing/enable` answered `ready` and the MX records showed at 1.1.1.1 within seconds,
but a Resend mail to the routed address sent about a minute later was `Bounced` with "Recipient not found" and then
`Suppressed`. Later mails to that address are dropped by Resend without trying; a mail to a second routed address
of the same zone sent eight minutes later was `Delivered`. The sending-only API key cannot list or remove
suppressions, and the Cloudflare `emailRoutingAdaptive` GraphQL dataset stayed empty for the delivered mail for
several minutes.

**해결:** wait for the MX to resolve at the sender's side (minutes; the zone had a cached negative answer for MX)
before the first test, and test with a throwaway address first. To undo a suppression: dashboard → Emails →
Suppressions tab → row "More actions" → "Remove email address", and type the address to enable the button. Check
delivery on the email's page (Sent → Delivered events) rather than in Cloudflare analytics.

## OPS-534 — `getPlatformProxy({ persist: { path } })` and `wrangler dev --persist-to` do not share a directory as given: dev writes under `<dir>/v3/`, the proxy reads `<dir>/` itself. An Astro-built Worker (`dist/server/wrangler.json`) also ignores `--test-scheduled`

`측정 2026-10-19 · wrangler 4.135.0 · @astrojs/cloudflare 14.3.2 · Astro 7.3.3 · macOS (Air)`

**증상:** a local D1 filled with `wrangler d1 migrations apply <db> --local --persist-to .state` and served by
`wrangler dev --persist-to .state` lives in `.state/v3/d1/miniflare-D1DatabaseObject/<hash>.sqlite`. A Node script
that opened the same binding with `getPlatformProxy({ configPath, persist: { path: ".state" } })` answered
`D1_ERROR: no such table` and left a second, empty database in `.state/d1/…` (no `v3`). Passing
`persist: { path: ".state/v3" }` opened the real one; the proxy then ran a `db.batch()` of six DELETEs against it
while `wrangler dev` kept the same files open (as in OPS-106).

In the same setup `wrangler dev --config dist/server/wrangler.json --test-scheduled` (the config `@astrojs/cloudflare`
writes, `no_bundle: true`, custom `main` with a `scheduled` export) answered `GET /__scheduled?cron=…` with Astro's
own 404 page: the request reached the Worker's `fetch` instead of the scheduled test endpoint. The `scheduled` export
itself was in `dist/server/entry.mjs` and `triggers.crons` from `wrangler.jsonc` was copied into the generated config.

**해결:** when `wrangler dev` or `wrangler d1 … --local` used `--persist-to <dir>`, give `getPlatformProxy` the path
`<dir>/v3`. To exercise a cron handler of an Astro Worker locally, call the handler's function through
`getPlatformProxy` (OPS-106) rather than `/__scheduled`, and check `grep scheduled dist/server/entry.mjs` plus
`"triggers"` in `dist/server/wrangler.json` for the deploy itself.

## OPS-535 — Loading ~39,000 rows into a Workers Free D1 spends the whole day's write quota; the next INSERT fails with "exceeded D1's free tier daily row write limit"

`측정 2026-10-20 · Cloudflare D1 (Workers Free) · wrangler 4.135.0 `d1 execute --remote --file``

**증상:** a new production D1 got two migrations, 4,499 rows in one table and 34,403 rows (with an index on a foreign key
column) in another, loaded in batches of 500. Two hours later the first real sign-up failed: the Worker caught
`Error: D1_ERROR: Your account has exceeded D1's free tier daily row write limit. Upgrade to a paid plan or wait until
tomorrow (midnight UTC) to continue.` Reads kept working. Rows written count each index entry, so ~39,000 rows with
indexes reached the 100,000-a-day account limit; the limit is per account, so every D1 database of the account stopped
taking writes until 00:00 UTC.

**해결:** load bulk reference data the day before a launch, or into a store without the quota (a Worker can run under
`wrangler dev` with a persisted local D1, OPS-332), or on Workers Paid. Afterwards load only the rows that changed. Log
the caught error in API catch blocks: a generic "could not save" answer hid this cause until `wrangler tail` showed the
message.

## OPS-536 — `wrangler dev --local-upstream <host>` behind a proxy: forwarding `Host: <host>` makes same-origin POST checks fail; keep the loopback Host

`측정 2026-10-20 · wrangler 4.135.0 dev (Astro 7 Cloudflare adapter output) · Node http proxy in Docker on Linux arm64`

**증상:** a Worker that rejects a POST unless `Origin` equals `new URL(request.url).origin` ran under `wrangler dev
--local-upstream dongnesosik.com` behind a small Node proxy. Every POST through the proxy answered the rejection,
while the same POST sent straight to `127.0.0.1:8788` with Node `fetch` (which drops a custom Host) passed. With
`http.request` the result depended only on the Host header: `Host: dongnesosik.com` → rejected,
`Host: 127.0.0.1:8788` or none → accepted. GET pages were fine either way.

**해결:** forward with `host: "127.0.0.1:8788"` and let `--local-upstream` present the public host to the Worker. Test
a POST through the full path (proxy and Traefik) before switching traffic, not only GETs.

## OPS-537 — `sxtwl` 2.0.7 on Apple Silicon with Python 3.12: no wheel, and the sdist is missing `src/`; build the wheel from the GitHub `python/` folder

`측정 2026-10-19 · sxtwl 2.0.7 · uv 0.12.10 · CPython 3.12.14 macOS arm64`

**증상:** `uv sync` fails with `clang++: error: no such file or directory: 'src/JD.cpp'`. PyPI has cp312 wheels only for
macOS x86_64, Linux and Windows. A `git+https://github.com/yuangu/sxtwl_cpp` dependency fails too: the repo root has no `setup.py`.

**해결:** `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/yuangu/sxtwl_cpp && cd sxtwl_cpp/python && cp -R ../src ./src && uv build --wheel --python 3.12 -o <repo>/wheels`,
then in pyproject: `[tool.uv.sources] sxtwl = [{ path = "wheels/sxtwl-2.0.7-cp312-cp312-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl", marker = "sys_platform == 'darwin'" }]`
(`find-links` alone lost to the PyPI sdist). Linux keeps the PyPI wheel.

## OPS-538 — Hermes Agent on the shared MacBook Air: the installer's own uv is blocked by LuLu (looks like a GitHub timeout); run the official Docker image in a separate colima profile

`측정 2026-10-19 · Hermes Agent v0.22.2 · install.sh --non-interactive · MacBook Air M1 with LuLu (alert mode) · colima vz · nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`

**증상:** `install.sh` always fails at "Downloading Python 3.14" with `Failed to download …python-build-standalone… client error (Connect) operation timed out`,
twice, while DNS checks a minute later resolved github.com in 0.05 s. The installer runs only its pinned uv
(`$HERMES_HOME/tools/uv-…/uv`, "never a uv already on PATH"), a new binary with no LuLu rule (OPS-227).
A manual `uv pip install -e .` into a 3.12 venv with the allowed `~/.local/bin/uv` installs, but `hermes gateway` then
demands `requires-python ==3.14.*` for its self-update and dies with `No module named 'ruamel'`.

**해결:** Docker: `colima start <own-profile> --vm-type vz --cpu 1 --memory 2`, `docker --context colima-<profile> run -d --name … -v <named-volume>:/opt/data -p 127.0.0.1:8644:8642 -e API_SERVER_ENABLED=true -e API_SERVER_HOST=0.0.0.0 --env-file <file with API_SERVER_KEY and the provider key> nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest gateway run`,
then `docker cp config.yaml <container>:/opt/data/config.yaml` and restart. VM traffic goes out through `limactl`, which LuLu already allows.
Use a named volume: a host bind mount puts Hermes' SQLite on virtiofs and it warns on every database.

## OPS-539 — CSS `mask-image` on a horizontal scroller: after a restored page scroll the scroller's children are not painted (headless Brave 155)

`측정 2026-10-20 · Brave 155 (Chromium 155) headless via Playwright 1.63 · MacBook Air M1`

**증상:** a horizontally scrolling chip row (`display:flex; overflow-x:auto`) with an edge fade
`mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0, #000 16px, #000 calc(100% - 16px), transparent)`
rendered as an empty band in a screenshot taken after a reload that restored the scroll position
(`window.scrollTo` to y ≈ 2000, then `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` on a section below the row). DOM and
computed style were normal: the row and its buttons had correct boxes, `opacity: 1`,
`visibility: visible`, `scrollLeft: 0`. Opening the page fresh and scrolling there painted the row.
Injecting `.chips { mask-image: none }` with nothing else changed made the row paint in the same sequence.

**해결:** do not put `mask-image` on a scroll container that can be reached by a restored or
programmatic scroll; drop the fade (or draw it with an overlay outside the scroller). Only headless
was measured; whether headed Brave or Chrome does the same was not checked. A check that asserts
only DOM boxes or computed styles passes on this failure — look at the screenshot.

## OPS-540 — Lighthouse simulated (Lantern) FCP/LCP flips between two values run to run on a fast local server: a web font that finishes before the observed first paint becomes render-blocking

`측정 2026-10-20 · Lighthouse 13.5.0 (trace_engine Lantern) · headless Brave 155 · Next 16 standalone on the MacBook Air M1, 127.0.0.1`

**증상:** the same build measured with `--throttling-method=simulate` gave LCP either ~3.2–3.6 s
or ~4.7–5.7 s, and FCP either ~1.0–1.4 s or exactly 2.86 s, with nothing in between. Eleven runs of
one build: 5 fast, 6 slow; eleven of a slightly larger build: 1 fast, 10 slow. Comparing three runs per
build reported a 1.56 s "regression" that was this coin toss. `--throttling-method=devtools` on the
same builds was stable (LCP spread under 0.1 s) and showed the larger build 0.17 s faster.

Lantern's FCP graph (`FirstContentfulPaint.getFirstPaintBasedGraph`) keeps every network request
that **ended before the observed, unthrottled FCP** and `hasRenderBlockingPriority()` (VeryHigh or
High). A web font discovered from CSS is fetched at VeryHigh. On a local server the 272 KB Korean
font finished at 90–115 ms and the page painted at 90–150 ms, so in some runs the font ended first,
was counted as render-blocking, and its throttled download (~1.5 s at the simulated 1.6 Mbps) was
added to FCP and LCP. The slow runs have font `networkEndTime` < `observedFirstContentfulPaint`
in the JSON (`network-requests` and `metrics` audits); the fast runs have it the other way round.

**해결:** for before/after comparisons use many alternating runs (≥ 5 pairs) and report the
distribution, not a 3-run median, or use DevTools throttling as the primary number. Check each slow
run by comparing the font's `networkEndTime` with `observedFirstContentfulPaint` before calling it
a regression.

## OPS-541 — VoiceOver from ssh on macOS 27: `VoiceOverStarter` is gone, and the welcome splash makes every AppleScript read time out

`측정 2026-10-20 · macOS 27.0.1 · VoiceOver (ScreenReader.framework) · MacBook Air M1, console unlocked, driven over ssh`

**증상:** OPS-363's start command fails: `/System/Library/CoreServices/VoiceOver.app/Contents/MacOS/VoiceOverStarter`
→ `no such file or directory`. A bare `osascript -e 'tell application "VoiceOver" to get content of last phrase'`
then hangs and launches `VoiceOver Quickstart.app` (the tutorial) instead. With VoiceOver started by
`launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.apple.VoiceOver`, every read (`text under cursor of vo cursor`,
`content of last phrase`) ended in `spawnSync osascript ETIMEDOUT` (8 s timeout) for the whole run. The
console showed nothing to ssh (`screencapture`: "could not create image from display").

The cause was VoiceOver's welcome splash, which waits for a click while VoiceOver answers no scripting.
`defaults read com.apple.VoiceOverTraining doNotShowSplashScreen` was `0`.

**해결:** before starting, `defaults write com.apple.VoiceOverTraining doNotShowSplashScreen -bool true`
and `defaults write com.apple.VoiceOver4/default SCREnableAppleScript -bool YES`; mute with
`osascript -e 'set volume output muted true'`; open the browser first, then
`launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.apple.VoiceOver` and wait ~10 s. Reads then answer at once (Korean
phrases such as "배틀마블 지금 플레이 버튼"). Afterwards `tell application "VoiceOver" to quit` and restore all
three values (here: splash `false`, delete `SCREnableAppleScript`, unmute). Kill a stray `VoiceOver Quickstart`
if a read was attempted before VoiceOver was running. Related: OPS-363, OPS-521.

## OPS-542 — A new Microsoft account signed in by Playwright gets locked (`account.live.com/Abuse`), and the owner's running Brave can be driven over ssh with `osascript` instead

`측정 2026-10-20 · Microsoft account (gmail address, email-code sign-in) · Azure free-trial signup · Brave 1.96 · macOS 27 · MacBook Air M1 over ssh`

**증상:** a freshly created Microsoft account (a `@gmail.com` address, no password, email-code sign-in) was signed in a few times by Playwright (persistent profile, `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled`, typed with delays) on the way to `signup.azure.com`. After the code was accepted the page became `account.live.com/Abuse`: "… 계정이 잠겨 있습니다. Microsoft 서비스 계약을 위반하는 활동을 감지하여 계정을 잠갔습니다. 다음 단계에서 본인이 사람임을 확인하면 됩니다." The owner signing in by hand in a normal browser did not clear it; the next automated sign-in landed on the same page. The unlock step asks for a phone number and an SMS code, and the Azure trial after it asks for a card, so a session cannot finish either.

What does work from ssh on the Air, against the owner's normal (non-automation) Brave and Safari:
- `osascript -e 'tell application "Brave Browser" to make new window'`, `set URL of active tab of w to …`, and `get {title, URL} of tabs of windows` all work without a prompt. Address windows by `id` so other sessions' windows are left alone.
- `execute … javascript` fails with "AppleScript를 통한 자바스크립트 실행 기능이 꺼져 있습니다 … 보기 > 개발자 > Apple Events의 자바스크립트 허용" (off by default).
- Page text is still readable: `tell active tab of w` → `select all`, `copy selection`, then `pbpaste` over ssh. Save and restore the clipboard around it; other sessions share it.
- `tell application "System Events" to tell process "Brave Browser" …` answered (menu bar names listed), so UI scripting is permitted for the ssh user.
- Safari: `make new document with properties {URL:…}` returns a reference that cannot be used afterwards (-1728); use `front document`.
- `set w to make new window` then `id of w` once returned the id of **another session's existing window** (a session that opens and closes one window per page): the `set URL` that followed navigated that session's tab. List `id of windows` before and after, take the id that is new, and stop if there is none. Windows you open can also be closed by such a session within a minute.

**해결:** do not script sign-ins of a new Microsoft account; one lock costs an SMS round trip on the owner's phone. Open the signup screen in the owner's own Brave with `osascript` and let the owner do the parts that need their mailbox, phone and card. For the CLI side, `~/.local/bin/uv tool install --python 3.12 azure-cli` installs `az` 2.91.0 under the LuLu rules (OPS-227), and `az login --use-device-code` keeps the account out of any automated browser.

## OPS-543 — Azure CLI signed in before the free-trial signup never lists the new subscription; ARM REST with its token does, and a body-less ARM POST from curl is HTTP 411

`측정 2026-10-20 · azure-cli 2.91.0 (uv tool, Python 3.12) · Azure free trial (quotaId FreeTrial_2014-09-01) · Microsoft.CognitiveServices api-version 2023-05-01 · MacBook Air M1`

**증상:** `az login --use-device-code --allow-no-subscriptions` was done while the account had no subscription (only `N/A(tenant level account)`). After the free-trial signup finished, `az account list --refresh` still showed only the tenant entry, every time over several minutes. `az account tenant list` failed instead ("The command requires the extension account … Pip failed with status code 1"). Yet `GET https://management.azure.com/subscriptions?api-version=2022-12-01` with `az account get-access-token` returned the new subscription ("Azure subscription 1", Enabled, FreeTrial) at once.

A curl `-X POST` with no body to ARM (`…/providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/register`, `…/accounts/<name>/listKeys`) gets **HTTP 411 Length Required** as an HTML page, which breaks a `| python -c 'json.load…'` pipe with `JSONDecodeError: Expecting value`.

**해결:** either `az login` again after the signup, or skip the CLI's subscription cache and call ARM REST with the CLI token: register the provider (`POST …/register`, poll `GET …/providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices` until `Registered`, about 10–20 s), `PUT …/resourcegroups/<rg>`, `PUT …/accounts/<name>?api-version=2023-05-01` with `{"kind":"SpeechServices","sku":{"name":"F0"},"location":"koreacentral","properties":{}}` (Succeeded within seconds), then `POST …/listKeys`. Give every body-less POST `-d '{}'`. Pipe `listKeys` straight into a 0600 file rather than printing it.

Measured on the result: Azure `ko-KR-SunHiNeural` in koreacentral through the LiveKit `azure` plugin (livekit-agents 1.8.8), first audio median 0.23 s over 33 utterances (0.19–1.03 s); raw REST `cognitiveservices/v1` MP3 first byte 0.57–0.60 s warm, 1.47 s cold. Edge TTS for the same voice in the same worker was 0.48–0.90 s.

## OPS-544 — Expo SDK 58 release APK with `@livekit/react-native-webrtc` 150 fails in R8 on `livekit.org.jni_zero.JniZeroJni`; add keep rules through `expo-build-properties`

`측정 2026-10-20 · Expo SDK 58.0.16 · React Native 0.88.0 · @livekit/react-native 3.1 · @livekit/react-native-webrtc 150.1 · Gradle 9.4.1 · JDK 25 (Temurin) · Pixel 7 Pro`

**증상:** `npx expo prebuild --platform android` writes `android.enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds=true` into `gradle.properties`, so `./gradlew assembleRelease` runs R8 and stops at `:app:minifyReleaseWithR8`:

```
ERROR: R8: Missing class livekit.org.jni_zero.JniZeroJni (referenced from: void livekit.org.jni_zero.JniZero.setJniClassLoader(java.lang.ClassLoader))
```

The generated `missing_rules.txt` offers only a `-dontwarn`. That makes the build pass but leaves R8 free to strip or rename the WebRTC classes that native code finds by name over JNI.

Two more things on the way: the prebuilt project has no `android/local.properties`, so a shell without `ANDROID_HOME` fails at configuration with `SDK location not found` (after Gradle has already spent minutes); and a single `Read timed out` from `dl.google.com` disables the Google repository for the whole run (`Repository Google is disabled due to earlier error below`) — rerun with `-Dorg.gradle.internal.http.socketTimeout=180000 -Dorg.gradle.internal.http.connectionTimeout=180000`.

**해결:** keep the rules in `app.json` so a later `prebuild --clean` keeps them: `npx expo install expo-build-properties` (it adds the plugin to `app.json` by itself — do not add a second entry), then give it

```json
["expo-build-properties", {"android": {"extraProguardRules":
  "-keep class livekit.org.webrtc.** { *; }\n-keep class livekit.org.jni_zero.** { *; }\n-dontwarn livekit.org.jni_zero.JniZeroJni"}}]
```

and run `prebuild` again. The release build (`-PreactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a`) then took 1 m 57 s and gave a 50.7 MB APK that installed and opened on a Pixel 7 Pro. `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` values are inlined into the Hermes bundle at build time; check with a byte search of `assets/index.android.bundle` (`strings` misses Hermes string tables).

## OPS-545 — Next 16 `experimental.inlineCss` ships every CSS rule twice (the `<style>` and the RSC payload): a 92-rule Pretendard dynamic-subset stylesheet doubled a page's HTML

`측정 2026-10-20 · Next 16.3.2 (Turbopack build, standalone) · pretendard@1.3.9 dynamic subset · curl + gzip on the MacBook Air`

**증상:** importing the official `pretendardvariable-dynamic-subset.css` (92 `@font-face` rules, 55 KB) into a layout of an app with
`experimental: { inlineCss: true }` grew the page's HTML from 41.2 KB to 82.4 KB gzip. The HTML held 196 `@font-face` occurrences
for 104 rules: every rule once in the inlined `<style>` and again, escaped, in the `self.__next_f.push` flight scripts. Only 16
of the 92 ranges were used by the page, so most of those bytes described fonts that are never fetched.

**해결:** with `inlineCss`, keep large rule sets small at the source. For a dynamic-subset web font, generate a stylesheet with
only the `@font-face` rules whose `unicode-range` covers characters the page can show (here 18 of 92, 17.8 KB raw; HTML back to
64 KB gzip, the rest being page CSS and content), point it at the unmodified woff2 files with absolute URLs, and add a test that
recomputes the needed ranges from the page's source so new copy cannot silently fall back to a system face.

## OPS-546 — A web font downloads for an element with no text: the body's `font-family` pulls the face whose `unicode-range` covers U+0020

`측정 2026-10-20 · Brave 155 (Chromium) headless · Next 16.3.2 page whose content sets its own font-family on a child div`

**증상:** a page whose every visible text node used Pretendard still fetched `NotoSansKR-latin.woff2` (62 KB) and listed
`Noto Sans KR Core` as `loaded` in `document.fonts`. No rendered element with text had Noto in its computed `font-family`
(checked over `body *`). The `<body>` kept the site-wide `font-sans` class (Noto first, its Latin face declared with
`unicode-range: U+0020-024F, …`). Chromium resolves the body's first available font for its line metrics, which needs the face
that covers the space character, so it downloads that face even when the body has no text of its own.

**해결:** on a page that switches faces below `<body>`, set the same family on `<body>` too (here
`body.migration-shell:has(> .cs) { font-family: "Pretendard Variable", … }`). The Noto request disappeared and
`document.fonts` listed only Pretendard. Check with `performance.getEntriesByType("resource")` for unexpected `.woff2` URLs, not
only with screenshots.

## OPS-547 — A horizontal scroll-snap strip shows an empty "peek" card: `loading="lazy"` images off to the side never load until swiped, and audits stay green

`측정 2026-10-20 · Brave 155 (Chromium) headless · 390 and 320 px viewports · Next 16.3.2 page, plain <img loading="lazy">`

**증상:** on phones, each service group was a horizontal `scroll-snap` strip showing a sliver of the next item (a "peek").
After a full vertical slow scroll, the peeking items still showed blank frames. 17 images in the strips were still
`complete === false`. Every automated check passed anyway: horizontal overflow 0, broken images 0 (a not-yet-loaded lazy
image is not broken), console errors 0 and axe 0. Only reading the viewport screenshots by eye caught it. A second cause made
the peek look empty even after the image loaded: a phone mock-up centred in a card as wide as a browser frame leaves the
card's left ~90 px as padding, and that padding is exactly what the peek shows.

**해결:** load a strip's images as soon as the strip nears the viewport. An `IntersectionObserver` on the strip with a
600 px `rootMargin` sets `loading="eager"` on its images; `eager` on the first two items also works. Pending images after
the scroll dropped from 17 to 0. Size each strip item to its content, for example a phone card at about 52 % of the strip
(min 176 px) and a browser frame at 80 %, so the peek shows the picture. To check: after scrolling, count
`[...document.images].filter(i => !i.complete)` and look at the strip in a screenshot.

## OPS-548 — Serving a customer's domain (CNAME to a tunnel hostname) on a free zone: Cloudflare for SaaS checkout, tunnel host as fallback origin, an ingress rule per custom hostname, and server code that still calls the old site on that name

`측정 2026-10-20 · Cloudflare free zone, Cloudflare for SaaS (usage-based) · dashboard ko UI in Brave 155 via CDP · cloudflared remote-managed tunnel run by Dokploy · Node 24/26 node:https`

**증상:** another company was asked to add `CNAME pa.<their-domain> → app.<our-zone>`, where `app.<our-zone>` is a proxied CNAME to a Cloudflare Tunnel. Without Cloudflare for SaaS such a request reaches Cloudflare with a hostname no zone owns and fails; the API answers `custom_hostnames` with `1404 No quota has been allocated` and `fallback_origin` with `1456` (OPS-415). The old site on that name (WordPress) was also the target of our own server-side form submission, so after the CNAME flip the server would have called itself.

- Dashboard: zone → SSL/TLS → 사용자 설정 호스트 이름 → 「Cloudflare for SaaS 사용」 → checkout page `…/checkout/payment` ($0/개월, 사용량 기반, card on file). Its two consent checkboxes are hidden `input[aria-hidden]` (Playwright `check()` fails with "outside of the viewport"); clicking the label text (`getByText('에 동의합니다')`, `getByText('에 대해 이 카드를 청구하도록')`) ticks them, then `활성화` → `…/checkout/confirmation` 「구매 완료」. The zone API token worked for everything after that.
- `PUT /zones/<id>/custom_hostnames/fallback_origin {"origin":"app.<our-zone>"}` (the proxied tunnel CNAME itself) went `initializing` → `active` in under a minute. A custom hostname created before that shows `verification_errors: ["fallback origin is not active yet"]`; after it, the hostname stays `pending` with HTTP DCV `pending_validation` until the customer's CNAME exists, and validates by itself once it does.
- The tunnel matches on the **custom** hostname (the Host header stays `pa.<their-domain>`), so its ingress needs a rule for that name too (`PUT …/cfd_tunnel/<id>/configurations`, applied with no restart). Requests to `pa.<their-domain>` hit the edge before the flip but the hostname is not served until it is active.
- Server code that called `https://pa.<their-domain>/…`: keep URL, Host and TLS SNI, but connect to the old origin's IP with `node:https` `request(url, { lookup, agent: false })`. With the default keep-alive agent a reused socket ignored the custom `lookup`. Measured: the form page came back from the old origin through the pin; pointing the pin at `127.0.0.1` gave `ECONNREFUSED`, so the pin is what is used. The old origin's HTTP-01 certificate renewal will fail once the name points elsewhere, so the pin is temporary (until that cert's expiry).

**해결:** before the customer flips the CNAME: enable SaaS, set the tunnel hostname as fallback origin, create the custom hostname (`ssl.method: http`, `type: dv`), add the ingress rule, and pin any server-side calls to the old site. Ask the customer for a separate hostname for the old site before its certificate expires. Make canonical URLs a runtime setting so they can move to the customer's name after the flip without a rebuild.

## OPS-549 — Notification mail with no mail provider: a Worker with an Email Routing `send_email` binding, uploaded by REST, delivers only to verified destinations and says so per recipient

`측정 2026-10-20 · Cloudflare Workers Free · Email Routing enabled on the sending zone · Workers REST upload with a zone/account API token · Gmail recipient`

**증상:** a Node app on a Dokploy host had to email each form submission. Resend refused another domain (OPS-523), and `GET /zones/<id>/email/sending/subdomains` answered `2036 Unauthorized` for the zone token, so Cloudflare Email Sending was not usable either.

- A Worker can send through the `send_email` binding from any address on a zone that has Email Routing enabled, **but only to verified Email Routing destination addresses** of the account. For an unverified one, `env.MAIL.send()` throws `destination address is not a verified address`. In the same request a verified recipient still went through.
- `POST /accounts/<id>/email/routing/addresses {"email":…}` adds a destination as `unverified` and makes Cloudflare mail a verification link to that address. Nothing reaches it until its owner clicks.
- No wrangler needed: `PUT /accounts/<id>/workers/scripts/<name>` (multipart: `metadata` JSON with `main_module` and `bindings`, plus the module part as `application/javascript+module`), then `POST …/scripts/<name>/subdomain {"enabled":true,"previews_enabled":false}` for the `*.workers.dev` URL. Bindings used: `{"type":"send_email","name":"MAIL","allowed_destination_addresses":[…]}`, `plain_text` for the sender, and `secret_text` for a bearer token the app sends. Both calls answered `success: true` on the first try.
- `EmailMessage(from, to, raw)` takes **one** envelope recipient, so send once per address and keep both addresses in the `To:` header. The raw MIME needs RFC 2047 encoded `From`/`Subject` (`=?UTF-8?B?…?=`), `Date`, `Message-ID` and base64 parts. Measured: a multipart/alternative message reached the Gmail inbox (not spam) in under a minute, with the Korean subject and HTML table intact.

**해결:** for owner-facing notices, put a small relay Worker on the zone that already has Email Routing, protect it with a bearer secret (`crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual`), return per-recipient results, and have the app store the submission first so a mail failure never loses it. Add any outside recipient as a destination first and tell them to expect the Cloudflare verification mail.

## OPS-550 — Lighthouse mobile TBT: below-the-fold `content-visibility: auto` blocks near the first screen still lay out in the first-paint task; reveal them one per task, and do not use a CSS animation of `content-visibility` (it causes CLS)

`측정 2026-10-20 · Lighthouse 13.5.0 DevTools throttling (4× CPU) · headless Brave 155 · Next 16.3.2 page, 412 × 823 mobile`

**증상:** a long page whose sections below the hero already had `content-visibility: auto` still had a 56–68 ms task right
after FCP: `Layout` of 342 of 395 objects. The services section starts on the first screen of a phone, so it and its first
groups count as near the viewport and are laid out in the frame after first paint. With the base page at TBT 24 ms, this
one task kept the new page at 27–33 ms.

Measured in a proxy A/B (5 Lighthouse runs each): per-group `content-visibility: auto` alone did nothing (the groups are
within the proximity margin); `content-visibility: hidden` on the groups removed the task (diagnostic only). Starting the
groups `hidden` and turning them to `auto` after the first frame, one group per `setTimeout(0)`, gave TBT 19 against 26.
Doing the same with no script, `@keyframes { from, to { content-visibility: hidden } }` with staggered durations, also
gave TBT 18 but produced layout shifts: CLS 0.19 at 412 px in 4 of 5 loads and in Lighthouse (`layout-shifts` names the
group, previous rect at the section's top, current rect 0 × 0).

**해결:** `@media (scripting: enabled) { .group { content-visibility: hidden } }` plus an inline script that, on
`DOMContentLoaded` → `requestAnimationFrame`, sets `style.contentVisibility = 'auto'` on one group per task, with
measured `contain-intrinsic-size: auto <px>` per group and breakpoint so anchors still land. 15 alternating pairs: TBT 17
against 24, CLS 0. Put that inline script **at the end of the body**: placed at the top of the body it made the first paint
show only the eyebrow line and pushed LCP (the headline) one frame later, +60 ms.

## OPS-551 — Next 16 with `inlineCss`: a route group that imports the app-wide `globals.css` ships all of it inline on every page of the group; dropping it cut a page's HTML from 65 to 45 KB gzip and LCP by ~60 ms under throttling

`측정 2026-10-20 · Next 16.3.2 Turbopack, experimental.inlineCss · Tailwind 4 globals.css · Lighthouse 13.5.0 DevTools throttling`

**증상:** a self-styled company home in its own route group (`src/app/(company)/…/layout.tsx`) inlined 107 KB of CSS
(24 KB gzip), of which 75 KB was the portal's `globals.css` (Tailwind, board styles, `--tw-*`) it never used. Under
DevTools throttling (1.47 Mb/s) the first paint waits for the whole inline `<style>`, so LCP was 811 ms against the base
page's 754 ms. CSS is per route, not per rendered branch: a `page.tsx` that renders two different designs ships both
designs' CSS.

**해결:** do not import `globals.css` in that layout; restate in the group's own CSS what its other pages actually took
from it (here the Noto `@font-face` rules and per-language stacks, the zh/ja line-breaking reset, `box-sizing` including the
container itself, and `:where()`-wrapped `img`/`p`/`a` resets so they do not outrank the page's classes). Check those pages
with a pixel diff against the old build: the first try differed because `box-sizing` was not applied to the `min-height:
100svh` container and a `.x p { margin: 0 }` reset overrode `.description { margin-bottom }`; after the fix the diff box was
empty at 390 and 1440.

## OPS-552 — Cloudflare caches a 404 for a new static file requested while Dokploy is still swapping the container; the URL stays 404 for hours after the deploy says `done`

`측정 2026-10-20 · Dokploy drop deployment (nj2) · Cloudflare proxied hostname + Cloudflare for SaaS custom hostname · Astro 7 node adapter`

**증상:** right after `deployment.all` reported the new deployment `done`, a check script fetched the release's new
files. The first one (`…/assets/mobile-1.webp`) got 404 because the old container was still serving. A minute later
every other new file answered 200, but that one kept answering 404 with `cf-cache-status: HIT` and
`cache-control: max-age=14400`, while the same URL with `?v=1` returned 200. HTML stayed `DYNAMIC` and was not
affected; image, CSS and JS extensions are cached by default, 404 included.

**해결:** after a deploy reports `done`, wait until one new URL answers 200 (with a cache-busting query) before
requesting the others, or purge what was requested too early: `POST /zones/<zone>/purge_cache` with
`{"files": [...]}` listing the URL on **every** hostname (a Cloudflare for SaaS custom hostname such as
`pa.example.com` is purged through the same zone). The next request was `MISS` with the new file.

## OPS-553 — `rsync --exclude dist` also drops `node_modules/*/dist`: copying a working tree that way leaves Astro's CLI unable to start (`Cannot find module …/node_modules/astro/dist/cli/index.js`)

`측정 2026-10-20 · rsync 3.x (macOS) · Astro 7.3.3 · Node 26 on the Air`

**증상:** a new release directory was made with `rsync -a --exclude dist --exclude .astro old/ new/` so the old build output would not come along. `npm test` (tsx) still passed, but `npx astro check` and `npm run build` failed at once with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND … node_modules/astro/dist/cli/index.js`. An unanchored `--exclude dist` matches a directory named `dist` at any depth, and most packages ship their code in `dist/`.

**해결:** anchor build-output excludes to the transfer root: `--exclude /dist --exclude /.astro` (or exclude `node_modules` and run `npm ci` in the copy). If it already happened, `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci` restores it.

## OPS-554 — Astro 7 on Node behind a TLS proxy: `@astrojs/node` builds `request.url` as `http://` from the socket and ignores `X-Forwarded-Proto`, so same-origin POST checks fail; a 30-line custom adapter fixes it

`측정 2026-10-21 · Astro 7.3.3 · @astrojs/node 11.1.9 · Node 24.22 (busan) and 26.8 (Air)`

**증상:** a site whose API rejects a POST unless `Origin` equals `new URL(request.url).origin` moved from a Worker to Node behind Traefik and a relay. In `@astrojs/node` 11, `createRequestFromNodeRequest` takes the protocol from `req.socket.encrypted` and passes `undefined` for the forwarded protocol (only `x-forwarded-host` is read, and only with `security.allowedDomains`). Behind any TLS-terminating proxy `request.url` is `http://<host>/…`, the browser's `Origin` is `https://…`, and every same-origin POST is refused. Verification links built from `url.origin` would also say `http://`.

**해결:** skip `@astrojs/node` and give the build your own server entry. An adapter needs only `setAdapter({ name, entrypointResolution: "auto", serverEntrypoint: <absolute path of your entry.ts>, adapterFeatures: { buildOutput: "server", middlewareMode: "classic" }, supportedAstroFeatures: {...} })` in `astro:config:done`; in the entry, `import { createApp } from "astro/app/entrypoint"`, build the Web `Request` with the public origin yourself and call `app.render(request, { addCookieHeader: true, routeData: app.match(request) })`. Serve `dist/client` before the app (no HTML there in `output: "server"`). Put the integration in `adapter:`, not `integrations:` — there it fails with `[NoAdapterInstalled] Cannot use server-rendered pages without an adapter`. Code that imports `cloudflare:workers` keeps working through a Vite alias to a module exporting `env`. The whole Node build took 0.7 s; the bundle still imports some of astro's dependencies (`piccolore`, `html-escaper`, `devalue`, `cookie`, …), so run `npm ci --omit=dev` in the image (move `@astrojs/cloudflare` to devDependencies or the image grows by ~500 MB of wrangler/workerd).

## OPS-555 — A Node server that hands `Readable.toWeb(req)` to a Web `Request` dies when the handler cancels the body early: `ERR_INVALID_STATE: Controller is already closed`, uncaught

`측정 2026-10-21 · Node 26.8.2 (Air) · Astro 7 app behind a node:http server`

**증상:** a handler that limits bodies to 4 KiB calls `request.body.cancel()` on a larger one (a 3,012-byte JSON passed, a bigger one did not). The Node side kept pushing chunks into the converted stream, and the process exited: `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_STATE]: Invalid state: Controller is already closed at ReadableStreamDefaultController.enqueue … at Transform.onData (node:internal/webstreams/adapters)`. One oversized POST takes the whole site down. The browser test caught it on its "oversized body" case; unit tests with small bodies never do.

**해결:** read the body into a buffer first, with a cap (64 KiB here; drain and answer 413 past it), and pass the `Uint8Array` as `body`. Test with a handler that cancels without reading, a 30 KB body, a chunked 70 KB body, and then a normal request to prove the server is still up.

## OPS-556 — Worker code on Node: a D1-shaped wrapper over `node:sqlite` needs four D1 rules, and the miniflare D1 store is a plain SQLite file you can move with `.backup`

`측정 2026-10-21 · node:sqlite (Node 24.22 / 26.8) · wrangler 4.135.0 local D1 store · Ubuntu 24.04 arm64`

**증상:** the same Worker code (`prepare().bind().first()/all()/run()`, `batch()`) ran on `node:sqlite` for a move off `wrangler dev`. What differs from D1: rows have a **null prototype** (`assert.deepEqual(row, {…})` fails, spread them into plain objects); booleans are not bindable (D1 binds `true` as 1); `undefined` must be refused (D1 throws `D1_TYPE_ERROR`); `batch` must be one transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` … `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK` on error). `statement.columns().length > 0` tells a `run()` with `RETURNING` apart. Turn on `PRAGMA foreign_keys` (D1 enforces them).

**해결:** keep the wrapper in the app and put the unit tests behind it, so one adapter is tested and deployed. The `wrangler dev --persist-to /data` store is `/data/v3/d1/miniflare-D1DatabaseObject/<hash>.sqlite` (next to a `metadata.sqlite`): a normal SQLite database in WAL mode with the app's tables, `d1_migrations` (`id, name, applied_at`) and `_cf_METADATA`. With the old process stopped, `sqlite3 <hash>.sqlite ".backup /data/app.sqlite"` moves it; keep the `d1_migrations` table name so later migrations continue. Memory for the same app: 464 MiB under `wrangler dev`, 44.5 MiB idle and 68 MiB after a sign-up on Node.

## OPS-557 — `url.host = "example.com"` keeps a port the URL already had: `http://127.0.0.1:65194/x` becomes `https://example.com:65194/x`

`측정 2026-10-21 · WHATWG URL in Node 26 and workerd`

**증상:** a relay rewrite did `url.protocol = "https:"; url.host = SITE_HOST` and was correct on `*.workers.dev` (no port). The same code behind a local server produced `https://dongnesosik.com:65194/…`, so the same-origin check failed. The URL standard's `host` setter only replaces the port when the new value contains one.

**해결:** set `url.port = ""` after `url.host = …` (or build a new URL from the public origin and the path).

## OPS-558 — Ubuntu's `rrsync -ro` does not work with macOS's `openrsync` client; serve read-only backups through a forced command with `list` and `get`

`측정 2026-10-21 · rrsync (Ubuntu 24.04 rsync 3.2.7) · openrsync protocol 29 (macOS 27)`

**증상:** a backup key pinned with `restrict,command="/usr/bin/rrsync -ro <dir>"` was used from a Mac. `rsync -a --delete` answered `rrsync error: option --delete-before has been disabled on this server.`; without `--delete`: `rrsync error: invalid rsync-command syntax or options` and `rsync: error: unexpected end of file`. The Mac has no GNU rsync (no Homebrew on that host).

**해결:** a 20-line forced command instead: `set -- $SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`; `list` prints the files, `get <kind>/<name>` `cat`s one only if the name matches a strict pattern; anything else prints `refused` and exits 1. The client fetches what it lacks and prunes by its own count — never delete local copies because the server stopped listing them, or losing the server empties the copy too.

## OPS-559 — Non-hashed static files behind a relay Worker stayed at the edge 9.6 hours after a release; purge the zone in the release script. R2 needs a payment method first

`측정 2026-10-21 · Cloudflare free zone · relay Worker fetching the origin · public/_headers "/images/* Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800"`

**증상:** a release script compared the SHA-256 of every client file fetched through the apex with the build. `/images/brand/share.png` (the `og:image`) differed: `cf-cache-status: HIT`, `age: 34575`, the file from two releases before. Earlier releases had checked hashes on the origin host and passed. Hashed `/_astro/*` names never go stale; fixed names with a week of `max-age` do.

**해결:** after the swap, `POST /zones/:id/purge_cache {"purge_everything":true}` (find the zone with `GET /zones?name=<domain>&status=active`, which also follows the zone when a domain moves accounts), then check hashes through the public host. Side note from the same day: `GET /accounts/:id/r2/buckets` answers `10042 Please enable R2 through the Cloudflare Dashboard` on accounts without a payment method, so a free plan cannot use R2 for off-site backups.

## OPS-560 — Kakao Local API results may not be stored, not even for 20 minutes: they cannot go into prepared content

`측정 2026-10-21 · Kakao DevTalk FAQ "카카오맵 API (지도/로컬) 문의 전 꼭 읽어 주세요" (devtalk.kakao.com/t/faq-api/125610) and staff answers`

**증상:** a daily local edition wanted shop listings from Kakao Local. The FAQ: "당사가 제공하는 API는 실시간으로 호출하여 사용하는 것만 가능합니다." and "로컬 API 등을 호출하여 응답받은 결과 데이터를 별도로 저장하여 사용하는 것은 허용하지 않습니다." A DevTalk answer refuses a 20-minute per-session cache as well. Commercial use is allowed, reselling or charging for API-based features is not.

**해결:** use Kakao Local only for live lookups shown as they come. For stored or generated content use public data that may be stored: 소상공인시장진흥공단 상가(상권)정보, 서울 열린데이터, 기상청·에어코리아 on data.go.kr.

## OPS-561 — A `SameSite=Strict` session cookie set by an OAuth callback is not sent on the callback's own redirect: the user lands signed out, intermittently

`측정 2026-10-20 · Brave 1.97 (Chromium 155) headless on the Air · Astro 7 node server behind Cloudflare · Google OAuth (code + PKCE)`

**증상:** `/admin/callback` exchanged the code, set `__Host-…_admin=…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` and answered `303 Location: /admin`. `/admin` then rendered the sign-in screen with no error. It happened on some sign-ins and not others (2 of 3 runs in one sequence).

- The navigation chain started on `accounts.google.com`, so the request that follows the 303 is still a cross-site navigation, and the browser leaves `Strict` cookies off it. The cookie *was* stored: reloading `/admin` showed the console.
- Whether the earlier run passed seems to depend on whether Google answered from its own page click (chooser) or redirected straight back. Do not rely on it.

**해결:** on success, answer the callback with a tiny `200` HTML page that sets the cookies and navigates itself (`<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;url=/admin">` plus `location.replace('/admin')`). The page's own navigation is same-site, so the `Strict` cookie goes along. After that change, 3 of 3 real sign-ins reached the console. Error outcomes can keep plain redirects, since they carry no cookie the next page needs. (The alternative, `SameSite=Lax`, also works but weakens the session cookie.)

## OPS-562 — Google's account chooser shows the brand's app name: a Firebase-created brand reads "project-<number>(으)로 이동"; a project with its own branding reads its app name, unverified and with no logo

`측정 2026-10-20 · Google Cloud console (Google 인증 플랫폼, Korean UI) · Brave 1.97 on the Air, signed-in profile copy`

**증상:** an admin page signing in through a shared Firebase project showed "계정을 선택하세요 · project-896121654173(으)로 이동": Firebase had created the OAuth brand with the default name, even though the Cloud project itself is called "MNORI". The signed-out identifier page showed the redirect domain instead ("to continue to mnori1.firebaseapp.com"). So the two Google screens name the app differently.

- A new project with branding filled (app name "CUCKOO Rental America", homepage, privacy and terms URLs, one authorized domain, no logo), external audience, and "앱 게시" → 확인 (production at once, no review for `openid email profile`): the signed-in chooser read "CUCKOO Rental America(으)로 이동" and the footer "앱을 사용하기 전에 CUCKOO Rental America의 개인정보처리방침 및 서비스 약관을 검토하세요". This differs from OPS-491, where the chooser showed the domain; what decides between name and domain is not known.
- Console automation notes: the project-create page's inputs have no `type` attribute (`input[type=text]` matches nothing; use `#p6ntest-name-input`, and `#p6ntest-id-input` after clicking `프로젝트 ID를 수정합니다.`); "시작하기" on `/auth/overview` and "앱 게시" on `/auth/audience` are not `role=button` (use `getByText(…, {exact:true})`); the branding page's URL fields are `input[id$="mat-input-1|2|3"]`, and after `도메인 추가` the domain field is `mat-input-5`.

**해결:** to show your own product name on Google's chooser, do not share another product's Firebase/OAuth brand. Give the site its own Cloud project with branding and its own web client, and use authorization code + PKCE on the server.

## OPS-563 — Dokploy `application.saveEnvironment` rejects a call without `buildArgs` and `buildSecrets`, even when the app has none

`측정 2026-10-20 · Dokploy API (nj2) · application.saveEnvironment`

**증상:** `POST /api/application.saveEnvironment {"applicationId":…,"env":…}` answered 400 `Input validation failed` with `fieldErrors: {buildArgs: ["Invalid input: expected nonoptional, received undefined"], buildSecrets: [same]}`. `application.one` returned `null` for both.

**해결:** read the app with `application.one`, change only your line of `env`, and send `buildArgs` and `buildSecrets` too (empty strings when `null`). The call then saved; `application.one` listed the new variable. Print variable names only, never the env body. The change applies on the next deploy.

## OPS-564 — Google Auth Platform 브랜딩: a Firebase-created brand in production cannot save any change until homepage, privacy policy and developer contact are filled, and the page shows no error

`측정 2026-10-20 · Google Cloud console (Google 인증 플랫폼, Korean UI) · Firebase project brand "project-<number>", external, production · Playwright in Brave on the Air`

**증상:** removing one authorized domain from a Firebase project's 브랜딩 page left `저장` disabled (`isDisabled() === true`), with no `mat-error` or alert on the page. Adding the developer contact email alone did not enable it.

- The form's `.ng-invalid` controls named the cause: `homePageUrl`, `privacyPolicyUrl` and `developerEmails`. Firebase creates the brand without them, and the form will not save while they are empty.
- After filling homepage, privacy and terms URLs and one contact email, `저장` enabled and the domain removal saved.

**해결:** when a console form's save button stays disabled with no message, list `form .ng-invalid` elements (their `formcontrolname`) to find the required fields. Fill them with the product's real pages; do not leave the brand half-edited. Related: OPS-084 (the same fields gate "앱 게시").

## OPS-565 — `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` makes Chromium send `Origin: null` with a same-origin form POST; `fetch()` POSTs from the same page keep the real origin

`측정 2026-10-21 · Brave 1.97 (Chromium 155) headless via Playwright on the Air · plain Node http server`

**증상:** an admin page served with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` had a sign-out `<form method="post">` to its own origin. The server's same-origin check (`Origin` must equal the site) refused it, while the page's JSON `fetch()` POSTs to the same server passed the same check. A page on 127.0.0.1 measured both in one browser:

- policy `no-referrer`: form POST `origin=null`, `sec-fetch-site=same-origin`; fetch POST `origin=http://127.0.0.1:4499`.
- policy `same-origin`: form POST and fetch POST both `origin=http://127.0.0.1:4499`.

This is the Fetch spec's rule for non-CORS requests (`no-referrer` serializes the origin as `null` for methods other than GET/HEAD); `fetch()` from the page is CORS-mode and is not affected.

**해결:** on pages that post forms to themselves and check `Origin`, use `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` (still nothing is sent to other sites), or post with `fetch()`. Do not relax the server check to accept `null`: any sandboxed or `data:` page sends that too. `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` stays correct under both policies and is a useful second check.

## OPS-566 — Google OAuth sign-in to a new web client from an automation profile: headless Brave is refused, headed Brave on the Air wants a passkey, headed Chrome for Testing on the main Mac passes; a Testing-mode app lets its project owner in without a test-user entry

`측정 2026-10-21 · Google Auth Platform (Korean UI), new project, external, publishing status Testing, no test users · Brave 1.97 on the Air (copy of ~/kc-test/profile) · Chrome for Testing (ms-playwright chromium-1243) on the main Mac (copy of ~/.gstack/chromium-profile)`

**증상:** a server-side code flow (PKCE, `scope=openid email`) had to be tested once with the owner's real account.

- Headless Brave with the Air's signed-in profile copy: the account chooser appeared; clicking the account went to `accounts.google.com/v3/signin/rejected` — "로그인할 수 없음 · 브라우저 또는 앱이 안전하지 않을 수 있습니다". The same profile drives the Cloud console headless without trouble, because no new sign-in happens there.
- Headed Brave (off-screen) with the same copy: the chooser led to `/v3/signin/challenge/pk` (passkey) and stopped.
- Headed Chrome for Testing on the main Mac with a copy of the gstack profile, off-screen (`--window-position=-2400,-2400`), as in OPS-447: chooser → `challenge/pk` passed on its own → `SetSID` → consent `signin/oauth/id` → `계속` → the app's callback; session set. The app ran on the Air; the Mac reached it through `ssh -f -N -L 4417:127.0.0.1:4417 air`, so the registered loopback redirect URI `http://127.0.0.1:4417/...` matched.
- The app was in Testing with no test users, and the project owner's account still got through. Adding a test user by script failed: in the 대상 page's "Add users" panel the chip was accepted (`1 / 100`), but clicking `저장` (by locator, by mouse, by Enter) sent no request at all; the list stayed "사용자 0명".

**해결:** for a one-off real sign-in, run the browser where the Google session is freshest (OPS-447) and forward the app's port to it rather than moving the app. For an owner-only admin, Testing mode with no test users is enough. For the console wizard itself (project create, `/auth/overview/create`), the selectors that worked: `getByLabel("프로젝트 이름")`, `input[formcontrolname=displayName]`, `cfc-select[formcontrolname=userSupportEmail]` then `getByRole("option", {name})`, `mat-radio-button` with text `외부` → its `input`, the contact chip `input[aria-label="이메일 텍스트 필드"]` + Enter, the last `input[type=checkbox]` (policy agreement, OPS-084), then `만들기`. The client page reads ID and secret as in OPS-332/OPS-342.

## OPS-567 — A column flexbox with `flex-wrap: wrap` sizes each line to its widest child's max-content, so a horizontal chip scroller inside it overflows the phone screen

`측정 2026-10-21 · Brave 1.96 (Chromium 154) · Playwright 1.58 · CUCKOO admin console, product page toolbar`

**증상:** a toolbar `display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap` switched to `flex-direction:column; align-items:stretch` under 960 px. Its first child was a chip row with `overflow-x:auto` (seven category chips, `white-space:nowrap`). At a 390 px viewport the chip row and the search field below it were both 468 px wide and the page scrolled sideways. The old check `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` passed because a Playwright `isMobile` context widens the layout viewport (AGT-074).

- In a multi-line (wrapping) flex container the cross size of each line comes from its items' content, not from the container. The chips' max-content width set the line width, and `align-items:stretch` stretched every item to it. `overflow-x:auto` on the chip row never got the chance to scroll.
- `flex-wrap: nowrap` on the column container fixed it. Each item then stretches to the container width (390 → 358 px) and the chips scroll inside it.

**해결:** when a wrapping row toolbar becomes a column on phones, set `flex-wrap: nowrap` in the same rule. Check overflow against the requested viewport width (`page.viewportSize().width`), not `innerWidth`.

## OPS-568 — A screen-reader-only `<table>` with the usual 1 px `.visually-hidden` class still widens the page: tables ignore `width: 1px`

`측정 2026-10-21 · Brave 1.96 (Chromium 154) · CUCKOO admin console chart`

**증상:** a chart had a hidden data table for screen readers, `<table class="visually-hidden">` (`position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; overflow:hidden; clip:rect(0 0 0 0); white-space:nowrap`). With 4 columns it fitted. With 6 columns, a 320 px phone layout grew to 379 px. The elements past the edge were the `TABLE`, its `CAPTION`, `THEAD` and `TH`, all with `right` = 379.

- A table's used width is at least its min-content width, so `width: 1px` does not shrink it. `white-space: nowrap` from the class makes every header cell a single line, which makes that minimum larger.

**해결:** put the class on a wrapper `div` and leave the `table` unstyled: `<div class="visually-hidden"><table>…</table></div>`. The div keeps its 1 px box and clips the table. After the change the page was 320 px wide again.

## OPS-569 — A full-page screenshot taken right after a link click on a page with `@view-transition { navigation: auto }` comes out stretched

`측정 2026-10-21 · Brave 1.96 (Chromium 154) headless · Playwright 1.58 · CUCKOO admin console`

**증상:** a test clicked a link from the home page to another page of the same site, waited for the URL and for Alpine, and took `page.screenshot({fullPage: true})`. In the 1440 × 1779 image, the main column's text was squashed and stretched sideways, and everything ended at y ≈ 960 with blank space below. The sidebar looked normal. Taken 400 ms later, the same page looked correct. An axe scan run in that state still passed.

- The CSS cross-document view transition (0.16 s here) was still animating the root snapshot from the old page's size to the new one. To take a full-page shot, Playwright resizes the viewport to the document height, which rescales that snapshot.

**해결:** after navigating by click on a site that opts into view transitions, wait out the transition before visual checks: `await page.waitForTimeout(<duration> + 250)`, or wait on `document.getAnimations()` emptying. A shot from a direct `page.goto` does not have this problem. Related: OPS-271 (`page.route` aborting view transitions).

## OPS-570 — Playwright `emulateMedia({colorScheme:'dark'})` on a page with `<picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">` + `loading="lazy"`: the full-page screenshot shows empty frames

`측정 2026-10-21 · playwright-core 1.58 · Brave 1.96 (Chromium 154, headless) on macOS · Astro 7 SSR page with 14 lazy screenshots`

**증상:** a light-mode pass scrolled the page, every `<img>` was `complete` with a `naturalWidth`, and the full-page
screenshot was correct. Right after `page.emulateMedia({colorScheme:'dark'})` the same page's full-page screenshot
had black, empty frames for every picture below the first screen; axe and the overflow check still passed.

- Switching the colour scheme makes each `<picture>` pick its dark `<source>`: a new URL, so the browser drops the
  loaded light image and starts the dark one. With `loading="lazy"` it only fetches the ones near the viewport;
  `fullPage: true` does not scroll, so the rest stay unloaded.
- A related trap on the same page: a "scroll through to trigger lazy images" loop of `scrollTo(0, y)` every 40 ms
  never got far, because the site sets `html{scroll-behavior:smooth}` and each call restarts the animation (OPS-150).

**해결:** after every `emulateMedia` colour change, scroll through again with
`scrollTo({top: y, behavior: 'instant'})`, then wait for
`[...document.querySelectorAll('img')].every(i => i.complete)` and assert `naturalWidth > 0` before the
screenshot. The page itself is fine: a real dark-mode reader loads the dark sources as they scroll.

## OPS-571 — misa's own Dokploy is `https://misa.mnori.com` (dokploy.mnori.com is nj1); `compose.delete` with `deleteVolumes` leaves the network and the Traefik certificate behind

`측정 2026-10-21 · Dokploy v0.30.8 on misa (Ubuntu 24.04, Docker swarm) · Traefik v3.6.7 · user in the docker group, sudo needs a password`

**증상:** removing a stack that still runs on misa (here a WordPress compose) through `https://dokploy.mnori.com/api` cannot work:
that panel has been nj1's since the 2026-10-12 move (OPS-517) and does not list misa's projects. misa still runs its own
Dokploy for the stacks left there, with its panel at `https://misa.mnori.com` (Traefik `dynamic/dokploy.yml`). The
same `~/.config/dokploy/misa.key` authenticates on both panels, so a call to the wrong host succeeds and lists nj1.

- `POST https://misa.mnori.com/api/compose.delete {"composeId", "deleteVolumes": true}` removed the containers, both
  named volumes, `/etc/dokploy/compose/<appName>` and `/etc/dokploy/logs/<appName>`. It left the compose's bridge
  network (`docker network rm <appName>`), the now unused images, and the router's Let's Encrypt certificate (key
  included) in `/etc/dokploy/traefik/dynamic/acme.json`. `project.remove {"projectId"}` then removes the empty project.
- Dokploy's `/etc/dokploy/monitoring/<container>` folders of long-deleted containers also stay (root-owned).
- Root-owned files under `/etc/dokploy` can be changed without sudo through a throwaway container
  (`docker run --rm -v /etc/dokploy/traefik/dynamic:/t alpine …`). acme.json stays mode 600 if you overwrite it with
  `cat new > acme.json` instead of `mv`.

**해결:** call misa's API at `misa.mnori.com`. After `compose.delete`, remove the network and images, then drop the
certificate with jq (`with_entries(.value.Certificates |= map(select(.domain.main != "<host>")))`, keep a copy) and
`docker restart dokploy-traefik`; Traefik serves every other host again within 6 s. A whole-file cleanup that keeps
only certificates whose domain is in a live router (`Host(...)` from container labels plus the file provider) cut
misa's acme.json from 47 certificates to 7 with every routed host still on a valid certificate.

## OPS-572 — Moving a site between Cloudflare Tunnels by re-pointing its proxied CNAME: the apex kept reaching the old tunnel for about 2 minutes, `www` switched at once; a tunnel aimed straight at the container also drops Traefik's HTTP→HTTPS redirect

`측정 2026-10-21 · Cloudflare free zone · remotely managed tunnel (cloudflared 2026.10.1 as a Dokploy app) · Dokploy v0.30.8 · Next.js 14 (nixpacks)`

**증상:** a site ran behind tunnel A (locally managed, ingress `hostname → http://localhost:80`, i.e. Traefik). A new tunnel B was created with ingress `hostname → http://<dokploy-appName>:3000` and its connector deployed as a Dokploy app on the new host. Both CNAMEs (`example.com`, `www.example.com`) were PATCHed to `<B>.cfargotunnel.com` (still proxied). Each build has its own Next.js build id, so every response shows which host answered:

| Time after PATCH | `example.com` (apex, flattened) | `www.example.com` |
|---|---|---|
| ~30 s | 3 of 5 old | — |
| ~90 s | 11 of 20 old | 0 of 20 old |
| ~110 s | 0 of 20 old | 0 of 20 old |

Afterwards `http://example.com/` answered `200` over plain HTTP. Before, the request went through Traefik's `web` entrypoint and its `redirect-to-https` middleware; a tunnel pointed directly at the container skips Traefik, and the zone had `always_use_https: off`.

Separately: after a whole Dokploy install had been moved to another host (OPS-410), the source host's Dokploy kept running with the old database and all its services. Its containers (here a full copy of the site, 1.16 GB image) went on running for 9 days with no traffic, and the same API key still worked on its local panel (`curl http://localhost:3000/api/...` on that host).

**해결:** keep the old origin running until a few dozen requests to the apex all come from the new one (a per-build marker in the response is the easiest check), then stop it. Test tunnel B first through a temporary proxied name in another zone (`<x>.mnori.com` → B, added to B's ingress), and remove it afterwards. Turn on `PATCH /zones/<id>/settings/always_use_https {"value":"on"}` when the tunnel bypasses the proxy that used to redirect; `http://` then answers `301`. After a Dokploy host move, list services on the source host and remove leftovers with `application.delete` on the source's own panel (it removes the service, the Traefik file and the code directory), then `docker image rm`.

## OPS-573 — React Native `<Text>` on Android breaks Korean between any two syllables (`봐` / `요.`); U+2060 WORD JOINER between the characters of each word makes it break only at spaces

`측정 2026-10-21 · React Native 0.88 (Expo SDK 58, release APK, Hermes) · Android 17 on Pixel 7 Pro · Pretendard (embedded TTF)`

**증상:** a centred heading `무난한 날이에요. 하던 일 하나만 마무리해 봐요.` (21 px, two lines at 1440 px screen width) wrapped as `… 마무리해 봐` / `요.` — the line broke inside the word `봐요`, leaving one syllable alone. The web build of the same component does not do this, because it sets CSS `word-break: keep-all` (react-native-web passes it through). Android's `Text` has no keep-all equivalent among RN's props: `textBreakStrategy` (`simple` / `highQuality` / `balanced`) chooses how lines are balanced, not where Korean may break, and iOS-only `lineBreakStrategyIOS="hangul-word"` does nothing on Android.

**해결:** on Android only, rewrite string children before rendering: join the characters of every run of two or more non-space characters with U+2060 (WORD JOINER):

```ts
const glue = (s: string) => s.replace(/\S{2,}/g, (w) => Array.from(w).join('⁠'));
```

Same heading after the change: `… 마무리해` / `봐요.` — breaks only at spaces. U+2060 drew nothing visible with Pretendard (no tofu, no extra width seen in the screenshot). `Array.from` keeps surrogate pairs (emoji) whole. Apply it to string children only; nested `<Text>` elements handle their own strings. The same joiner trick for Godot is GDT-104.

## OPS-574 — Connecting GitLab.com to a fresh Dokploy without the panel UI: `gitlab.create` needs `authId`, and the OAuth callback answers 500 unless the authorize `redirect_uri` carries `?gitlabId=`

`측정 2026-10-21 · Dokploy v0.30.8 (nj2) · GitLab.com OAuth application (user settings) · Chrome-family browser driven by Playwright`

**증상:** a second Dokploy install had no git provider. With a new GitLab OAuth app (callback `https://<panel>/api/providers/gitlab/callback`, scopes `api read_user read_repository`, not confidential — same as the first install's app) and `gitlab.create`, the browser authorize step landed on the callback with `Internal Server Error`, and `gitProvider.getAll` kept `isConfigured: false`.

- `gitlab.create` rejects a body without `authId` (and `name`, `gitlabUrl`). `authId` is the Dokploy user id (`user.get` → `userId`). It returns `null`; read the new `gitlabId` from `gitProvider.getAll`.
- The callback (`pages/api/providers/gitlab/callback.ts`) reads `gitlabId` from the query, not `state`, and exchanges the code with `redirect_uri = <redirectUri>?gitlabId=<id>`. Authorize with exactly that: `https://gitlab.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=<appId>&redirect_uri=<callback>?gitlabId=<id>&response_type=code&scope=api read_user read_repository`. GitLab accepts the extra query on the registered URI; the provider turned `isConfigured: true` at once.
- GitLab shows the app secret only on the page right after 「Save application」. If the script misses it, 「Renew secret」 on the app page shows a new one (no confirmation dialog). The 「Authorize」 button sits under an overlay for a few seconds; `dispatchEvent('click')` works where `click()` times out.
- An existing project hook pointing at the old panel can be re-pointed with `PUT /projects/:id/hooks/:hook_id url=https://<panel>/api/deploy/<application.refreshToken>`; `POST …/hooks/:id/test/push_events` started a deploy on the new panel within 8 s, and a real commit did too.

**해결:** create the provider by API with `authId`, authorize with the `?gitlabId=` redirect, then `application.saveGitlabProvider` (OPS-191) and `autoDeploy: true`. To check what a container actually received without docker access on the host, use `docker.getContainersByAppNameMatch?appName=<appName>` and `docker.getConfig?containerId=<id>` (its `Config.Env`); compare values, do not print them.

## OPS-575 — Rotating a Gmail app password by script: every launch re-asks the passkey, the trash button revokes at once with no confirmation, and a revoked password drops the SMTP connection instead of answering 535

`측정 2026-10-21 · myaccount.google.com/apppasswords (ko UI) · Chrome for Testing (ms-playwright chromium-1243) headed off-screen on the main Mac, copy of ~/.gstack/chromium-profile · smtplib on Ubuntu (Python 3.14)`

**증상:** the app-password page needs a fresh re-auth. Brave on the Air with a copy of `~/kc-test/profile` stopped at 「패스키를 사용하여 로그인을 완료합니다」 (OPS-447). Chrome for Testing on the main Mac passed the same challenge on its own in 3 of 4 launches within about 60 s; once it went to `/challenge/pk/error` 「블루투스가 켜져 있고 기기가 서로 가까이에 있는지 확인하세요」 and the next launch passed again. Each new launch asked again.

- Create: fill the textbox named 「앱 이름」, click 「만들기」; the dialog shows the password as four groups of four lowercase letters (`/[a-z]{4}\s[a-z]{4}\s[a-z]{4}\s[a-z]{4}/`); write it straight to a mode-600 file.
- Revoke: each row's button is `button[aria-label="앱 비밀번호 취소"]` (same label on every row, so pick it by the row's name). One click deleted the password with **no confirmation dialog**.
- After revocation, `smtplib.SMTP_SSL("smtp.gmail.com", 465).login(user, old)` raised `SMTPServerDisconnected: Connection unexpectedly closed` twice, not `535`; the new password logged in with `235`.

**해결:** order the rotation so nothing breaks: create the new password, prove it with an SMTP `login()` (no send) from the server that will use it, put it in the app's environment, deploy, confirm the container's env holds it (OPS-574), and only then revoke the old one. Re-run the browser step if the passkey challenge errors once. Treat a disconnect on `login()` with the old password as "rejected".

## OPS-576 — Playwright `addScriptTag` for axe-core fails on a site with an enforced CSP; `bypassCSP: true` on the context fixes it, and a page with only a manifest plus a small network-first service worker gets Brave's install offer in about 0.2 s

`측정 2026-10-21 · Brave 1.96 (Chromium 154) headless on the Air · playwright-core · Next.js 16.3 production build on localhost`

**증상:** an accessibility check that injected axe with `page.addScriptTag({ url: 'https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/axe-core/4.10.2/axe.min.js' })` threw at once: `page.addScriptTag: Loading the script '…axe.min.js' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' …"`. The site's enforced CSP (sent by Next `headers()` on every path, including a local `next start`) blocks the CDN. The run aborts on the first page, so every later check is skipped.

Same session, same browser: a PWA install check in `chromium.launchPersistentContext(<temp dir>, { executablePath: Brave, headless: true, isMobile: true, userAgent: <Android Chrome UA> })` (OPS-364) got `beforeinstallprompt` at 209 ms and 272 ms after navigation start on a cleared profile, `Page.getInstallabilityErrors` → `[]`, `Page.getAppManifest` → no errors, for a manifest with `id`, same-origin `start_url`/`scope`, 192/512/maskable icons, four `form_factor: "narrow"` 1080×1920 WebP screenshots, and a 40-line service worker (network-first navigations with `navigationPreload`, cached offline page only). With `ctx.setOffline(true)` the worker served the offline page for an uncached URL.

**해결:** create the test contexts with `browser.newContext({ bypassCSP: true, … })` when the test injects its own scripts; keep the real CSP (no bypass) in the context that checks the service worker and the install offer, since those are what the CSP must allow (`worker-src 'self'`, `manifest-src 'self'`).
