## OPS-577 — A test that reads free disk space fails on the shared Air (92 % full); a 64 MB RAM disk made with `hdiutil`/`diskutil` without sudo gives the test its own volume

`측정 2026-10-22 · MacBookAir10,1 macOS · APFS data volume 228 GiB, 17 GiB free · Node 26 statfsSync · hdiutil/diskutil (no sudo)`

**증상:** a browser test of an operator dashboard expected "할 일이 없어요" and timed out on `.todo-clear`. The dashboard was right: it warns below 10 % free disk, measured with `statfsSync(dbPath)`, and the Air's data volume, shared by every session, had 17 GiB of 228 GiB free (`df -h ~` → 92 %). Deleting one's own leftovers (about 1 GB) does not bring it under the line, and other sessions' files are not ours to delete. The same test had also failed on "아직 백업이 없어요" because a fresh checkout has no backup files.

**사실:**
- `DEV=$(hdiutil attach -nomount ram://131072 | awk '{print $1}')` (512-byte sectors, so 64 MB) then `diskutil erasevolume HFS+ <name> $DEV` mounts `/Volumes/<name>` as the user, no sudo. hdiutil prints a deprecation warning for `-nomount` (it suggests `diskutil image attach --noMount`) but works.
- A SQLite database at `DB_PATH=/Volumes/<name>/x.sqlite` makes `statfsSync` report that volume (nearly all free), so a disk check passes without touching the real disk or the app's rule.
- Empty files with fresh mtimes in the folders the status code scans (here `hourly/*.sqlite`, `offsite/hourly/*.sqlite.enc`, …, plus the pull marker) stand in for a production backup set.
- `hdiutil detach $DEV` frees the memory at the end.

**해결:** for tests whose result depends on the machine's free space or files, give them a RAM disk of their own instead of loosening the check or cleaning someone else's files. Keep the disk warning itself: on the Air it is true.

## OPS-578 — Naver without a Naver sign-in: IndexNow to `searchadvisor.naver.com/indexnow` takes 4,503 URLs at once; `api.indexnow.org` refuses a brand-new key for about 20 minutes

`측정 2026-10-22 · IndexNow protocol, JSON POST · key file at the site root · Astro site behind a Cloudflare Worker`

**증상:** a site had to be registered with Naver search, but no browser profile on the Air held a Naver sign-in and the password is the owner's. Naver Search Advisor (ownership, sitemap upload, reports) cannot be used without it.

**사실:**
- Naver accepts IndexNow (listed on indexnow.org since 2023). With the key served as `https://<host>/<key>.txt` (body = the key), `POST https://searchadvisor.naver.com/indexnow` with `{ host, key, keyLocation, urlList }` answered `200` (empty body) for 4,503 URLs in one request (the limit is 10,000).
- The same body to `https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow` a few minutes after the key file went live answered `403 {"errorCode":"SiteVerificationNotCompleted","message":"Site Verification is not completed. Please wait for some time for the verification to complete and try again."}`; about 20 minutes later it answered `200` for all 4,503.
- A later single-URL request to Naver with only the site root `https://<host>/` answered `422 Invalid urls`, while a single other page answered `200`. Cause not established (possibly a recent duplicate); the root had been in the accepted batch.
- Korean paths are sent percent-encoded exactly as the sitemap lists them (`encodeURI`).

**해결:** when a console needs a sign-in nobody can give, push the URLs with IndexNow: one key file, one script that reads the live sitemap and posts it to both endpoints. Retry `api.indexnow.org` after half an hour if it says the site is not verified yet. Search Advisor's reports still need the sign-in.

## OPS-579 — After renaming a project folder: `uv run` fails with "Failed to spawn" (venv shebangs keep the old path) and Gradle refuses to configure (cached autolinking paths)

`측정 2026-10-21 · uv 0.12.10 (Air, macOS) · Gradle 9.4.1 · Expo SDK 58 / React Native 0.88 · macOS (Mac)`

**증상:** a project folder was renamed with `mv ~/work/<old> ~/work/<new>`; nothing else changed.

- Python (uv): `uv sync -q` exited without error, and afterwards `.venv/bin/uvicorn` still started with
  `#!/Users/<user>/work/<old>/server/.venv/bin/python`. `uv run pytest` then printed
  `error: Failed to spawn: `pytest`` / `Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`. Every console
  script in the venv (uvicorn, pytest, …) is affected; `uv run python -m …` still works, so a service started
  with `-m` can look healthy while one started by script name does not.
- Android (Gradle, Expo prebuild project): `./gradlew assembleRelease` failed at configuration with
  `Configuring project ':livekit_react-native-webrtc' without an existing directory is not allowed. The configured
  projectDirectory '/Users/<user>/work/<old>/app/node_modules/@livekit/react-native-webrtc/android' does not exist`.
  The old absolute paths are cached in the build output, not in any tracked file.

**해결:**

- uv: `rm -rf .venv && uv sync` (a fresh venv writes shebangs with the new path). `uv sync` alone does not rewrite them.
- Gradle: `rm -rf android/.gradle android/build android/app/build android/app/.cxx` and `./gradlew --stop`, then
  build again (deleting the four together fixed it; which one held the path was not isolated).
- Do both on every machine that holds a copy of the project (here the Mac and the Air test host).

## OPS-580 — Gmail app dark mode darkens an HTML mail but not its images: a logo PNG on baked-in paper shows as a pale slab

`측정 2026-10-21 · Gmail iOS app, system dark mode · Resend HTML mail with <meta name="color-scheme" content="light">`

**증상:** a transactional mail with a cream background (`#fbf7f0`) and a 205 × 54 logo PNG whose own background was
the same cream. In light mode the logo blends in. In the Gmail iOS app with the phone in dark mode, Gmail repainted
the body and table backgrounds dark and the text light, but left the PNG untouched, so the logo sat in a hard-edged
cream rectangle on a dark page. `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light">` did not stop Gmail from doing this, and
Gmail ignores `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`, so an image swap by media query does not reach it.

A transparent PNG is not the fix on its own: a black wordmark on a transparent ground becomes black on Gmail's dark
background and disappears.

**해결:** make the image carry its own ground only where the mark has one, and be transparent elsewhere. Here the
masthead became the seal mark alone (a framed stamp), with paper filled inside the frame and alpha outside it,
rendered at 3× from the SVG with Playwright `page.screenshot({ omitBackground: true })`. A stamp, badge or app-icon
style mark reads on both grounds; a bare wordmark does not. Give the new image a new URL: Gmail's image proxy and
already-sent mails keep the old one. Checked in a forced-dark render (backgrounds darkened, images untouched) at
320 and 600 px; not yet re-checked in the Gmail iOS app itself.

## OPS-581 — Testing a PWA offline on an Android phone: `cmd connectivity airplane-mode enable` leaves Wi-Fi on, so the page stays online; also the install-to-open hand-off timed on Chrome 155

`측정 2026-10-21 · Pixel 7 Pro (Android 17) · Chrome 155.0.8059.84 · adb 1.0.41 · WebAPK minted through Play`

**증상:** to see a service worker's offline page inside an installed WebAPK, a session ran `adb shell cmd connectivity airplane-mode enable` and navigated the app (over CDP, `adb forward tcp:9333 localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote`) to a URL never loaded before. The real page loaded: the airplane icon showed in the status bar, but the phone had re-enabled Wi-Fi under airplane mode (Android remembers Wi-Fi on per airplane session), and `dumpsys connectivity` still had a default network. Only after `adb shell svc wifi disable` did `dumpsys connectivity` say `Active default network: none`, `navigator.onLine` turn `false`, and the worker's offline page appear. A URL visited earlier can still load offline from the HTTP cache (the worker's `fetch()` goes through it), so test with a fresh query string.

Also measured the same day with the OPS-284 hand-off (poll `getInstalledRelatedApps()`, +3 s, `intent://…?open-app=1`), tap on 「설치」 in Chrome's sheet to `SameTaskWebApkActivity` in front: **7.5 s** and **8.0 s** (two fresh installs; `adb uninstall` of the WebAPK in between, then 「데이터 보관」 in `ClearDataDialogActivity`). With manifest `description` and four `form_factor: "narrow"` 1080×1920 WebP `screenshots`, `prompt()` opened the large sheet (`com.android.chrome:id/button_install` 「설치」, `app_name`, `app_origin`, `description`, screenshot carousel). A cold launch from the launcher showed the manifest `background_color` (#ffffff) splash with the maskable icon.

**해결:** for an offline check, `svc wifi disable` (and `svc data disable` on a SIM phone) in addition to airplane mode, confirm with `dumpsys connectivity | grep 'Active default network'`, and restore with `svc wifi enable` plus `airplane-mode disable`. An offline page that listens for `online` reloads by itself within a few seconds of Wi-Fi coming back (seen here). Strip any hand-off marker on every page load, including the standalone path: the app opens on the address the intent carried, so `?open-app=1` stays in the installed app's URL otherwise.

## OPS-582 — `ssh air '… script …'` never returns when the script starts an `ssh -fN` control master: the backgrounded master keeps the session's stdout open

`측정 2026-10-21 · OpenSSH (macOS) on the MacBook Air · Python 3.9 subprocess · Dokploy deploy helper`

**증상:** a deploy helper on the Air opened an SSH tunnel with
`subprocess.run(["ssh","-fN","-L",…,"-o","ControlMaster=yes",…],check=True)` and then called the Dokploy API.
Run from the controller as `ssh air 'zsh -lc "python3 operate.py deploy && python3 operate.py status"'`, both steps
finished and printed their output (deployment `done`), but the outer `ssh air` hung until the 300 s tool timeout.

**사실:** `ssh -fN` forks to the background after authentication but keeps the stdin/stdout/stderr it inherited.
The outer SSH session waits for every holder of its stdout to close, so it stays open as long as the tunnel lives.
Run interactively on the Air itself, nothing looks wrong.

**해결:** start the master with `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL`
(shell: `ssh -fN … </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1`), and close it when done with `ssh -S <socket> -O exit <host>`.
If a run is already stuck, the work has usually finished: check the deploy status, then stop the local task.

## OPS-583 — A "play when on screen" animation never starts if the observed element is folded with `clip-path`: IntersectionObserver measures the clipped area, so the ratio never reaches a high threshold

`측정 2026-10-21 · Brave 1.96 (Chromium 154) headless and headed on the MacBook Air · IntersectionObserver · axe-core 4.10`

**증상:** a link was shown "folded" before it was seen (`clip-path: inset(0 calc(100% - 56px) 0 0 round 999px)` on the `<a>`, leaving only a round icon) and an `IntersectionObserver` on the same `<a>` was to unfold it once it was on screen. With `threshold: 0.9` it never fired; with `threshold: [0,.25,.5,.75,1]` plus a check of `getBoundingClientRect()` it still stayed folded after being scrolled fully into view. No error anywhere: the element just stays a circle.

**사실:**
- The intersection rectangle respects the target's own `clip-path`, while the ratio is taken against the unclipped box. A target clipped to a fifth of its width reports at most about 0.2, so every higher threshold is never crossed and the callback does not run again after the first `0`.
- axe `color-contrast` fails text that is mid-reveal (`opacity`/`filter: blur` keyframes): an audit run in the first second after load flagged the number inside the animating link as serious, though it passes at rest.

**해결:** observe the outer element and put the `clip-path` on an inner wrapper (`<a><span class="face">…</span></a>`), so the observed box is never clipped; decide "on screen" from `getBoundingClientRect()` (for example three quarters of its height inside `innerHeight`). In test suites, wait for the animation class to be gone before running axe.

## OPS-584 — `spacetime publish --anonymous` makes a new identity every run: republishing to the same local database answers 403 and the old module keeps serving

`측정 2026-10-21 · SpacetimeDB CLI and standalone 2.8.0 on the MacBook Air · local test database`

**증상:** a test loop published a rebuilt Rust module with
`spacetime publish --server http://127.0.0.1:3097 <db> --bin-path … --anonymous --delete-data=always --yes`. The first run
printed `Created new database`; the second printed only
`HTTP status client error (403 Forbidden) for url (http://127.0.0.1:3097/v1/database/<db>?clear=true&host_type=Wasm)`.
The script went on, the integration tests passed, and they had tested the previous module.

**사실:** `--anonymous` signs the request with a fresh throwaway identity, so the second publish is not the owner of the
database the first one created. Nothing else in the output says the module was not replaced, and a `tail -1` of the publish
output shows only the 403 line among other noise.

**해결:** for throwaway test databases publish each build under a new database name (or reuse one non-anonymous identity),
stop the script when publish fails (`set -e`, or check for `Created new database`/`Updated database` in its output), and
confirm the module with `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/database/<db>/schema?version=9` before running tests.
Relates to OPS-381 (a stale module after a skipped rebuild looks the same from the test side).

## OPS-585 — Testing a Firebase Google sign-in after Google starts refusing the automated browser: open the real chooser, then `signInWithCustomToken` on the page's own Firebase instance; the SpacetimeDB identity is the same as a popup sign-in

`측정 2026-10-21 · Firebase JS SDK 12.17.1 (project mnori1) · Brave 1.96 headless, Playwright 1.58 on the MacBook Air · SpacetimeDB 2.8.0 standalone · Godot 4.7.2 web build`

**증상:** a browser test drove the real Google popup (copy of the Air's signed-in profile, headless). The first two runs signed in. From the third run on, picking the account in the chooser led to `accounts.google.com/v3/signin/rejected` ("로그인할 수 없음 · 브라우저 또는 앱이 안전하지 않을 수 있습니다", OPS-566), and the game waited for an account that never came. Nothing on the page reports this: the popup just stays open.

**사실:**
- A page that loads Firebase from `https://www.gstatic.com/firebasejs/<ver>/firebase-auth.js` can be signed in from the test with `page.evaluate(async t => { const A = await import('<same URL>'); await A.signInWithCustomToken(A.getAuth(), t); }, token)`. Same URL, same module instance, so `getAuth()` is the app's own `Auth` and its `onAuthStateChanged` listeners fire as for a popup sign-in.
- The custom token needs the account's uid: `POST https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<id>/accounts:lookup {"email":[...]}` with a cloud-platform token from the Admin SDK service account, then an RS256 JWT `{iss: sa, sub: sa, aud: "https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/google.identity.identitytoolkit.v1.IdentityToolkit", uid, exp: iat+3600}` signed with the account's key (Node's `crypto.sign`, no SDK). The mnori.com hub container keeps that account in `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` **base64-encoded**, not as JSON; a parser that echoes its input on failure prints the private key into the log.
- SpacetimeDB derived the same identity (`c200c3e8…`) from the custom-token session as from the earlier real popup session: the identity comes from `iss|sub`, and `sub` is the uid either way.
- Clicking the game's own Google button first and leaving the popup open keeps the click path under test (whatever the game sends before opening the popup still goes out); close the popup afterwards, which the game sees as `auth/popup-closed-by-user`.
- Two things that look like failures and are not: Chromium logs `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy policy would block the window.closed call` as console errors during every Firebase popup, and the sign-in still completes. And on `http://localhost` an MNORI-SSO page (hub cookie on `.mnori.com`) signs itself out on reload, because it cannot see the hub cookie and follows the hub; check reload persistence only on a `*.mnori.com` origin.

**해결:** keep one real-popup run for the chooser itself, and make the repeatable test mint a custom token (script reads the service account from stdin, writes the token to a 0600 file) and sign in with it as above. Filter the COOP line out of the test's console-error check.

## OPS-586 — data.go.kr file datasets download with curl and no login: two POST/GET calls, and 상가(상권)정보 carries each shop's 5-digit postal code

`측정 2026-10-21 · data.go.kr 15083033 소상공인시장진흥공단_상가(상권)정보_20260630`

**증상:** the 다운로드 button on a data.go.kr file dataset runs JavaScript (`fileDetailObj.fn_fileDataDown`), so the page holds no file link, and a captcha modal appears only after a per-file limit.

- `curl -X POST https://www.data.go.kr/tcs/dss/selectFileDataDownload.do -d "publicDataDetailPk=<uddi:… from the page's hidden input publicDataDetailPk>&publicDataPk=<dataset no>&atchFileId=&fileDetailSn=1&publicDataTyCode=PR0051"` answers JSON with `status: true` and `atchFileId` (`FILE_000000003695831`).
- `curl -L -A "Mozilla/5.0" -e "https://www.data.go.kr/data/<no>/fileData.do" "https://www.data.go.kr/cmm/cmm/fileDownload.do?atchFileId=<id>&fileDetailSn=1"` returns the file. No account, key or cookie.
- 상가(상권)정보: 352,699,739-byte zip, one UTF-8 CSV per 시도 (2026 editions have `전남광주`), 2,771,992 shops, CP949 member names. The server sent 150–200 KB/s (about 35 min); start it detached. Columns include 행정동코드·법정동코드·`신우편번호` (5-digit 기초구역번호)·경도·위도, so shops join a postal-code table directly: 492 of 2,771,992 rows had a code missing from Korea Post's 2026-10-08 edition.

**해결:** script the two calls; take `publicDataDetailPk` from the dataset page. Quarterly editions change `atchFileId`, so look it up each time.

## OPS-587 — 서울 열린데이터광장 file download: POST to datafile.seoul.go.kr with the page's own infSeq, or it answers a 183-byte "잘못된 접근" page

`측정 2026-10-21 · data.seoul.go.kr OA-15560 서울시 상권분석서비스(영역-상권)`

**증상:** `POST https://datafile.seoul.go.kr/bigfile/iot/inf/nio_download.do?&useCache=false` with `infId=OA-15560&seq=5&infSeq=2` (the `infSeq` of the API form) returned HTML: `alert('잘못된 접근입니다. 파일 목록에서 다시 선택하세요.')`, saved as a .zip.

- The page has two hidden forms; the file form `frmFile` carries its own `infSeq` (3 here), and `seq` is the number in `downloadFile('5')`. With `infId=OA-15560&seq=5&infSeq=3&seqNo=` and a Referer of the dataset page it returned the 2,123,078-byte zip. Other `seq` values answer the same 183-byte page.
- The zip's member names are CP949 (macOS `unzip` fails with "Illegal byte sequence"; decode `cp437 → cp949` in Python). The shapefile's .dbf is UTF-8 (its .cpg says so), EPSG 5181. 1,650 상권: 골목상권 1,090, 전통시장 305, 발달상권 249, 관광특구 6, each tagged with one 행정동.

**해결:** read `infSeq` from `<form name="frmFile">`, `seq` from the `downloadFile` call, and check the file is a zip before using it.

## OPS-588 — Taking customer payments and paying suppliers by Zelle, Venmo or Stripe: the terms that bite a small US merchant (Chase "not intended for the purchase of goods from retailers", BoA new-recipient caps, Venmo 180-day holds, stored-value restrictions)

`측정 2026-10-21 · Chase Zelle Service Agreement (last updated 10/16/2026) · BoA Online Banking Service Agreement (effective 2026-10-19) · Venmo User Agreement (effective 2026-08-24) · Stripe Restricted Businesses (2026-09-22)`

**증상:** a startup plans to collect consumer orders by Zelle/Venmo/card and pay ~20 suppliers weekly by Zelle, and assumes the published daily limits are the only constraint.

**사실:**
- Chase Zelle terms: "The Service is not intended, and should not be used, for the purchase of goods from retailers, merchants, or the like". Business Banking send limits are per-transaction tiers set dynamically: $1,000 / $5,000 / $7,500 / $15,000 per day; "We do not currently limit the dollar amount you may receive". Chase's deposit agreement lets it debit funds back when the sending bank says a payment was "procured by fraud, scam or financial exploitation", "even if you have already withdrawn the funds".
- Bank of America Zelle (consumer or small business accounts): no receiving limit; send limits $2,000/day (≤15 days enrolled), $4,000 (16–30), $8,000 (31–60), $15,000 (60+), each "/ 20 transactions"; monthly $100,000 / 120 transactions; recipients not enrolled in Zelle $2,000/day and newly added recipients $4,000/day for the first 5 days. "NEITHER WE NOR ZELLE OFFER PURCHASE PROTECTION FOR AUTHORIZED PAYMENTS."
- Reg E covers only consumer accounts (12 CFR 1005.2(b)(1) "primarily for personal, family, or household purposes"); a business account has no Reg E error-resolution rights.
- No Zelle API for reconciling incoming payments was found; J.P. Morgan's Zelle Disbursements API only sends.
- Venmo business profile: 1.9% + $0.10 per payment received; risk-based holds "may remain in place for up to 180 days"; unverified profiles $2,499.99/week sending. Purchase Protection lets buyers dispute within 180 days; the seller pays the payment plus fees on a loss. Excluded from Purchase Protection: "stored value items such as gift cards and pre-paid cards". The PayPal AUP Venmo links needs pre-approval for "the sale of stored value cards".
- Stripe: stored value is *restricted*, not prohibited: "Seller-maintained stored value or credits may be subject to limits." Payment facilitation is restricted too, including "receiving settlement proceeds for goods or services that you did not provide". Stripe Billing credits must not be used to "sell gift cards" or "offer stored value". Dispute fee $15, plus a $15 counter fee that is refunded only if you win. Stripe Tax: 0.5% per transaction where registered (no-code).

**해결:** pay suppliers by ACH/bill pay instead of Zelle, or enroll the account and every recipient well before the first payout. Do not route consumer purchases through a Chase Zelle account. Put an order code in every Zelle memo and match by hand. Ask Stripe and PayPal/Venmo in writing before selling a prepaid balance through them.

## OPS-589 — FreePD.com is closed (2026-10-21); OpenGameArt's CC0 filter and Kenney are the working CC0 music sources

`측정 2026-10-21 · freepd.com, opengameart.org`

**증상:** FreePD's main page shows "Site Closed" and its category pages (for example `upbeat.php`)
return 404, so the long-standing public-domain music library is no longer usable for a game build.

**해결:** search OpenGameArt with the license filter set to CC0 only and record the author and URL per
file (authors used for an arcade game: Holizna, Fupi, G_P, Archonic, Robin Lamb). Kenney's audio packs
are CC0 for effects. Check each OpenGameArt entry's license line on the page itself; the site mixes
CC0, CC-BY and GPL entries in one listing.

## OPS-590 — How US food marketplaces structure money (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Too Good To Go): shop is always the seller, collection is "agent" wording or Stripe Connect, stored value sits in a subsidiary or bank-group issuer, payouts are ACH weekly

`측정 2026-10-21 · DoorDash Merchant ToS 2026-04-27, Marketplace Addendum 2025-11-03 · Uber Eats Merchant Terms 6/2/2026, Uber ToU 10/12/2026, Uber Cash Purchase Agreement 3/6/2023 · Grubhub ToU 2024-12-17, 10-K FY2020 · TGTG Store Terms v3.0 2025-06-16`

**증상:** a small marketplace founder assumes it should be merchant of record, collect into its own account and pay shops by Zelle, and that a prepaid balance is a simple ledger.

**사실:**
- None is merchant of record for the shop's goods: DoorDash "Merchant is the seller, retailer, and supplier"; Uber "The Merchant is the “merchant”, “retailer”, or “seller”"; TGTG "TGTG is only an intermediary … not a party to the sale"; Grubhub books revenue net "Because we act as an agent of the merchant".
- Collection: Uber (Portier, LLC) is the shop's "limited payment collection agent", and its consumer terms say payment to Uber "shall be considered the same as payment made directly by you to the Third-Party Provider"; grocery funds sit in an FBO account "for the benefit of the Merchant". TGTG holds a "power of attorney to receive payments … in full discharge". DoorDash instead makes each shop sign the Stripe Connected Account Agreement and "by funding the Merchant’s account with the Payment Processor, DoorDash will discharge its payment obligations". Grubhub (2020 10-K) pooled diner money in "a non-interest bearing operating bank account that is used to fund daily operations".
- None of the 10-Ks discloses a US money-transmitter licence; Uber's licences are NL/UK/Mexico only; DoorDash names only a Finnish e-money licence. Stripe Payments Company lists NJ DOBI among its licensing regulators.
- Stored value: DoorDash gift cards and Purchased Credits are issued by DoorDash Giftcards LLC (Virginia), "closed-loop", no expiry, no cash-out, max $2,000 loaded per account per day and $10,000 bought per day. Uber Cash gift cards are "issued directly to you by" TBBK Card Services, Inc. (South Dakota), with auto-refill below $10. Grubhub Holdings Inc. issues its own gift cards (CashStar distributes), $1,000 per card, $2,000 per person per day. TGTG US has none.
- Payouts: DoorDash weekly on a fixed weekday (day changes need 10 days' notice), daily opt-in; Uber "weekly by direct deposit"; Grubhub weekly / twice a week / every two weeks, bank linked via Plaid; TGTG monthly on the 20th of the following month. None pays by Zelle.
- Refund cost: DoorDash and Uber charge the merchant for merchant-caused problems ("missing and incorrect Orders"; "Substandard Items") by payout deduction; DoorDash gives merchants 14 days to dispute.
- Sales tax: DoorDash and Uber collect from customers and remit as marketplace facilitator where required; Uber lists New Jersey from 4/1/2021.

**해결:** keep the shop as seller in writing, pair shop-side "collection agent" wording with customer-side "payment discharges your debt to the shop" wording, move shop money through a licensed processor's connected accounts rather than your own account, pay weekly by ACH, write the refund-cost split into the shop contract, and treat a prepaid balance as a licensing question (subsidiary issuer with caps, or a bank-partner issuer) before launch.

## OPS-591 — How Amazon, Etsy, Shopify and Starbucks let a balance pay sellers: a separate issuer LLC plus a licensed or agent collector, Shopify bans cross-merchant gift cards, and the caps cluster at $2,000

`측정 2026-10-21 · Amazon Balance & Gift Card Terms, BSA (US), Conditions of Use 2026-08-14 · Etsy Payments Policy 2026-07-31, Etsy US Gift Card Terms (cards after 2024-05-01) · Shopify ToS 2026-10-20, Gift Card & Store Credit Service Terms 2024-01-24 · Starbucks Card Terms 2023-07-24 · 10-Ks FY2025 · NJ statutes through P.L.2026 c.50`

**증상:** a small marketplace wants one pre-loaded, Starbucks-style balance that customers can spend at many independent shops. It assumes the closed-loop exemption ("redeemable by the issuer in goods or services") covers it.

**사실:**
- Starbucks sells almost everything its card buys. "We issue the Starbucks Card", and the value is "a prepayment for the goods and services of participating stores". Limits: "not more than $500 in value", "$2,000 ... in a single day", "$10,000 on any given day". No expiry and no fees. FY2025 breakage was $200.4M (company stores) plus $22.0M (licensed stores), and the card liability was $1,751.7M, held as deferred revenue, not segregated.
- Amazon: "Amazon.com Gift Cards are issued by ACI Gift Cards LLC" (not Amazon.com Services LLC). For sellers: "Amazon Payments, Inc. may process the redemption of the portion of your Amazon.com Balance used to purchase goods and services sold by third parties". Amazon Payments, Inc. is the seller's agent ("buyers satisfy their obligations to you ... when we receive the Sales Proceeds") and is a licensed money transmitter with an NJ licence listed. Payout is "bi-weekly (14 day)". Gift card liability was $5.6B at 2025-12-31.
- Etsy: "Etsy Gifting, LLC is the sole card issuer and sole obligor ... Etsy, Inc. is neither the Card Issuer nor an obligor" (a "novation"). The card is spendable at any shop on Etsy Payments, $25–$2,000 per card, $10,000 per account, no expiry, "may be subject to escheat". "Shop-Specific Gift Certificates are not permitted on Etsy." Etsy, Inc. is each seller's collection agent, and the 10-K names no US money transmitter licence.
- Shopify: merchant gift cards must be "closed-loop (i.e., the Gift Card may only be used at your locations for purchase of goods and services from you and no other merchant or company)", with redemption capped at "$2,000 during any one day". Shopify "does not provide or issue Gift Cards". Its only cross-merchant value, Shop Cash, is unpurchased: "has no cash value ... only promotional", and it expires after 180 days (US). The money itself moves through Stripe Payments Company as the merchant's agent "for the limited purpose of directing, receiving, holding and settling funds".
- The $2,000 figure matches FinCEN: "not a prepaid program if ... closed loop prepaid access to funds not to exceed $2,000 maximum value ... on any day" (31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(4)(iii)(A)). That this is why the companies chose it is an inference; none of them says so.
- New Jersey:
  - Any collector that "collects payment ... and transmits that payment to the marketplace seller" is a marketplace facilitator and owes NJ sales tax (N.J.S.A. 54:32B-3.6).
  - Stored value cards are presumed abandoned after 5 years without activity, and 60% of the value escheats.
  - Issuers that sold "$250,000 or less" in the past year are exempt.
  - Funds "shall not expire".
  - A balance under $5 must be refunded in cash on request, except for cards usable at unaffiliated merchants (N.J.S.A. 46:30B-42.1).

**해결:** do not launch a purchased multi-shop balance as a plain ledger. Either be the seller of record for what the balance buys (Starbucks), or put the balance in a separate issuer entity and have a licensed processor or agent redeem it for the shops (Amazon, Etsy). Start with unpurchased, expiring promotional credit (Shop Cash style). Cap at or below $2,000 a day, and plan for NJ escheat and marketplace-facilitator tax from day one.

## OPS-592 — How Instacart, Weee!, Gopuff and HungryPanda handle seller of record, collection and balances: only the first-party sellers run a purchased balance; the marketplace agent (HungryPanda) parks refunds in a withdrawable balance

`측정 2026-10-21 · Instacart ToS 2026-05-07, Gift Card & Credit terms, MPF Tax Policy 2026-06-26, 10-K FY2025 · Weee! ToS 2026-09-08 · Gopuff ToS 2024-12-13 · HungryPanda US User Terms eff. 2023-11-20 · NYC DCWP release 2026-04-08`

**증상:** a small multi-shop food marketplace wants to collect all customer money, sell a pre-loaded balance and pay shops itself, and looks to grocery and Asian-community delivery apps for a template.

**사실:**
- Instacart: "We don't sell the goods ourselves"; "The Retailer ... is the seller of the goods to you and the merchant of record ... Instacart does not take title". The consumer terms call Instacart the customer's agent for ordering; the 10-K calls it "an agent of the retailer in the sale of goods". The retailer is paid at its own till: Instacart "remits the purchase value of the related goods to the retailer at the retailers' point-of-sale" with issuer-supplied shopper cards; retailer fees are invoiced, "due immediately to 45 days". Gift cards: "Maplebear Inc. d/b/a Instacart is the Gift Card issuer and sole obligor", spendable across retailers, no expiry, no reload, no cash-out. Credits are capped at "$1,500 total or more than $2,000 added in a single day". Instacart is marketplace facilitator for sales tax. The 10-K has no money-transmitter disclosure.
- Weee!: sells its own stock and runs a Marketplace of "Sellers" (seller agreement not public; payout terms not public; "Only pay commission on what you sell"). Two balances: WeeeCash ("the balance you purchase from Weee! with money and the balance for refunds", "refundable ... and does not expire") and WeeePoints (awarded, expire 90 days after issue from 2026-09-08; bonus points for loading WeeeCash, up to 4%). Both "may only be used to purchase eligible goods and services provided by Weee!" and cannot be transferred. Refund window 48 h by default; Weee! decides.
- Gopuff (GoBrands, Inc.): first-party seller ("Gopuff does sell products ..."), card charged by "Gopuff's third party payment processor". GoCash = gift-card value (never expires) plus refund value (may expire); "not refundable, returnable, or redeemable for cash except where required by law", app-only, not transferable.
- HungryPanda US INC: merchants are the sellers ("A contract to supply the items on your Order forms between you and the merchant"); "Merchants who entered agreements with us authorized us to accept payment on their behalf". "All refunds will be automatically added to the balance of your HungryPanda account"; the global FAQ says the balance can be withdrawn to the payment account in "1-7 business days". No US gift-card terms. NYC DCWP settled for "more than $875,000" over fee-cap overcharges labeled "promotion deductions".
- None of the four publishes a payout by Zelle; Instacart and Weee! name only an unnamed "payment processor". NMLS licence status could not be checked (AGT-161).

**해결:** a purchased balance is only clean when the issuer is also the seller of what it buys (Weee!, Gopuff). If shops stay the seller, copy HungryPanda's "authorized us to accept payment on their behalf" clause plus a customer-side discharge sentence, publish the shop fee schedule, and keep refunds as card refunds or non-cash promotional credit rather than a withdrawable balance until a licensed issuer or counsel approves.

## OPS-593 — Single-pass ffmpeg `loudnorm` leaves 1–4 LU spread across 1–3 s speech clips; measure with `ebur128` and apply a gain

`측정 2026-10-21 · ffmpeg loudnorm I=-16 · Edge TTS clips of 1–3 s in three voices`

**증상:** after single-pass `loudnorm` to −16 LUFS, short clips measured −17 to −20 LUFS for one voice
(Jenny) and about −16 for another (Nanami), so answers changed volume between languages.

**해결:** measure each clip with `ebur128` (or the first `loudnorm` pass in JSON) and apply a plain
`volume` gain to the target; that brought every clip within ±1 LU. See OPS-174 for the two-pass
fallback trap.

## OPS-594 — SpacetimeDB 2.8 dev server: get a fixed publishing identity with `POST /v1/identity` + `spacetime login --token`, and keep its CLI config outside any tree you `rsync --delete`

`측정 2026-10-21 · SpacetimeDB CLI and standalone 2.8.0 on the MacBook Air · local database on its own port`

**증상:** OPS-584 says not to publish with `--anonymous`, but the 2.8 CLI has no option to log in to a
self-hosted standalone server. A project kept the CLI config inside its working tree on the test host; the next
`rsync -az --delete ./ air:work/<project>/` from the dev machine removed it, the publishing identity was gone, and
the next publish to the project's own database could only answer 403 (not the owner). The database had to be wiped
and recreated.

**사실:**
- `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/identity` returns `{"identity": …, "token": …}` from that server.
  `spacetime --config-path <dir>/cli.toml login --token <token>` stores it; every later
  `spacetime --config-path <dir>/cli.toml publish --server http://127.0.0.1:<port> …` is the same owner and prints
  `Updated database`.
- `spacetime call`, the HTTP `/v1/database/<db>/call/<reducer>` and `spacetime sql` run `client_connected` **and**
  `client_disconnected` once per invocation, each with a new connection id (one `SELECT` on a fresh production
  database created a player row for the CLI identity). A reducer that sets `online = false` on
  disconnect marks a player who is connected from the game offline whenever someone calls a reducer for them over
  HTTP; count live connections (a private presence table keyed by connection id) instead of a boolean.

**해결:** put the CLI config in the host's home (`~/.config/<project>-stdb/cli.toml`), not in the synced tree, and add
every directory the host's server writes (`.stdb-data`, logs) to the rsync excludes. A script that starts the server
when the port is free, mints the token once when the config is missing and then publishes makes the whole thing one
command (`trade/scripts/dev-server.sh`).

## OPS-595 — Real-time action over SpacetimeDB 2.8 without a server tick: rollback on an input log. Two clients with 90/160 ms injected lag ended on identical state checksums

`측정 2026-10-21 · SpacetimeDB 2.8.0 standalone on the Air (M1) · Rust module · Godot 4.7.2 GDScript clients (v2.bsatn, headless) · 30 Hz integer simulation`

**증상:** a 2–4 player real-time platformer needed instant response and authoritative shared state.
A scheduled per-tick reducer grows the commit log without bound (OPS-316) and per-move public writes
saturate a core (OPS-143); server-side physics also means every move waits a round trip.

The design that worked:

- The server never steps the game. Tables: `round` (stage, seed, `start_micros` of tick 0) and a
  public `input` log, one row per **change** of a player's buttons: `(round_id, slot, tick, bits)`.
  Clients subscribe `SELECT * FROM input WHERE round_id = N`.
- Every client runs the same integer simulation (positions in 1/1000 tile, seeded LCG, no floats)
  from tick 0. The tick to be at comes from the server clock (`ReducerResult` timestamp, lowest-RTT
  sample of a few `ping` reducer calls).
- Missing inputs are predicted ("still holding what they held"). A row for a tick already simulated
  restores the snapshot saved before that tick and replays to now in the same frame. Snapshots are six
  `PackedInt32Array.duplicate()` calls per tick, kept for 12 s.
- `send_input` clamps the tick to `[server_tick - 45, server_tick + 20]` and keeps each slot strictly
  increasing, so rollback depth is bounded. A client treats its **own** inputs as predictions until
  their row comes back (FIFO), and replays if the server re-stamped one.
- A leaving player gets a server-written row with a "bot" bit at `server_tick + 3`; the simulation
  turns that runner into a deterministic bot from that tick on every client.

Measured with two headless clients through the real server, random inputs every 9 ticks, 160 ms and
90 ms of extra delay applied to every incoming row: 20 and 19 rollbacks, deepest 6 ticks (200 ms),
and the snapshot checksums at ticks 900 and 1000 were identical on both clients. An idle server
writes nothing: there is no scheduled reducer except a 60 s sweep that returns without writing when
there is nothing to delete.

**해결:** for small-room real-time games on SpacetimeDB, store inputs, not state, and keep the
simulation deterministic and client-side. Test determinism with two real clients and injected lag
before building anything on top. Reference: `~/work/trapout/godot/net/rollback.gd`,
`server/src/lib.rs` (`send_input`, `stamp_input`), `godot/tests/net_test.gd`.

## OPS-596 — Two game processes on one machine with the same saved SpacetimeDB token are one identity: the second "joins" the first's room as itself and the host never sees a second seat

`측정 2026-10-21 · SpacetimeDB 2.8.0 · Godot 4.7.2 headless clients on one Mac`

**증상:** a host process created a room and wrote the code to a file; a guest process read it and
called `join_room`, which returned success. The host waited for a second seat that never came. The
server log showed both websockets with the **same** identity: both processes read the token from the
same `user://….cfg` key and connected as the same player, so `join_room` saw the caller already
seated and returned `Ok` without inserting anything.

**해결:** give every test client its own token key (e.g. `--seat=h` / `--seat=g`, appended to the
storage key, as bearhunter's `Session` tag does) and check identities differ before asserting on
seats. A reducer that returns `Ok` for "already there" hides this; log the caller identity in tests.

## OPS-597 — A new *.mnori.com game on nj1: proxy `/stdb/` straight to the shared SpacetimeDB container, give the Dokploy domain `https: false`, and point the CNAME at the nj1 tunnel

`측정 2026-10-22 · Dokploy on nj1 (raw compose) · Cloudflare tunnel · SpacetimeDB 2.8 shared host spacetimedb.mnori.com · trade.mnori.com`

**증상:** a new game needed its own subdomain, a same-origin `/stdb/` websocket proxy and a database on the shared
SpacetimeDB host. Three choices were not obvious from the existing apps' docs.

**사실:**
- `spacetimedb.mnori.com` is the container `compose-copy-back-end-card-qcuwql-spacetimedb-1:3000` on nj1's
  `dokploy-network`. A game's nginx on the same network can `proxy_pass` `/stdb/` to that name directly instead of
  going back out through Cloudflare; the websocket upgrade (`/v1/database/<db>/subscribe` → 101) works.
- nj1's app routers all use Traefik's `web` entrypoint only: TLS ends at Cloudflare and the nj1 tunnel sends
  `*.mnori.com` to Traefik `:80`. A domain created with `"https": false, "certificateType": "none"` served on the
  first try. (Whether `https: true` with letsencrypt fails there was not tried.)
- Until a host has its own record, the zone's wildcard A record (unproxied) answers for it; add a proxied CNAME to
  the nj1 tunnel's `<id>.cfargotunnel.com` (the same target button and cobramission use).
- An `alpine:3.22` nginx with `nginx-mod-http-brotli` runs as `USER nginx` with `read_only`, `tmpfs /tmp` and
  `cap_drop: [ALL]` when the config is rendered into `/tmp` and started as `nginx -e stderr -c /tmp/nginx.conf`;
  without `-e stderr` it tries to open the default error log path at startup and fails.

**해결:** copy `trade/deploy/` (Dockerfile, nginx.conf.template, compose.yml, dokploy.py) and `trade/scripts/deploy.sh`,
which export, upload, build, deploy and verify in one command.

## OPS-598 — SpacetimeDB 2.8 Rust module on edition 2024: `ctx.rng().gen()` does not compile (`gen` is a reserved word); appended `#[default]` columns plus new tables migrate a live database

`측정 2026-10-22 · SpacetimeDB 2.8.0 Rust module, Rust 1.97.1, edition 2024 · standalone dev server`

**증상:** a reducer drawing a random number with `ctx.rng().gen::<f64>()` does not compile in an edition 2024 crate:
`gen` became a keyword there, and the error points at the method call, not at the edition.

**사실:**
- Write `ctx.rng().r#gen::<f64>()`, or use `gen_range(0.0f64..1.0f64)` (only the bare name `gen` is reserved);
  the latter compiled and ran in the module.
- Appending three columns with `#[default(...)]` to an existing public table and adding three new tables (one of
  them scheduled) published as `Updated database` with data kept (no `--delete-data`), as OPS-169 found for
  TypeScript modules. As there, `init` does not run again: arm new scheduled tables from `client_connected` too.
- `spacetime subscribe` keeps a connection open, so `client_connected` runs once and the CLI identity counts as
  online for as long as it runs — the way to keep a CLI-driven test captain "connected" while reducers that only act
  on online players (OPS-594: `call` and `sql` connect and disconnect per invocation) are exercised.

## OPS-599 — SpacetimeDB 2.8: the database owner can delete chosen rows with `spacetime sql "DELETE FROM t WHERE identity = 0x…"`; a row whose client is still connected comes back on its next reducer call

`측정 2026-10-22 · SpacetimeDB 2.8 CLI · self-hosted server behind a Cloudflare tunnel`

**증상:** a live game database had test players left by browser tests, mixed with a real player. Wiping the database (`publish -c`) was not an option.

`spacetime sql --server <nick> <db> "DELETE FROM player WHERE identity = 0xc200…"` run by the owner's CLI identity deletes exactly that row and prints nothing on success; a hex literal works for `Identity` columns, and `SELECT COUNT(*)` afterwards confirms it. Repeat per table that holds the identity (other tables keyed by `owner` etc.), since there are no foreign keys. One of the test identities had a live connection (a row in the module's private connection table, `online = true`) from a client that was not ours: its `player` row was back within a minute with a new `joined_at`, because the module creates a missing player on connect or on the next reducer call. Check for a live connection before deleting and leave those rows alone.

When the deletes are driven by a shell loop, run it in bash, not zsh: zsh does not split an unquoted `$IDS` or `set -- $pair`, so the loop ran once with the whole list and every statement failed with `sql parser error: Expected an expression:, found: =`, which at least deleted nothing.

**해결:** select the rows first (`SELECT identity, name FROM player WHERE …`), delete per identity in every table that holds it, then select again. To stop tests from adding rows to production, persist each test seat's token between runs (Trade's `web_play.mjs` keeps them in `~/.config/trade-web-seats.json` on the test host) so the same captains are reused.

## OPS-600 — A SpacetimeDB game listed in the MNORI portal gets 4 SQL connections every 3 minutes; a module that creates a player in `client_connected` grows by 4 rows per poll

`측정 2026-10-22 · SpacetimeDB 2.8 · mnori portal match recorder (src/lib/stdb.ts, RECORDED_GAMES) · Trade module`

**증상:** within 40 minutes of adding a game to `src/lib/games.ts` with a non-`coming-soon` status, its production `player` table gained 52 unnamed captains, four at a time with `joined_at` on whole minutes 3 minutes apart (03:42:00, 03:45:00, …).

The portal derives `RECORDED_GAMES` from the catalogue and polls `/v1/database/<id>/sql` for every playable game's `match_result` and related tables on a 3-minute background sync. Each anonymous SQL request is a new identity that runs `client_connected` and `client_disconnected` (OPS-594), so a module that inserts a player row on connect keeps one per query. The queries fail harmlessly for a game without those tables, but the connect hook has already run.

**해결:** in the game module, delete a player on its last disconnect while it is still in its starting state (default name, starting values, no inventory), and sweep such rows with no live connection from an existing scheduled reducer; a returning visitor gets the same captain back because the default name derives from the identity. After publishing that, Trade's table went from 75 rows to the 2 real ones within 30 s and stayed there across the next poll. Alternatively set `STDB_DATABASES` on the portal, but that removes the game from match recording too.

## OPS-601 — 폰 Chrome을 CDP로 붙여(`connectOverCDP`) `fullPage` 스크린샷을 찍으면 첫 화면이 화면 높이마다 반복된다. 화면 확인은 스크롤 + `adb exec-out screencap`으로 하고, 찍기 전에 전면 탭이 내 탭인지 본다

`측정 2026-10-22 · Pixel 7 Pro (Android 17) · Chrome 155.0.8059.84 · playwright-core connectOverCDP (adb forward tcp:9333 localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote, ssh -R로 Air에 연결)`

**증상:** `page.screenshot({fullPage:true})`가 1439×31,682(DPR 3.5) PNG를 오류 없이 만들었는데, 내용은 첫 화면(헤더·히어로)이 화면 높이마다 되풀이된 것이었다. OPS-453의 16,384px 한계보다 훨씬 위에서부터 반복된다. 레이아웃이 반복되는 버그처럼 보여 시간을 쓰게 된다.

- 실제 화면은 `scrollTo` 후 `adb exec-out screencap -p`로 찍어야 맞다. 화면 좌표 = CSS 좌표 × `devicePixelRatio` + 상태줄·주소창 높이(이 기기 1440×3120에서 339px). 이렇게 `adb shell input tap`으로 진짜 터치도 보낼 수 있다.
- **공유 폰 주의:** 다른 세션이 같은 폰의 Chrome에서 자기 탭을 앞으로 띄우면, 내 스크립트가 내 탭을 스크롤해도 `screencap`에는 남의 화면(게임)이 찍힌다. 남의 탭을 건드리지 않도록 페이지는 URL로 찾고(`pages().find(url 포함)`), 못 찾으면 `pages()[0]` 같은 대체 없이 멈춘다. 찍기 전에 `adb shell dumpsys activity activities | grep topResumedActivity`와 CDP의 `document.visibilityState === 'visible'`로 내 탭이 전면인지 확인한다.
- 운영 통계를 더럽히지 않으려면 QA 서버를 `adb reverse tcp:<port> tcp:<port>` + `ssh -L`로 폰에 열어 `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`로 시험한다. 끝나면 `adb forward --remove`, `adb reverse --remove`로 내 포워드만 지운다.

**해결:** 폰에서는 넘침 같은 수치는 CDP로 재고(`scrollWidth - innerWidth`), 모양은 전면 탭을 확인한 뒤 `screencap`으로 본다. `fullPage`는 폰 CDP에서 쓰지 않는다.

## OPS-602 — Google Fonts의 Pixelify Sans는 11~17px에서 숫자 2·5가 8처럼 읽힌다. 픽셀 느낌의 숫자는 DotGothic16을 쓴다

`측정 2026-10-21 · Google Fonts Pixelify Sans 500/700 · Brave 1.96(Chromium 154) headless · macOS Air`

**증상:** HD-2D 풍 게임 HUD의 수치를 Pixelify Sans로 찍었더니 21이 81, 42가 48, 5/24가 8/84, −45 G가 −48 G로 보였다. 오류나 폴백은 없고 글자 모양 자체가 그렇다. 스크린샷 검토에서 "데이터가 틀렸다"로 오해해 로직을 다시 보게 된다.

- 1·3·4는 멀쩡해서 일부 숫자만 틀린 것처럼 보인다. 390px 폰(DPR 2)과 1600px 데스크톱(DPR 1) 모두 같다.
- 같은 화면을 `DotGothic16`(Google Fonts, 픽셀풍, 한글 폴백은 Gothic A1)으로 바꾸자 모든 숫자가 바로 읽혔다.

**해결:** 점수·금액·날짜처럼 읽혀야 하는 숫자에는 Pixelify Sans를 쓰지 않는다. 픽셀풍이 필요하면 DotGothic16을 쓰고, 픽셀 폰트를 넣은 화면은 2·5·8이 섞인 값으로 캡처해 눈으로 확인한다.

## OPS-603 — Japan MOFA's overseas-resident statistics (海外在留邦人数調査統計): mofa.go.jp answers 403 to fetch tools, the same tables download from e-Stat

`측정 2026-10-22 · WebFetch / WebSearch from a Claude Code session · MOFA 2025 edition (as of 2025-10-01, published 2025-12-25)`

**증상:** a market study of Japanese residents in New York needed the MOFA tables. `https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/toko/tokei/hojin/` and the consulate site (`ny.us.emb-japan.go.jp`) returned 403 to the fetch tool, so only search snippets came back.

**사실:**
- e-Stat mirrors each edition as a file: `https://www.e-stat.go.jp/stat-search/file-download?statInfId=<id>&fileKind=2`. The 2025 edition is `statInfId=000040394912`; the 2020 edition (city trend 2016–2020) is `000032117338`; 2018 is `000031965464`; 2016 is `000031585594`. These downloaded without a block.
- Since about 2019 the yearly summary no longer prints a per-consulate table (jurisdiction total, long-term vs permanent, 日系企業拠点数). The newest per-consulate figure found was the 2018 edition; later years give only country and city-area totals (for example ニューヨーク都市圏 38,251 in 2025).
- The city-area series has a break: New York fell from 47,563 (2018) to 40,496 (2019) with no stated reason, so treat 2019 as a likely method or boundary change before drawing a trend across it.

**해결:** take country and city figures from the e-Stat file of the edition you need, cite the edition year, and mark any per-consulate number after 2018 as unverified rather than reading it from a news summary.

## OPS-604 — ffmpeg `alimiter` without `latency=1` shifts the audio by its lookahead: 131 zero samples in front, the same cut from the end, file length unchanged; a sample-exact game loop then starts silent and ends truncated

`측정 2026-10-22 · ffmpeg 9.0.2 (Homebrew, macOS 27) · alimiter attack=3 · 44.1 kHz float WAV`

**증상:** music loops mastered with `alimiter=limit=0.7:attack=3:release=60:level=false` kept their exact sample count, but a loop-seam check (step at the wrap vs the 99th percentile of neighbouring steps, GDT-282) failed at 2–3.6x on 4 of 13 loops. Decoding showed the files begin with ~130 samples of zeros and the last ~130 samples of the mix are gone. A constant 0.5 signal through the filter: output `[0, 0, 0, …]` for 131 samples, then 0.5; length identical to the input. `alimiter` buffers `attack` ms of lookahead and, by default, emits that buffer as silence first and drops the final buffer at EOF.

**해결:** `alimiter=…:latency=1` ("compensate delay", available since ffmpeg 6): the same test then returns 0.5 from sample 0 and the end is intact. Any limiter whose lookahead is not compensated shifts the whole file; check the first samples of the output, not only its length. (With the fix, all 13 loops passed the seam check at 0.1–0.7x.)

## OPS-605 — Playwright WebKit lets a page's `fetch` PUT past `context.route`; the same handler catches it in Chromium

`측정 2026-10-22 · playwright-core 1.64.1 (bundled WebKit) · MacBook Air M1, macOS 27 · page served from a local Node http server`

**증상:** a settings test asserted that a switch saves the account preference with `fetch('/api/me/prefs', { method: 'PUT', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body })`. The context had two handlers: `context.route('**/api/me', …fulfill)` and, registered after it, `context.route('**/api/me/prefs', route => { prefs = route.request().postDataJSON(); route.fulfill(…) })`. In Brave (Chromium) the second handler ran. In WebKit it never ran, three runs of three, at the code before and after an unrelated change: `page.on('request')` showed `PUT …/api/me/prefs {"scripture":"show"}`, and the request reached the real server (404 in the console). The GET to `/api/me` in the same page was fulfilled by its handler. Waiting longer (up to 2 s) changed nothing, so it is not timing.

**해결:** when a test only needs to know what the page sent, read it from the request event instead of a route handler — `page.on('request', r => { if (r.method() === 'PUT' && r.url().endsWith('/api/me/prefs')) prefs = r.postDataJSON(); })` — which works in both engines. Keep the route if the page needs a fake answer, but do not let a WebKit test depend on it being called for a body-carrying `fetch`.

## OPS-606 — One Next.js server answering two hostnames makes two PWAs, but the file-based `app/manifest.ts` gives both the same manifest: the second site installs under the first one's name

`측정 2026-10-22 · Next.js 16.3.2 (next build / next start) · Brave 1.96 (Chromium 154) headless on the Air · CDP Page.getAppManifest, Page.getInstallabilityErrors`

**증상:** a company home (apex, served by a host rewrite) and a games portal (subdomain) ran from one Next app. The apex had no install UI and no service worker, yet `Page.getInstallabilityErrors` on it was `[]` and `Page.getAppManifest` returned the portal's manifest (`name: "MNORI GAMES"`): Chrome's own "Install app" menu item put the portal's name on the home screen, and the icon opened the company home. `app/manifest.ts` adds `<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest">` to every page of every root layout, whatever the host. A service worker is not needed for installability in Chromium 154, so "we never added install there" does not mean the site cannot be installed.

**사실:** each origin is its own app (its own `id` resolves against its own origin), so one file has to answer differently per host. `app/manifest.ts` may read the request: `export default async function manifest() { const host = (await headers()).get("host"); return companyHosts.has(host) ? company() : games(); }`. The build then lists `ƒ /manifest.webmanifest` (dynamic) instead of a static file, and with `next start` on one port `http://localhost:<port>` and `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` received the two different manifests, each with zero installability errors. For local tests, make the company origin an env value (`NEXT_PUBLIC_COMPANY_URL=http://localhost:<port>`, portal at `127.0.0.1`) so both apps can be checked from one server.

**해결:** whenever one deployment serves several hostnames, open each host's page and read `Page.getAppManifest` before shipping; if a host is not meant to be an app, its manifest still decides what Chrome's menu installs. Serve the manifest per host from `app/manifest.ts` with `headers()`, and purge `/manifest.webmanifest` per hostname at the CDN after the change.

## OPS-607 — SpacetimeDB SQL over HTTP names a Rust field `p256dh` as column `p_256_dh`; a reader of `row.p256dh` gets `undefined`

`측정 2026-10-22 · SpacetimeDB 2.8.0 standalone (Air) · POST /v1/database/<db>/sql with the owner's token · Node 26 fetch`

**증상:** a Web Push sender read a private table `push_sub { identity, endpoint, p256dh, auth, hour, made_at }` through `POST /v1/database/<db>/sql` and mapped each row by `schema.elements[i].name.some`. Every send failed quietly (`keys.p256dh` was `undefined`, so `web-push` threw before any request), and the test's push service received nothing.

**사실:** the SQL result names that column `p_256_dh` (the schema element is `{"name":{"some":"p_256_dh"}}`): the server splits letters and digits into words when it makes the SQL name. `endpoint`, `auth`, `hour` and `made_at` came back unchanged. Reducer arguments over the websocket are positional, so the client side never notices. A private table read without the owner's token answered HTTP 400.

**해결:** read columns by the name the SQL schema reports (or check `schema.elements` once in a test), or give such fields names without digits next to letters (`p256` → `key_p`, etc.). Assert on the decoded payload in an end-to-end test rather than on "sent N".

## OPS-608 — Brave (Playwright, fresh profile) takes about 30 s to resolve its first `pushManager.subscribe()`: it is registering with FCM, not hanging

`측정 2026-10-22 · Brave 1.96 (Chromium 154) headed via playwright 1.58.2 launchPersistentContext · macOS (MacBook Air M1) · brave.gcm.channel_status=true (OPS-330)`

**증상:** a reminder flow called `Notification.requestPermission()` (granted by `grantPermissions`) then `reg.pushManager.subscribe(...)`; a test that waited 32 s saw no subscription, no error and no toast, and failed as "subscription never saved".

**사실:** on a brand-new profile the first `subscribe()` resolved with an `https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/…` endpoint after 31.2 s and 27.2 s on a bare page (with and without dropping Playwright's default `--disable-background-networking`; the flag made no difference), and after about 80 s inside a busy WebGL game page. Once it resolved, a VAPID push sent from Node `web-push` was shown by the service worker 271 ms later (`registration.getNotifications()`).

Sending right after that first subscription is unreliable. In five runs (fresh profile each, VAPID push from `web-push` within a few minutes of `subscribe()`): twice FCM answered 201 and the notification showed (271 ms, 1,010 ms); once 201 and nothing showed within 90 s; twice FCM answered **404** for the brand-new endpoint. A sender that drops a subscription on any 404 (a common reading of the Web Push spec) would have deleted those two valid-looking registrations at once.

**해결:** wait up to two minutes for the first subscription in tests, and show progress in the UI while it runs ("켜는 중…" on the button) instead of leaving a disabled button that looks broken. Do subscribe → send → check notification in one browser session (OPS-330), and let the test retry the send a few times a minute apart. In the sender, treat 410 as final but drop on 404 only when the subscription is older than about a day; retry a fresh one on the next pass with a small daily cap.

## OPS-609 — Playwright WebKit on the Air: `Executable doesn't exist … webkit-2248` for Playwright 1.58.2, while the cache holds webkit-2359/2370; NODE_PATH cannot swap the version

`측정 2026-10-22 · MacBook Air (shared test host) · ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright has webkit-2359, webkit-2370 · playwright 1.58.2 and 1.64.1`

**증상:** a WebKit test using the project's `tests/node_modules/playwright` (1.58.2) failed at `webkit.launch()` with `Executable doesn't exist at …/ms-playwright/webkit-2248/pw_run.sh`. Running it with `NODE_PATH=<other>/node_modules` did not help: `require('playwright')` resolves the `node_modules` next to the script first, and NODE_PATH is only the last fallback.

**사실:** webkit-2370 is the build of Playwright 1.64.1 (`playwright-core/browsers.json`), already installed on the Air by other projects. Installing `playwright@1.64.1` into a separate folder of your own takes about a second and downloads no browser.

**해결:** keep a small runner folder (`npm install playwright@1.64.1`) and load it explicitly from the WebKit test: `require(process.env.PLAYWRIGHT || 'playwright')` with `PLAYWRIGHT=$PWD/webkit-runner/node_modules/playwright`. Do not borrow another project's `node_modules`; it may be deleted mid-run. Match the version to a cached build with `grep -A2 '"webkit"' node_modules/playwright-core/browsers.json`.

## OPS-610 — Playwright mobile emulation (Chromium): `window.screen` does not follow the viewport; a landscape 844×390 context reported a screen height of 800

`측정 2026-10-22 · playwright 1.58.2 · Brave 1.96 headless · newContext({viewport:{width:844,height:390}, isMobile:true, hasTouch:true})`

**증상:** a page compared the browser's visible height with the whole screen (`innerHeight` against `Math.min(screen.width, screen.height)`) to show how much larger the game gets as an installed app. In the test it claimed "390px → 800px, +105 %".

**사실:** without a `screen` option the context keeps a default screen size that has nothing to do with the emulated phone, so any code that reads `screen.*` gets numbers no phone has. Real phones report their own size (Android Chrome swaps width and height with the orientation; iOS Safari keeps the portrait numbers).

**해결:** pass `screen` equal to the viewport (`newContext({viewport:size, screen:size, …})`) in phone emulation, and have the page ignore implausible ratios (here: anything above +60 % shows no percentage) so a wrong `screen` never turns into a wrong claim on screen.

## OPS-611 — Dokploy raw compose: an `env_file:` with a host path fails with "env file … not found", while bind mounts of the same folder work

`측정 2026-10-22 · Dokploy on nj1 (compose, sourceType raw) · docker compose up -d --build --remove-orphans`

**증상:** a new compose service got its secrets from `env_file: [/home/<user>/.mnori-deploy/<app>/secrets/push.env]` (file present on the host, mode 600). The deployment stopped before any container changed: `env file /home/<user>/…/push.env not found: stat …: no such file or directory` → `Error: ❌ Docker command failed`, and Dokploy marked the compose `error`. The services already running (web, database, tunnel) kept running the previous release.

**사실:** Dokploy runs `docker compose` inside its own container, so paths the compose CLI itself reads (`env_file`, and the `.env` it writes) are looked up in that container's filesystem. Volume sources are handed to the Docker daemon and resolved on the host, which is why `- /home/<user>/…/releases/<rev>/web:/usr/share/nginx/html:ro` in the same file works.

**해결:** mount the secrets file instead (`- /home/<user>/…/secrets/push.env:/run/secrets/push.env:ro`) and have the service read it (a `SECRETS_FILE` it parses at start), or put the values into Dokploy's own environment (`compose.saveEnvironment`; note that call replaces the whole env, so merge the existing variables first). Check `docker ps` after `compose.deploy`: a failed run leaves the old containers up, so the site looks fine while the new service never started.

## OPS-612 — nginx 1.28 (alpine image) serves `manifest.webmanifest` as `application/octet-stream`

`측정 2026-10-22 · nginx:1.28-alpine with the stock /etc/nginx/mime.types · behind Cloudflare`

**증상:** `curl -I https://<site>/manifest.webmanifest` answered `content-type: application/octet-stream` for a PWA manifest; the file and its `<link rel="manifest">` were right.

**사실:** the stock `mime.types` maps `.json` but has no line for `webmanifest`, so the file falls to `default_type`. The type was fixed before any browser check, so whether Chromium tolerates the octet-stream type was not measured here; validators expect `application/manifest+json`.

**해결:** `location = /manifest.webmanifest { default_type application/manifest+json; expires -1; }` (`default_type` applies because no extension matches), or add `application/manifest+json webmanifest;` to a `types {}` block. Purge the URL at the CDN afterwards.

## OPS-613 — iOS 27 home-screen web app: its own localStorage but Safari's cookies; `start_url` comes from the manifest linked at page load, a manifest link swapped in later is ignored

`측정 2026-10-22 · Xcode 27 iOS 27.0 simulator (iPhone 18 Pro, Korean UI) · Safari 27 "홈 화면에 추가" (웹 앱으로 열기 on) · XCUITest-driven, page served over an ssh -L tunnel to 127.0.0.1`

**증상:** a site wanted its iPhone home-screen app to start with what the visitor had in Safari (progress kept in `localStorage`). Probe page logging to its server:
- the home-screen app saw `localStorage` empty (`ls=null`, Safari had `probe=safari`), but `document.cookie` and request cookies held Safari's cookie (`probe=safari`). Storage is split, the cookie jar is shared;
- swapping `<link rel="manifest">` to `/m.webmanifest?carry=X` 0.8 s after load: Safari never fetched the new URL (one manifest request, at load) and the add sheet and the app used the first manifest's `start_url`;
- a manifest link written by an inline `<head>` script from `location.search` (`/?carry=X` → `/m.webmanifest?carry=X`, `start_url: "/?carry=X"`) was fetched at load and the app opened `/?carry=X`;
- the share sheet's preview uses `<title>` and showed a compass for an SVG `apple-touch-icon`; the add sheet and the home-screen icon used the manifest/touch icon and the name from `short_name`;
- with the default status bar style the app's status bar stayed white over a dark page (theme-color not applied); `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style: black-translucent` set at add time draws the page under it (then pad with `env(safe-area-inset-top)`).
- XCUITest: Safari's page menu cell `ShareButton` (label 공유); in the share sheet the action row's `더 보기 (⌄)` is not in the tree and the apps row has another `더 보기` that opens the app list — tap the action one by coordinate (402×874 pt screen: 332, 780). The add sheet's `추가` is at 355, 100. A second icon with the same name lands on the next home page: swipe left before tapping it.

**해결:** to hand state from Safari to the home-screen app without a sign-in, leave it on the server under a short-lived one-time code and put the code in a cookie when the install guide opens; the app's first launch reads the cookie and takes the state (no reload or manifest tricks needed). Put a PNG `apple-touch-icon` (180 px, full-bleed) and `apple-mobile-web-app-title` in the page before anyone adds it — both are fixed at add time (OPS-483).

## OPS-614 — Real iPad Safari 26.6 (iPadOS 26.7.1): the toolbar's Share button sits 120 pt from the right edge, so an on-page arrow pointing at it is placed from the right, not at a share of the width

`측정 2026-10-22 · iPad mini 5 (iPad11,1) · iPadOS 26.7.1 · Safari 26.6.2, landscape 1024×768 pt · safaridriver (OPS-351) + devicectl screenshots (OPS-325)`

**증상:** an install guide drew an arrow at `left: 84%` of the viewport under the toolbar's Share button (taken from a simulator layout). On the real iPad in landscape the arrow landed at x 860 pt and pointed between Share's left edge and the page; the Share icon's centre in the device screenshot (2048 px wide) was at x 1807 px = **904 pt**, 120 pt from the right edge. In the iPadOS 27 portrait simulator (OPS-508) Share was at 624 of 744 pt, also 120 pt from the right: the right-hand toolbar group (공유 · + · 탭) is a fixed-width cluster anchored to the edge. OPS-508's follow-up gives 882 pt for this iPad in landscape; this run measured 904 with a single Safari window and no sidebar open.

Other measured facts from the same run:
- UA: `Mozilla/5.0 (iPad; CPU OS 18_7 like Mac OS X) … Version/26.6.2 Mobile/15E148 Safari/604.1` — the OS part is frozen at 18_7 here too; `Version/` gives 26.
- `innerHeight` 682 against `screen` 768×1024: a page in Safari loses 86 pt (11 %) to the toolbars in landscape.
- A safaridriver session's Safari shows the address pill in orange (automation) but the toolbar geometry is the normal one.

**해결:** place such an arrow with `left: calc(100% - 120px)` (or `right: 120px` minus half its width) for iPad Safari, and check it against a real-device screenshot: `xcrun devicectl device capture screenshot` shows Safari's own toolbar, which a WebKit browser test never draws.

## OPS-615 — `accent-color` on `<progress>`: a light lime (`#c5fa71`) draws as dark green in Android Chrome 155 and iPad Safari 26.6; style the bar's pseudo-elements instead

`측정 2026-10-22 · Pixel 7 Pro, Android 17, Chrome 155.0.8059.84 · iPad mini 5, iPadOS 26.7.1, Safari 26.6.2 · Godot 4.7 web export's #status-progress`

**증상:** a loading screen set `#status-progress { accent-color: #c5fa71 }` (a light lime on a near-black page). On both real devices the filled part of the bar was a dark green (about `#3c7d1e`), not the lime, so the bar looked like a different product's. Screenshots taken in desktop browsers had not flagged it.

**해결:** draw the bar yourself:
`#status-progress{-webkit-appearance:none;appearance:none;background:#2b3142;border:0;border-radius:3px;overflow:hidden}`
`#status-progress::-webkit-progress-bar{background:#2b3142}`
`#status-progress::-webkit-progress-value{background:#c5fa71}`
`#status-progress::-moz-progress-bar{background:#c5fa71}`.
After this both devices drew the exact lime (checked in device screenshots). Look at a loading screen on a real phone at least once; `accent-color` results differ per engine.

## OPS-616 — Real Pixel, installed PWA: the launcher shows a shortcut's `short_name` behind a "바로가기" row, and a changed `short_name` waits for the user in a "이름 업데이트 검토" dialog on the app's next launch

`측정 2026-10-22 · Pixel 7 Pro, Android 17, Pixel Launcher · Chrome 155.0.8059.84 · WebAPKs of mnori.com and play.mnori.com · adb + Chrome remote debugging`

**증상:** a company site's manifest had three `shortcuts` with `name` "서비스 10개", "MNORI GAMES", "문의하기" and `short_name` "서비스", "게임", "문의", and the install sheet showed the `name`s. After a real install, a long press on the icon showed the app menu (삭제, 앱 정보, 앱 일시중지, 대화창) and one collapsed row "바로가기"; only a tap on it opened the shortcuts, labelled with the `short_name`s and their own icons. Separately, the games app on the same phone was installed with `short_name` "MNORI"; after the manifest changed to "MNORI GAMES", launching the WebAPK showed Chrome's "이름 업데이트 검토" dialog (old icon and name → new, buttons 앱 제거 / 확인) before the page.

**사실:**
- Install timing on this phone from the page's button: Chrome's install sheet → 설치 → WebAPK package present after 4 s, the app (`SameTaskWebApkActivity`) in front after 8 s, with the hand-off of OPS-284.
- After 확인 in the name dialog, the WebAPK's package (`lastUpdateTime`, `versionCode`) had not changed 4.5 minutes later, and the home-screen label still read the old name. The rename is not instant.
- Chrome on Android does not cope with Playwright's browser-wide `connectOverCDP` when the phone has many frozen background tabs: the second connection hangs. Attaching to the one page's `webSocketDebuggerUrl` from `/json` works; a tab opened in the background loaded the service worker's offline page until it was activated (`/json/activate/<id>`).

**해결:** give every shortcut a `short_name` that is the whole label you want people to see, and do not promise "long-press and go" — on Pixel it is long-press, then 바로가기. Treat a `short_name` change as a prompt the user must accept on next launch, not a silent rename; installed copies keep the old label until they do.

## OPS-617 — Offline test of a PWA in Playwright: `context.setOffline(true)` still answers a page from the HTTP cache through the service worker, and `navigator.onLine` stays `true` on a page the worker served from its cache

`측정 2026-10-22 · Brave 156.1.98.60 headless on the Air · playwright-core 1.64.1 · launchPersistentContext · network-first service worker for navigations`

**증상:** a site's service worker answers navigations network first and falls back to its own cache (`kn-pages`) when the fetch fails; the page shows a "오프라인이에요" note when `!navigator.onLine`. In a test, after reading `/nj`, `context.setOffline(true)` and `page.goto('/nj')` showed the page **without** the note. Two things were true at once:
- The page had `Cache-Control: public, max-age=120`. The worker's `fetch(request)` was answered by the browser's HTTP cache, so the worker never reached its fallback and served it as a network response.
- After clearing that cache the worker did serve its kept copy, but `navigator.onLine` on that page was still `true` (`{ online: true }` read with `page.evaluate`), so a check on `navigator.onLine` alone never shows an offline note there.

**해결:** let the worker mark what it serves from its cache instead of trusting `navigator.onLine`: rewrite the kept HTML on the way out (`new Response((await r.text()).replace('<body', '<body data-kept'), { status: r.status, headers: r.headers })`) and show the note when `!navigator.onLine || document.body.hasAttribute('data-kept')`. In the test, clear the HTTP cache before going offline: `await (await context.newCDPSession(page)).send('Network.clearBrowserCache'); await context.setOffline(true);`. With both, the kept page showed the note and an unread page got the offline page. On a real phone a page still inside its `max-age` also comes from the HTTP cache while offline, without the note; that is fine, it is fresh. (Installability in a non-persistent context: OPS-364.)

## OPS-618 — Astro + Cloudflare: a `prerender = true` page behind a sign-in middleware is built as a "Redirecting to: /" page, even when the runtime treats its path as public

`측정 2026-10-22 · Astro 7.3.3 · @astrojs/cloudflare 14.3 · middleware that redirects signed-out requests to /`

**증상:** a self-contained `/offline` page (for a service worker to keep) was marked `export const prerender = true`. The site's middleware lets a list of public paths through and sends everything else without a session to `/`. In `astro dev` the page answered 200 with its content. In production it answered **200 `text/html` whose body was `<title>Redirecting to: /</title>`**: at build time the prerender ran through the middleware, which had no session (and no runtime env) and redirected, and Astro wrote that redirect out as the static page. Nothing in the build output warned.

**해결:** do not prerender a page on a site whose middleware gates by session; let it render on request (drop `prerender`), and make the middleware's public list include the path. Check production by content, not status: `curl -s https://<host>/offline | grep -o '<title>[^<]*'`. If a service worker cached the stub, change the worker's bytes (a version constant) so it installs again and re-fetches the page.

## OPS-619 — Playwright WebKit drops a `Secure` `__Host-` session cookie on `http://127.0.0.1`; send the cookie as a header with `context.route`

`측정 2026-10-22 · playwright-core 1.63 WebKit 2370 and Brave 1.97 on the Air · astro dev on http://127.0.0.1`

**증상:** a local test signs a member session with the site's own `seal()` and loads it as `storageState` (`__Host-kc_session`, `secure: true`). In Brave (Chromium) the pages opened signed in: Chromium treats `127.0.0.1` as a secure origin. In WebKit the same state led to the signed-out redirect on every page: WebKit does not keep a `Secure` cookie on plain-http `127.0.0.1`.

**해결:** for WebKit contexts, add the cookie to every request yourself: `ctx.route(url => url.href.startsWith(base), route => route.continue({ headers: { ...route.request().headers(), cookie: 'name=value' } }))`. Also note the session's own limits: here `unseal()` refused any session whose `exp - iat` exceeded 6 hours, so a 24-hour test session was silently "signed out" in every browser.

## OPS-620 — 2026-10-22: Google now stops every automation profile tried at the passkey challenge, including a copy of the main Mac's gstack profile that passed on 2026-10-16 (OPS-447)

`측정 2026-10-22 · Brave 1.97 on the Air (~/kc-test/profile and a copy) · Chrome for Testing chromium-1243 on the main Mac (copy of ~/.gstack/chromium-profile, headed, off-screen)`

**증상:** signing in to a site with "Google로 로그인" picked `chowooick@gmail.com` in the account chooser and then stopped at `accounts.google.com/v3/signin/challenge/pk` ("본인 확인 중... 패스키를 사용하여 로그인을 완료합니다") in all three: the Air's `~/kc-test/profile`, a copy of it, and an off-screen headed copy of the main Mac's gstack profile, which is how OPS-447 got through six days earlier. The site's own session cookie in those profiles had expired, so nothing signed-in could be reached.

**해결:** a session cannot pass this alone. Do signed-in checks on a local server with a locally sealed session (OPS-619), verify public files in production by content with curl, and leave the signed-in production check as the owner's one step: open the passkey challenge in a headed window and ask the owner to approve it, then save the site session for the tests.

## OPS-621 — jsQR misses QR codes drawn with round dots at some sizes; rounded squares (0.4 square stroked 0.6, round joins) read at every size

`측정 2026-10-22 · jsqr 1.4.0 · qrcode 1.5.4 (version 4, error correction H, 11×11 modules cleared for a centre icon) · sharp rasterising the SVG · Brave 1.96 screenshots on the Air`

**증상:** a styled QR code (data modules as round dots — a zero-length path with `stroke-linecap: round`, width 0.9–1.0 module — and rounded finder eyes) decoded in the local Playwright check but returned `null` from jsQR on the live page at 1x (124 px, ≈3.2 px per module) for the production URL. Nothing else differed except the URL, i.e. the module pattern.

**사실:** a sweep of 3 URLs × 9 sizes (116–148 px, step 4) × 1x/2x = 54 renders per style:

| Data modules | Decoded |
|---|---|
| plain squares | 54/54 |
| round dots, 0.96 module | 47/54 (misses at 1x *and* 2x) |
| squares, rounded eyes, centre icon | 54/54 |
| rounded squares: `M x+.3 y+.3 h.4v.4h-.4z`, fill + `stroke-width: .6; stroke-linejoin: round` (1 module, 0.3 corners) | 54/54 |

Rounded finder eyes and the cleared centre (≈11% of a v4 code at level H) cost nothing; the round dots are what fail. Passing in one check proves little — the failures depend on the exact pattern and pixel size.

**해결:** draw data modules as rounded squares (the stroke trick keeps the path ≈20 bytes per module), keep rounded eyes and the icon if wanted, and guard it with a unit test that rasterises the SVG at many sizes and scales and decodes each with jsQR.

## OPS-622 — Chrome 155 on Android may answer a PWA install with a home-screen shortcut instead of a WebAPK: the launcher's "홈 화면에 추가" dialog appears and `getInstalledRelatedApps()` never sees an app

`측정 2026-10-22 · Pixel 7 Pro (Android 17) · Chrome 155.0.8059.84 · new origin, manifest with id, icons 192/512/maskable, screenshots, related_applications`

**증상:** a site's own install button called the saved `beforeinstallprompt`, Chrome's install sheet showed, and 「설치」 was tapped. On the first two tries the WebAPK never came: 13 s and then 60 s after the tap, `topResumedActivity` became the launcher's `com.android.launcher3.QuickstepAddItemActivity` (logcat: `START … act=android.content.pm.action.CONFIRM_PIN_SHORTCUT`), a "Chrome · 교민마트 1×1 · 취소 / 홈 화면에 추가" pin-shortcut dialog. Chrome's own log said nothing about why. The page, polling `getInstalledRelatedApps()` to open the new app (OPS-284), waited in "설치 중" for its whole timeout. The third try on the same phone, minutes later, minted the WebAPK (`GoogleAssociationService` fetched `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` first; `firstInstallTime` set), the page saw it and the `intent://` opened the app. The same phone had minted another origin's WebAPK normally the day before, so this was not a broken Play setup.

**해결:** do not assume 「설치」 always ends in a WebAPK. While waiting, watch `visibilitychange`: the pin dialog hides the page; once the page has been visible again for ~15 s with no app, tell the visitor to check the home screen and offer 다시 시도 (a reload, which brings a fresh `beforeinstallprompt`), and keep polling in case the WebAPK still lands. Test this path with a faked `document.hidden` toggle; a real phone reproduces it only sometimes. On a test phone, cancel the pin dialog (`uiautomator dump`, tap 「취소」) so no stray shortcut is left.

## OPS-623 — Xcode 27.1 `test-without-building` on a real iPad (iPadOS 26.7.1) fails with "Root install style is not supported on this device"; delete `DSTROOTPath` from the .xctestrun
