`측정 2026-10-22 · Xcode 27.1 (27A9275) · iPad mini 5 (iPad11,1) · iPadOS 26.7.1 (23H30) · UI-test-only project, Personal Team signing`

**증상:** a project with one UI-testing bundle and no app target built (`build-for-testing … -allowProvisioningUpdates`, `TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED`), but `xcodebuild test-without-building` (with `-project/-scheme` or with `-xctestrun`) ended at once with `Failed to install or launch the test runner. (Underlying Error: Root install style is not supported on this device. To install internal content, the device must allow installing app bundles and roots, and be running an internal OS build.)`. The log also printed `Supported platforms for the buildables in the current scheme is empty` and `operatingSystemBuild = <DVTBuildVersion 24A94232>, error = invalidDigitCount(94232)`. `xcrun devicectl device install app --device <udid> <Runner>.app` installed the same runner without complaint. The generated .xctestrun carried `"DSTROOTPath" => "/tmp/<Target>.dst"` under the test target.

**해결:** `plutil -remove TestConfigurations.0.TestTargets.0.DSTROOTPath <file>.xctestrun`, then run `test-without-building -xctestrun <file>`: the runner installed and started ("Running tests…") and the device asked for Touch ID (OPS-374). Adding `SDKROOT = iphoneos; SUPPORTED_PLATFORMS = "iphoneos iphonesimulator"` to the test target removes the empty-platforms warning but not the error. A runner re-signed this way can come back with `Developer App Certificate is not trusted`: open 설정 › 일반 › VPN 및 기기 관리 with `xcrun devicectl device process launch --device <udid> --payload-url 'prefs:root=General&path=ManagedConfigurationList' com.apple.Preferences` for the owner to trust it.

## OPS-624 — A service worker that answers a page load with a cached `/offline` response turns the page's address into `/offline`; with a reload-on-`online` handler the tab then loops

`측정 2026-10-22 · Brave 1.96 (Chromium 154) headless via Playwright, offline emulation · Cloudflare Workers static assets`

**증상:** offline, a navigation to `/privacy` was answered by `caches.match('/offline')`. The page showed the offline text, but Playwright's `framenavigated` reported `/offline` after `/privacy`: the cached Response keeps the URL it was fetched from and Chrome gives that URL to the document. The offline page had `addEventListener('online', () => location.reload())`; under the emulation the tab then flipped between `/privacy` and `/offline` every second or so, and every later `goto('/')` or `location.href = '/'` was overwritten (Playwright's `goto` returned `null`). Separately, Workers static assets answer `/offline.html` with a 307 to `/offline`; a redirected response cannot serve a navigation, so precache `/offline`, not `/offline.html`.

**해결:** answer navigations with a fresh Response built from the cached one, which has no URL of its own: `new Response(await cached.blob(), { status: cached.status, statusText: cached.statusText, headers: cached.headers })`. The page then keeps the address it was opened at. Drop automatic reloads from offline pages and keep a 「다시 열기」 button. Check it with `framenavigated`: one navigation per `goto`, not a stream.

## OPS-625 — iOS 27.0 simulator (Xcode 27.1): a home-screen web app gets `PushManager` and permission, but `pushManager.subscribe()` and `getSubscription()` never settle because `webpushd` is killed at launch

`측정 2026-10-25 · Xcode 27.1 (27A9275) · iOS 27.0 simulator runtime (24A434), iPhone 18 Pro · macOS 27 main Mac · driven by a one-test XCUITest (OPS-239)`

**증상:** a diagnostic page served over a quick tunnel (HTTPS), added to the home screen through Safari's page menu → 공유 → 더 보기 → 홈 화면에 추가 → 추가, reported inside the web app: `standalone=true`, `PushManager=true`, `Notification=true`, `permission=default`, service worker ready. `Notification.requestPermission()` showed the real "'<name>'에서 알림을 보내고자 합니다" alert and returned `granted` after 허용. Then `reg.pushManager.subscribe({ userVisibleOnly: true, applicationServerKey })` neither resolved nor rejected for more than a minute. A site whose app first calls `getSubscription()` before asking (to skip people already subscribed) therefore never shows its question at all. The simulator's log (`xcrun simctl spawn <udid> log show --last 2m --predicate 'process == "webpushd" OR subsystem CONTAINS "webpush"'`) showed `com.apple.webkit.webpushd` exiting at every spawn with `OS_REASON_CODESIGNING | Launch Constraint Violation` and launchd throttling the respawn. In plain Safari (not added) `PushManager` and `Notification` are absent, as on a real iPhone.

**해결:** this simulator cannot check web push subscription or delivery; use a real iPhone or iPad (OPS-483). It still checks the add-to-home-screen steps, the web app's start URL and standalone layout. In the app's code, do not let a hung `getSubscription()` hide the whole prompt: race it against a timeout. The iOS 27 page menu also lists 「알림 받기」 for an ordinary website; what it does was not checked.

## OPS-626 — Wrapping a user-supplied PocketBase `filter` in parentheses does not isolate it: `x") || ("y` closes them and ORs past the server's condition

`측정 2026-10-25 · PocketBase filter syntax (fexpr) behind a Cloudflare Worker proxy · node:test against a mocked upstream`

**증상:** a proxy hid moderated records by rewriting the member's query to `filter=((id != "a" && id != "b") || owner = "me") && (<member filter>)`. A member filter of `id!="x") || (id!="y"` turns that into `(…) && (id!="x") || (id!="y")`, and `&&` binds tighter than `||`, so every hidden record comes back. The id list also lengthens the URL with every hidden record.

PocketBase has no bound parameters for a filter that arrives as raw text from the client, so parentheses alone do not separate trusted and untrusted parts.

**해결:** do not splice the client's filter into a server-side condition. Either drop the hidden rows from the JSON answer (filter `items` by id and owner, lower `totalItems` by the number dropped, and append `id,owner` to a `fields=` the client sent so the rows can be identified), or put the rule in the collection's own API rule where PocketBase enforces it. If you must combine filters, reject a client filter whose parentheses go negative or do not balance outside quoted strings.

## OPS-627 — An exact-path blocklist in a Worker wrapper misses `/path/`, other letter case and `%2D`; Astro still routes them, so a cron-only endpoint reaches signed-in users

`측정 2026-10-25 · Astro 5 on Cloudflare Workers (trailingSlash default 'ignore') · production curl, anonymous POST`

**증상:** a wrapper answered 404 for internal cron paths with `if (path === CRON_PATH) return 404`, and the same paths were listed as public so the cron's own request skipped the session check. Anonymous `POST /api/regions/operations-run` got 404, but `POST /api/regions/operations-run/` got 401 `LOGIN_REQUIRED`: it skipped the block, met the session check, and with a member's session it would have gone on to the route, which had no auth of its own.

**해결:** compare in the form the router matches. Decode percent-escapes, collapse repeated slashes, strip the trailing slash and lowercase the path, then block it (`/api/regions/operations-run/`, `/api/Regions/Operations-Run`, `/api/regions/operations%2Drun` all answer 404 after the change). Better still, give the internal request a secret header and check it in the route.

`측정 2026-10-25 · MacBook Air (air.local) · Brave 1.98.60 · Playwright launchPersistentContext on a copy of the default Brave profile`

A copy of Brave's default profile opens `myaccount.google.com` as the signed-out about page, and a site's "Google로 로그인" popup stops at the empty email field (`accounts.google.com/v3/signin/identifier`).

## OPS-629 — PocketBase `auth-with-oauth2` answering 403 "The request doesn't satisfy the collection requirements to authenticate." after Google already passed: the auth collection's `authRule` failed (here a private header key the caller sent was not the one in the rule)

`측정 2026-10-25 · PocketBase 0.40.4 (db.kyomincenter.com) · Cloudflare Worker calling auth-with-oauth2 server-side with PKCE · kc_members authRule = @request.headers.x_kyomin_private = "<key>"`

**증상:** a site's own Google sign-in (popup → PocketBase `/api/oauth2-redirect` → realtime `@oauth2` event → the server exchanges the code with `POST /api/collections/<auth>/auth-with-oauth2`) showed only "Google 계정을 확인하지 못했습니다". The popup reached `/_/#/auth/oauth2-redirect-success`, so Google and the redirect were fine. The exchange answered **403** with `{"message":"The request doesn't satisfy the collection requirements to authenticate."}`. That message is the `authRule`, checked after the OAuth exchange succeeds; the rule had only a header-key clause, and the Worker's secret held a different value than the live rule (the key had been rotated, or the secret was set from an old copy). `auth-methods` worked with the same wrong header, since it needs no rule, so the "prepare" step gave no hint. Local tests with a synthetic PocketBase fixture passed because the fixture checked its own key.

**해결:** log the exchange's status and PocketBase `message` (never the code or tokens) so this shows in `wrangler tail` at once. Read the live rule's key on the database host and pipe it into the secret without printing it: `ssh <db> "sudo sqlite3 -readonly …/data.db \"SELECT json_extract(options,'\$.authRule') FROM _collections WHERE name='<auth>'\" | grep -oE '[0-9a-f]{64}' | head -1 | tr -d '\n'" | npx wrangler secret put <NAME> --name <worker>` (`options` holds the rules in 0.40; there is no `authRule` column). A test fixture must not invent the auth answer's rules; check the secret against the live rule after every key rotation.

## OPS-630 — Driving a phone plugged into another Mac from the Air: point the Air's `adb` at that Mac's adb server through `ssh -R` (`ADB_SERVER_SOCKET`), so test scripts stay on the Air

`측정 2026-10-25 · adb 1.0.41 (platform-tools 37.0.1) on both Macs · Pixel 7 Pro on the main Mac's USB · OpenSSH reverse forward to the Air`

**증상:** tests must run on the Air, but the test phone is plugged into the main Mac. `adb devices` on the Air lists nothing. OPS-601 forwards only Chrome's DevTools port. A first try of the relay failed with `adb: failed to check server version: protocol fault (couldn't read status): Connection reset by peer` and the ssh session printed `connect_to 127.0.0.1 port 5037: failed`: the main Mac's adb server was not running (an earlier `adb forward --remove` session had ended and the server had exited).

**해결:** on the Mac with the phone: `adb start-server` (listens on localhost:5037), then keep `ssh -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -R 15037:127.0.0.1:5037 -R 19333:127.0.0.1:9333 air` open. On the Air: `export ADB_SERVER_SOCKET=tcp:127.0.0.1:15037`; then `adb devices`, `adb shell …`, `adb exec-out screencap`, `adb install`/`uninstall` all run from the Air's scripts against the Mac's phone. `adb forward tcp:9333 localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote` issued from the Air binds the port on the Mac (the server's host), which the second `-R` brings to the Air as 127.0.0.1:19333. Keep both adb versions equal: a mismatched client makes the server restart.

## OPS-632 — busan.mac (the test host since 2026-10-25) has no Godot or Rust; a user-level install takes about two minutes and runs Godot's GPU tests over ssh

`측정 2026-10-25 · busan.mac (Mac mini M4 Pro, macOS 26.6, user jupiter) · Godot 4.7.2-stable · rustup 1.99.1`

**증상:** `ssh busan.mac 'zsh -lc "which godot cargo"'` printed `godot not found` and `cargo not found`; only Homebrew node was there. Godot and Rust test suites written for the Air could not start.

**해결:** install both per user, no sudo:
- Godot: `mkdir -p ~/godot && cd ~/godot && curl -fsSL -o godot.zip https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases/download/4.7.2-stable/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_macos.universal.zip && unzip -q godot.zip && rm godot.zip && mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && ln -sf ~/godot/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot ~/.local/bin/godot` (~/.local/bin is already on the login shell's PATH).
- Rust: `curl -fsSL https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --profile minimal`, then use `~/.cargo/bin/cargo` or add it to PATH in the job script.
- Measured: a full landgrab run there (import, cargo test 32, 13 headless Godot suites, the GPU suite with a window, two screenshot captures) all passed from a detached script started over ssh; non-headless Godot opens its window in the logged-in session without extra setup.

## OPS-633 — Reading news articles server-side to fact-check summaries: TEGNA TV sites answer 403 to everyone, nj1015.com drops a named bot, Korea Daily keeps its body outside `<article>` in `<br>` lines

`측정 2026-10-25 · plain fetch() from Node 26 on busan.mac (KR residential) and on the Air (US) · 31 article URLs of one day's briefs`

**증상:** a fact check that compares a short summary with the original article read nothing for half the articles:
- **TEGNA stations** (9news.com, khou.com, kvue.com, 11alive.com — the main TV sources for Colorado, Houston, Austin and Atlanta) answered **403** (Akamai) to a browser user agent and to a named bot alike, from both machines. 14 of 31 articles.
- **nj1015.com** closed the connection (no status) to `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; <name>/1.0; +https://…)` and answered 200 to a desktop Chrome string.
- **koreadaily.com** returned 200 with the story's text **outside** its `<article>` element (which held only the date), written as text separated by `<br> &nbsp; <br>` with almost no `<p>`; JSON-LD has only a truncated `description`. An extractor that takes `<article>` paragraphs got 38 characters.
- Same URL, different HTML per user agent (gothamist.com): an extractor's output, and so a gate's decision, can change with the UA.

**해결:** send a desktop browser user agent; take the paragraphs of the largest `<article>`, and when they are under a few hundred characters take that element's whole text, then the page's. Treat a short text or a page that names "Access Denied / Just a moment / captcha" as unreadable. Plan for TEGNA sources to be unreadable server-side: anything that requires the original will not publish them.

## OPS-634 — Screen Sharing to a Mac on the tailnet fails when the viewer's Tailscale is stopped; tunnel 5900 over the ssh path that works instead

`측정 2026-10-25 · developer Mac m1max64 (Tailscale macsys, WantRunning=false, ExitNodeID = jupiter) · busan.mac (jupiter, macOS 26.6.2, Tailscale idle, ShieldsUp=false, application firewall off, screensharingd listening on *:5900)`

**증상:** the owner opened `vnc://100.102.194.77` (busan.mac's Tailscale address) and got a connection failure. From the developer Mac, ssh to the same address timed out on ports 22 and 2221. Nothing was wrong on busan.mac. Its `tailscale status` listed every other device offline: `m1max64` (the developer Mac), the iPad and the phone. On the developer Mac, the app's CLI says `Tailscale is stopped.` and there is no `100.x` address. `scutil --nc list` still shows the VPN configuration as `(Connected)`, which misleads.

The stop is deliberate. The saved prefs name jupiter as exit node with `RouteAll=true`, so `tailscale up` would send all of the Mac's traffic through Busan (OPS-347-style side effects, ~175 ms to everything).

**해결:** do not give anyone a `100.x` address before checking the viewer's own `tailscale status`. Reach Screen Sharing through the ssh path that already works: `ssh -f -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -L 127.0.0.1:15900:127.0.0.1:5900 busan.mac`, then `open vnc://127.0.0.1:15900` and sign in as the remote Mac's user. Use a port other than 5900 locally: Screen Sharing refuses `localhost:5900` as "your own screen". Check the tunnel without opening a window: `nc -w 5 127.0.0.1 15900 </dev/null | head -c 12` prints `RFB 003.889`. On the developer Mac this is wrapped as `~/.local/bin/busan-screen` (`check`, `stop`).

## OPS-635 — busan.mac for SpacetimeDB + Godot web tests and nj1 deploy checks: spacetime 2.8.0, the one web template, cloudflared from Homebrew, and the Mac's key through `ssh -A`

`측정 2026-10-25 · busan.mac (macOS 26.6.2, user jupiter) · spacetime 2.8.0 · Godot 4.7.2 · cloudflared 2026.10.3 · blabla`

**증상:** a SpacetimeDB + Godot web project's tests and deploy helpers, written for the Air, could not start on busan.mac: no `spacetime`, no web export template, no `cloudflared` for the nj1 Access ssh hop, and the repo's ssh config named `/Users/chowooick/.local/bin/cloudflared`. In `ssh busan.mac 'zsh -lc "echo $PATH"'` the directory `~/.local/bin` was **not** on PATH (it appears only with `zsh -lic`), so job scripts must prepend it themselves.

**해결:**
- SpacetimeDB: `curl -sSf https://install.spacetimedb.com -o /tmp/i.sh && sh /tmp/i.sh --yes`, then `~/.local/bin/spacetime version install 2.8.0 --use` to match a 2.8.0 production server (the installer brings the newest, 2.13).
- Godot web export: the editor is already in `~/godot` (OPS-632). Templates ship only as a 1.28 GB `.tpz` (GDT-172); copy the one file a non-threaded web export needs, `web_nothreads_release.zip` (10,245,903 bytes) plus `version.txt`, into `~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.7.2.stable/` with `tar | ssh busan.mac tar -x` (scp fails on the space in the path). Check: an export packaged the same 82 web assets as on the Air.
- Rust wasm: `~/.cargo/bin/rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- nj1 over Cloudflare Access ssh: `brew install cloudflared`. With `ssh -A busan.mac`, `ssh -o ProxyCommand="cloudflared access ssh --hostname %h" chowooick@nj1-ssh.mnori.com` logs in with the forwarded key; no browser login was asked for. In shared ssh configs write the ProxyCommand as `sh -c 'PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH" exec cloudflared access ssh --hostname %h'` so it works on both hosts.
- Before writing into a shared `~/.local/bin`, run `ls -la` on the name: another session's `godot` there was a symlink into `~/godot/Godot.app`, and a `printf > ~/.local/bin/godot` wrapper overwrote the real binary through it (restored from the same official zip; `codesign --verify --deep` passed again).

## OPS-636 — `wrangler login` on a remote test host without Screen Sharing: run it with `--browser=false` over `ssh -L 8976:localhost:8976` and open the printed link on the Mac you sit at

`측정 2026-10-25 · wrangler 4.135.0 on busan.mac (macOS 26.6.2) · developer Mac in the US · Cloudflare dashboard already signed in in the local browser`

**증상:** a new test host (busan.mac) had no wrangler login (`You are not authenticated. Please run \`wrangler login\`.`), so deploys could not run there. `wrangler login` opens a browser on the host and waits for Cloudflare's OAuth redirect to `http://localhost:8976/oauth/callback` on that host; doing it through Screen Sharing stalled (the viewer showed only a progress bar). Copying the developer Mac's `~/Library/Preferences/.wrangler/config/default.toml` was avoided: both machines would hold one refresh token, and the one that refreshes second may be signed out.

**해결:** from the developer Mac: `ssh -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -L 8976:localhost:8976 <host> 'zsh -lc "cd <project> && npx wrangler login --browser=false"'` in the background, read the `Visit this link to authenticate: https://dash.cloudflare.com/oauth2/auth?…` line from its output, and `open` that link on the developer Mac. The consent page's redirect to `localhost:8976` lands on the developer Mac's forwarded port and reaches the host's wrangler, which printed `Successfully logged in.` within seconds; `wrangler whoami` on the host then showed the account. The host gets its own OAuth grant; the developer Mac's login is untouched.

## OPS-637 — Screen Sharing through an ssh tunnel to `127.0.0.1:15900` works end to end; a "Connecting…" that never ends was the saved entry with the Tailscale address, not the tunnel

`측정 2026-10-25 · viewer: developer Mac (macOS 27, Screen Sharing.app, Tailscale stopped) · server: busan.mac (macOS 26.6.2, screensharingd, RFB 003.889) · tunnel ~/.local/bin/busan-screen (OPS-634)`

**증상:** the owner opened the tunnel launcher and reported the window stuck on "연결 중". The kernel flow log (`log show … | grep cfil_inp_log`) showed Screen Sharing connecting to `100.102.194.77:5900` from the LAN address: the owner had picked the old saved connection in the 「모든 연결」 list, whose address only answers while the viewer's Tailscale runs. `open vnc://127.0.0.1:15900` sent to an already running Screen Sharing made no connection by itself at that moment.

A later attempt through the tunnel worked. On busan.mac, `screensharingd` logged `SendAuthenticationInfoMessage`, then nothing for 55 s while the viewer waited for the user name and password: a new address has no saved keychain entry. After that came `HandleViewerInitialization` and `encode tables`, and the remote desktop showed live. Over Tailscale with saved credentials the same step takes 250 ms.

- To find which address a viewer really dialled, use the viewer's own kernel log: `log show --start … --style compact | grep '\[<pid> Screen Sharing\]'` prints `faddr` for every TCP connect. The server's log shows only `<private>` unless authentication succeeds.
- `busan-screen check` (and any `nc` probe) shows up on the server as `accept new screen sharing connection` followed at once by `read error 0` / `close the connection from viewer authentication thread`. That is the probe, not a failed viewer.
- Measured throughput of that ssh path, busan.mac → viewer: 20 MB in 15.4 s (~1.3 MB/s).

**해결:** remove the Tailscale-address entry from 「모든 연결」 (or leave Tailscale on, without the exit node), and connect only with the tunnel launcher. Enter the remote user's password once and let Screen Sharing save it to the keychain for `127.0.0.1`.

## OPS-638 — A Cloudflare tunnel ingress rule `path: ^/v1/.*` to the SpacetimeDB container bypasses every nginx rule for /v1; nginx guards only take effect after that rule is removed

`측정 2026-10-25 · cloudflared 2026.10.1 remote-managed tunnel · nginx 1.28 · SpacetimeDB 2.8 · blabla on nj1`

**증상:** after deploying an nginx that answers `location /v1/ { return 403; }` and refuses the database owner token, a probe from the server to the public hostname still got **200** for `POST /v1/database/blabla/sql` with the owner token, and **405** (not 403) for `POST /v1/database/blabla`. `nginx -t` passed and the container had the new config. The tunnel's remote configuration (`GET /accounts/{acc}/cfd_tunnel/{id}/configurations`) had two rules for the host: `{"path":"^/v1/.*","service":"http://<db-alias>:3000"}` first, then the site to nginx. Cloudflare matched /v1 to the database directly, so nginx never saw those requests. A database-container network alias like `<app>-spacetime-xxxx` is the hint that such a rule exists.

**해결:** `PUT` the configuration back without the path rule (keep a copy of the old JSON for rollback); the change applied within about 20 s, and the same probe then returned 403 for the owner token in every form (Bearer, lowercase bearer, Basic, `/v1/identity/websocket-token`, `?token=`, percent-encoded) and for publish/delete/other /v1 paths, while `GET /v1/database/<db>/identity`, the game's websocket (`/subscribe` with and without `?token=`) and the admin SQL path kept working. Publish and owner SQL then run inside the database container (`docker exec <db> spacetime --config-path <tmp> publish --server http://127.0.0.1:3000 ...`, token written to a 0600 temp file and removed). Check every SpacetimeDB app behind a tunnel for the same rule before relying on nginx for /v1.

## OPS-639 — Moving a caller-side API token off a workstation into a GitLab CI variable: create it `masked_and_hidden`, prove the copy by a sha256 prefix in the job log and a real call

`측정 2026-10-25 · GitLab.com (SaaS shared runner, curlimages/curl:8.10.1) · glab 1.82.0 · Cloudflare Worker secret`

**증상:** a Worker accepted a bearer token stored as a Worker secret, and the only readable copy of the value was a 64-byte key file on a test host that was being retired. Worker secrets are write-only (`wrangler secret list` shows names only), so once the file is gone nobody can tell whether a new copy is right except by calling the endpoint.

- `POST /projects/:id/variables` with `"masked_and_hidden": true, "protected": true` makes a variable whose value the API never returns again: `GET /projects/:id/variables/<KEY>` answers `"value": null, "hidden": true`. Hidden is set only at creation.
- Send the value as a JSON body file (`glab api -X POST … -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --input body.json`, file mode 0600, deleted after) so it is never in argv or shell history. In the job, pass the header through stdin, `printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "$TOKEN" | curl -H @- …`, so it is not in the job's process list either.
- Masking hides the value, not a hash of it: `printf %s "$TOKEN" | sha256sum | cut -c1-12` in the job log, compared with `shasum -a 256 <file> | cut -c1-12` on the old host, proves the copy byte for byte (a trailing newline in the file would change the hash, so check the file's length first).
- A protected variable reaches only pipelines on protected branches. `POST /projects/:id/pipeline?ref=main` has source `api`; a `.gitlab-ci.yml` whose `workflow:rules` admit only `web`, `api` and `schedule` makes pushes start no pipeline at all, so a check job costs nothing until someone runs it.

**해결:** compare the prefixes, run one pipeline and require the real endpoint's answer (here `HTTP 200 {"ok":true,"latencyMs":360}` with prefix `950e1062b047` matching the file), then delete the file on the old host and confirm with `ls` (`No such file or directory`).

## OPS-640 — Moving Air test scripts to busan.mac: hard-coded `/Users/chowooick/...` imports break (user is `jupiter`), a plain `nohup zsh job.sh` has no Homebrew `node`, and saved dev-server tokens answer 401

`측정 2026-10-25 · busan.mac (macOS 26.6.2, user jupiter) · node 26.12.1 · Playwright from ~/kc-test · spacetime 2.8.0 · Godot 4.7.2 web export · trade`

**증상:** three failures when a SpacetimeDB + Godot web project's Air workflow first ran on busan.mac:
- a Playwright test with `import … from '/Users/chowooick/kc-test/node_modules/playwright-core/index.mjs'` cannot load there: the home directory is `/Users/jupiter`.
- `ssh busan.mac 'nohup zsh ~/work/job.sh > log 2>&1 &'` printed `command not found: node` (exit 127): a non-login zsh has neither `/opt/homebrew/bin` nor `~/.local/bin` on PATH. The same script started from inside `ssh busan.mac 'zsh -l -s'` found `node`.
- browser tests that keep per-origin seat tokens in a file (keyed `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) copied from the Air failed against the new local SpacetimeDB: the console showed `Failed to load resource: … 401 (Unauthorized)` and the client fell back to a new identity. The tokens were issued by the Air's dev server; a new server (or `--reset`) refuses them. Production-origin entries in the same file are unaffected.

**해결:** load Playwright by home: ``const { chromium } = await import(`${homedir()}/kc-test/node_modules/playwright-core/index.mjs`)``. Start detached jobs with `nohup zsh -l job.sh` and still prepend `$HOME/.local/bin` in the script (OPS-635). Expect one failing run after moving a dev server; it saves the new tokens and the next run passes. A dev-only CLI identity (`spacetime login --token` from the dev server's `/v1/identity`) is not worth copying between hosts: issue a new one on the new host and delete the old file.

## OPS-641 — Android WebAPK: the gesture-bar strip takes the manifest's `theme_color` and ignores dark mode; Chrome 156 mints no dark colours from `user_preferences.color_scheme_dark`

`측정 2026-10-25 · Pixel 7 Pro · Android 17 · Chrome 156.0.8078.47 · system dark mode on · WebAPK shell 194`

**증상:** a PWA whose manifest has `theme_color` / `background_color` `#ffffff` and `user_preferences: { color_scheme_dark: { theme_color: "#0c1214", background_color: "#0c1214" } }` was freshly installed as a WebAPK. In dark mode the app's status bar was dark, taken from the page's `<meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">`. The 69 px navigation (gesture) strip at the bottom was white. The same page in a Chrome tab had a dark strip.

- The minted APK's `AndroidManifest.xml` (`adb shell pm path <pkg>`, pull, `aapt2 dump xmltree --file AndroidManifest.xml`) carries `org.chromium.webapk.shell_apk.themeColor = -1L` (white) and `darkThemeColor = ""` / `darkBackgroundColor = ""`. The dark keys exist in the shell but Chrome left them empty. All 29 WebAPKs on the phone had them empty.
- The strip colour is the manifest `theme_color`, not `background_color` and not the page's meta tag. An installed app with `theme_color` #141416 and `background_color` #ffffff drew the strip #141416. Another with `theme_color` #000065 drew it #000065, while its status bar followed the page.
- A WebAPK installed before a manifest change keeps the old values until Chrome updates it. Reinstall, or wait for Chrome's periodic update check, before measuring.

**해결:** do not rely on `user_preferences.color_scheme_dark` in Chrome 156 (keeping it is harmless). The gesture strip has one colour for both modes: the manifest `theme_color`. Pick it for the mode most readers use, or a colour that sits acceptably on both grounds. The status bar still follows the page's media-qualified `theme-color` meta tags.

## OPS-642 — Android Play upload key in GitLab CI variables: Gradle reads `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_*`, a 6-character alias cannot be masked, hidden values cannot be read back, and macOS `/usr/bin/keytool` 25 crashes on `-printcert` in a Korean locale

`측정 2026-10-25 · GitLab.com SaaS runner saas-linux-small-amd64 · cimg/android:2026.08.1 · AGP 8.13.0 · Gradle 8.14.3 · glab · macOS keytool 25.0.1 · Android Studio JBR keytool`

**증상:** moving a Play upload keystore and its passwords from a workstation into GitLab CI/CD variables hit four things that are not obvious:
- A 6-character key alias cannot be masked (GitLab masks only values of 8+ characters), so it stays a protected, unmasked variable. The passwords (28 characters) masked fine.
- A variable created with `--hidden` (needs `-m`) returns no `value` from `GET /projects/:id/variables` any more, so the stored copy cannot be compared by hash afterwards. Only a real signed build proves it.
- A Gradle `signingConfigs` block guarded by `if (findProperty("…StoreFile") != null)` builds an **unsigned** release bundle without any error when the property is missing, so a "BUILD SUCCESSFUL" alone proves nothing.
- On the developer Mac, `/usr/bin/keytool -printcert -jarfile app.aab` (keytool 25.0.1, system locale ko) printed `서명자 #1:` / `Certificate #1:` and then `keytool 오류: java.util.IllegalFormatConversionException: d != java.lang.String`, exit 0 and no fingerprints. `-J-Duser.language=en` did not help. Android Studio's bundled `…/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home/bin/keytool` printed the certificate normally.

**해결:** name the CI variables `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_<property>`; Gradle reads each as `-P<property>`, so `build.gradle.kts` needs no change. Store the keystore as a **file** variable holding one-line base64 (`base64 -i key.jks | tr -d '\n' | glab variable set NAME -t file -p -m --hidden -r`; 5,708 characters masked fine), feed every value through stdin with output sent to `/dev/null`, and mark all of them protected (they then reach only protected branches). In the job: `base64 -d "$NAME" > .upload.jks`, export the store-file property, build, then fail unless `jarsigner -verify` says `jar verified`, and delete the keystore in `after_script`. Prove the move by comparing the bundle's certificate SHA-256 with the keystore's (`keytool -list -v -storepass:env VAR`) using the JBR keytool. A full `bundleRelease` on the small SaaS runner took 5 min 45 s including the image pull.

## OPS-643 — wrangler on a second host logged in to several Cloudflare accounts stops with "More than one account available but unable to select one in non-interactive mode"

`측정 2026-10-25 · wrangler 4.135.0 · busan.mac logged in through OPS-636 · 6 accounts on the login`

**증상:** `npm run deploy` over ssh printed the account table and exited. The log had `✘ [ERROR] More than one account available but unable to select one in non-interactive mode.` The same project deployed from the developer Mac without a prompt, because that checkout had `node_modules/.cache/wrangler/wrangler-account.json` from an earlier interactive pick. A fresh checkout on another host has no such cache.

**해결:** pass `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=<id>` to the deploy, or copy the developer checkout's `node_modules/.cache/wrangler/wrangler-account.json` (account id and name only, no secret) to the host's checkout. Both deployed at once. Add `account_id` to the wrangler config to make it permanent.

## OPS-644 — nj2 has no cron and no sudo for `chowooick`, but `loginctl enable-linger chowooick` works without a password, so a systemd user timer runs hourly jobs there across logout and reboot

`측정 2026-10-25 · nj2 (Ubuntu, x86_64, user chowooick, no docker group) · systemd user instance`

**증상:** moving an hourly pull job (dongnesosik's off-site backup copy) from the Air to nj2: `command -v crontab` printed nothing and `/var/spool/cron` did not exist; `loginctl show-user chowooick -p Linger` was `Linger=no`, so a user timer would stop at logout.

**해결:** `loginctl enable-linger chowooick` succeeded with no prompt (polkit allows it for your own user); `Linger=yes` after. Then install a `~/.config/systemd/user/<name>.service` (`Type=oneshot`, `StandardOutput=append:<log>`) and `<name>.timer` (`OnCalendar=*-*-* *:25:00`, `Persistent=true`), `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now <name>.timer`, and check `systemctl --user list-timers`. Measured: the first run copied and matched all 53 files busan lists. Disk there was 851 GB free. Make any ssh key such a job needs on nj2 itself (`ssh-keygen` there) and pin it with `restrict,command=…` on the far side, so the private key is never copied between machines.

## OPS-645 — A `fetch()` whose response body is never read keeps Playwright's `networkidle` from ever firing; the request never "finishes"

`측정 2026-10-25 · Brave 1.98 (Chromium) headless · playwright-core 1.64 · Astro 7 node adapter`

**증상:** after a page started to POST once at load (`fetch('/api/x',{method:'POST',body})`, the promise used but the response never read), every `page.goto(url,{waitUntil:'networkidle'})` on that page timed out at 30 s, in suites that had passed for days. `page.on('response')` fired at once with 200; `requestfinished` never fired for that request, so Playwright counted it as in flight forever. `keepalive: true` was the first suspect and was not the cause: without it the same thing happened.

**해결:** always consume the body (`.then(r=>r.text())` or `r.json()`, or `r.body?.cancel()`). The request then finishes and `networkidle` comes as before. To find such a request: log `request`, `response` and `requestfinished` for the page; the culprit has a response and no finish.

## OPS-646 — Put a URL into a QR code in upper case: the alphanumeric mode fits a 47-character link in version 4 (33 modules) instead of version 6 (41) at level H

`측정 2026-10-25 · qrcode-generator 1.4.4 · jsqr 1.4.0 · Apple Vision (VNDetectBarcodesRequest) on macOS 26.6 · Brave 1.98`

**증상:** a short link `https://cuckoo-qr.chowooick.workers.dev/q/ab12c` (47 characters) in byte mode needed version 6 at level H (byte capacity: v4-H 34, v5-H 44, v6-H 58), 41×41 modules, too dense for an 84 px stamp on a desktop page.

QR alphanumeric mode holds `0-9 A-Z space $ % * + - . / :` at 5.5 bits a character, so the same link upper-cased (`HTTPS://CUCKOO-QR.CHOWOOICK.WORKERS.DEV/Q/AB12C`) fits version 4 (alphanumeric v4-H holds 50), 33×33. A 35-character `https://pa.cuckoorental.com/q/ab12c` goes to version 3 (29×29). Scheme and host are case-insensitive; the path is not, so the server must accept the token in either case and lower-case it.

**해결:** `q.addData(url.toUpperCase(),'Alphanumeric')` when the upper-cased URL matches `^[0-9A-Z $%*+\-./:]*$`, and match the token with `/i`. Checked: jsQR and Apple Vision (OPS-365) read every visible code, including a version-4 code drawn as rounded squares (OPS-621) at 84 CSS px and one rotated 6°; both return the upper-case text, and a browser opens it.

## OPS-647 — A popover opened from inside a modal `<dialog>` but living outside it is inert: it shows on top, yet nothing in it can be clicked

`측정 2026-10-25 · Brave 1.98 (Chromium) · Popover API (popover="manual") · showModal()`

**증상:** a QR panel (`popover="manual"`, appended to `<body>`) opened by a phone link inside an open modal order dialog was drawn above the dialog (top layer, opened later), but `document.elementFromPoint` at its centre returned the dialog's backdrop, and its close button could not be clicked or focused. `showModal()` makes everything outside the dialog inert, top layer or not.

**해결:** before `showPopover()`, move the popover into the dialog that holds its opener (`(opener.closest('dialog')||document.body).appendChild(panel)`; hide it first if it is open, since moving an open popover closes it). Inside the dialog it is not inert and still opens above it. The dialog's own type rules then apply to the popover's headings and paragraphs (`.order-dialog h2{…}`), so give the popover's text rules a selector at least as specific (`.panel .title`).

## OPS-648 — The shared nj2 Dokploy key (`~/.config/dokploy/nj2.key`) can run out of calls for the day; the next call of any session is `401 Unauthorized`

`측정 2026-10-25 · Dokploy on nj2 · key file dated 2026-10-24 22:04 (local)`

**증상:** `application.dropDeployment` for one service returned `true` at 20:47:18Z; the same call for a second service nine seconds later, and every call after (`project.all` included), returned `401 {"message":"Unauthorized"}`. The key is shared by the docs of at least seven projects (battris, cuckoo, darklord, dungeonpop, fake, papa, threekingdom). This matches OPS-424 (a key created through `user.createApiKey` gets better-auth's default limit of 10 calls a day and then answers 401, not 429). The account `chowooick` on nj2 has no docker access, so the `apikey` row cannot be fixed from there.

**해결:** spend no calls on probing: make the real call the probe and retry it on a long interval (CUCKOO: `deploy-cuckoo2-when-key-works.sh`, every 30 minutes for 25 hours). Put sessions that deploy two services from one release first in line for the day's calls, or remove the limit for good from `dokploy-postgres` (`update apikey set rate_limit_enabled=false, request_count=0 where …`, OPS-424); that needs someone with docker on nj2.

**갱신 (2026-10-26, better-auth 1.3.27 source · Dokploy on nj2):** the window is counted from `lastRequest`, which only a *successful* call moves (`isRateLimited` returns `update: null` when it refuses). So the key comes back exactly 24 h after its 10th successful call (here 2026-10-26T20:47:18Z), no matter how many 401s came in between; probing every 30 minutes neither helps nor hurts. With the reset key, a new key without the limit was made over REST with `x-api-key` alone (no panel, no password): `GET /api/organization.all`, then `POST /api/user.createApiKey` with `{"name":"…","metadata":{"organizationId":"<id>"},"rateLimitEnabled":false}`. The reply still says `rateLimitMax: 10` but `rateLimitEnabled: false`; the new key answered 12 calls in a row. The key is in the reply's `key`; write it straight to the file (mode 600), never print it. `~/.config/dokploy/nj2.key` now holds that key; the old one is `nj2.key.old-20261026`.

## OPS-649 — Cloudflare's login page hides "Sign in with Google" when the visitor's IP is in Korea; open `oidc.iam.cfapi.net/api/v1/sso/init?client=google` directly

`측정 2026-10-26 · dash.cloudflare.com/login · Brave 1.98 (Chromium 156) via Playwright on busan.mac (Korean IP), profile copied from ~/kc-test/profile`

**증상:** on a host in Korea the login page showed only email and password (and 「가입」); no Google, Apple or GitHub button,
in English and in Korean, before and after typing the email. `https://dash.cloudflare.com/login/google` redirected back
to `/login`. The same profile family on a US host had shown 「chowooick@gmail.com 계정으로 Google 사용하여 계속」 (OPS-399,
OPS-474). The page script decides it: `N0=e=>!(globalThis?.bootstrap?.ip_country==='KR'||…)`. An account that only
signs in with Google cannot sign in there at all through the page.

**해결:** go straight to the URL the hidden button would open:
`https://oidc.iam.cfapi.net/api/v1/sso/init?client=google&env=production&login_hint=<email>`. With a profile already
signed in to Google it returned to `https://dash.cloudflare.com/` signed in, with no clicks; `GET /api/v4/memberships`
from the page then answered 200. `client=apple` and `client=github` are the other values the script uses.

## OPS-650 — A Cloudflare login at its account-creation limit had five additional accounts, two of them empty and unrecorded; list the accounts after a 422

`측정 2026-10-26 · dash.cloudflare.com (ko UI), account switcher → 「계정 생성」 · one login, six accounts`

**증상:** 「계정 생성」 answered `POST /api/v4/accounts` → **422** `{"code":1206,"message":"The standalone free account
creation limit has been reached"}`; the dialog said 「생성할 수 있는 계정 수의 한도에 도달했습니다」. `GET /accounts` listed
six accounts: the original plus five created between 2026-10-19 15:43 and 2026-10-20 01:37 UTC. That is the "five
additional Free accounts" of the official "Create account" page; OPS-528 counted three. Two of the five
(`withthebible.com` 05b8049b…, created 01:36:43, and `kyominmart.com` 1d5bc010…, 01:37:06) held no zone, Worker, D1, KV,
Pages project, registration or API token, and the session's notes did not mention them; they were created in the minute
when that session recorded every creation as failed. A second account with an existing name is accepted, so two
accounts can carry the same name.

**해결:** after any failed or batch account creation, read `GET /api/v4/accounts?per_page=50` (works from a signed-in
dashboard page, OPS-301) and compare names and `created_on` with your notes before calling the limit reached. Empty
accounts are free slots: rename one (`PUT /accounts/:id {"name": …}`, OPS-528) instead of waiting for a new one.

## OPS-651 — A CNAME from another DNS host to a proxied hostname of a Cloudflare zone gives Error 1001 until that zone lists it as a custom hostname

`측정 2026-10-26 · Cloudflare for SaaS on zone mnori.com · cloudflared remote-managed tunnel`

**증상:** `888.cuckoorental.com` (DNS at GoDaddy) was made a CNAME of `cuckoo2.mnori.com`, a proxied record on Cloudflare pointing at a Cloudflare Tunnel. DNS resolved to Cloudflare's addresses, but every request returned **Error 1001 "DNS resolution error"** ("Cloudflare is currently unable to resolve your requested domain"). Cloudflare does not follow a foreign hostname into a zone that has not claimed it.

**해결:** two calls, no change at the other DNS host:
1. `POST /zones/<zone>/custom_hostnames` with `{"hostname":"888.cuckoorental.com","ssl":{"method":"http","type":"dv","settings":{"min_tls_version":"1.2"}}}` (the zone needs Cloudflare for SaaS and a fallback origin). With the CNAME already live, the hostname was `active` within about 20 s and the certificate within about 2 minutes (HTTP validation).
2. If the origin is a tunnel, add an ingress rule for the new hostname (`PUT /accounts/<acct>/cfd_tunnel/<id>/configurations`, whole config, rule before the final `http_status:404`). Requests keep the visitor's `Host`, so without the rule they fall through to the 404 rule even though the fallback origin is right. Then the page answered 200.

## OPS-652 — macOS glab keeps its existing OAuth credentials in Library/Application Support, not necessarily ~/.config/glab-cli

`측정 2026-10-26 · macOS controller + busan.mac · GitLab API v4 · Node 26.12.1`

**증상:** GitLab SSH from busan.mac (including the controller's forwarded identity) returned `Permission denied (publickey)`; HTTPS credential lookup returned `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://gitlab.com': terminal prompts disabled`. `~/.config/glab-cli/config.yml` did not exist on the controller. This did not mean there was no usable existing authorization: the config was at `~/Library/Application Support/glab-cli/config.yml`, under `hosts.gitlab.com`, with `token`, `oauth2_refresh_token`, and `oauth2_expiry_date`. Its access token was expired (API 401).

**해결:** read the existing config through SSH stdin into a mode-0600 file outside the remote source tree; refresh its OAuth token on the designated test host as in OPS-526, then verify authenticated `GET /api/v4/user` (200). A temporary Git credential helper that returns username `oauth2` and the refreshed token allowed HTTPS source push without another browser login. Preserve both the rotated refresh token and expiry in the original config, checking the original file's SHA-256 against the snapshot before the write to avoid overwriting another session's credential update. Never print token values or put them in a remote URL; delete temporary copies and helpers after pushing.

## OPS-653 — Cloudflare Web Analytics injects a newline with its beacon; removing the script alone leaves a false HTML mismatch

\`측정 2026-10-26 · Cloudflare proxied HTML / Web Analytics · Python 3.9 urllib\`

**증상:** a deployed standalone HTML report differed from its committed source even after removing the injected script whose tag contains \`data-cf-beacon\`. A character-level diff showed exactly one extra LF before \`</body>\`: source had \`</div>\n</body>\`, normalized response had \`</div>\n\n</body>\`. Trimming only the document's outer whitespace did not fix this internal difference. All report text and authored scripts were identical.

**해결:** exclude the CDN-injected analytics script **and its following optional CRLF/LF**, then compare the rest of the HTML. The measured pattern was \`<script\b[^>]*\bdata-cf-beacon\b[^>]*>.*?</script>(?:\r?\n)?\` with DOTALL. Compare CSS, JavaScript, fonts and other binary files byte-for-byte; do not collapse whitespace throughout authored HTML just to make a mismatch disappear.

## OPS-654 — Proxied Dokploy ZIP uploads can fail at socket write with Broken pipe; check deployment history before retrying

`측정 2026-10-26 · nj2 Dokploy application.dropDeployment · macOS Python 3.9.6 urllib · Cloudflare-proxied panel`

**증상:** A 106,272,766-byte (101.35 MiB) committed ZIP failed in urllib's HTTP request write with
URLError: <urlopen error [Errno 32] Broken pipe>. No HTTP status was captured, and deployment.all
showed no new deployment afterward; ordinary API calls still returned 200. A later header-only
Expect: 100-continue probe timed out, so it did not establish a 413 response or prove the failure's
exact cause.

**해결:** Check the archive size and deployment history before retrying this ambiguous write failure.
The same helper successfully uploaded a 102,189,306-byte (97.46 MiB) archive and received true.
Committed .gitattributes export-ignore rules removed docs/tests and duplicate licensed font files;
the committed Dockerfile restored those fonts from identical existing bytes before build.
All nine runtime report files were compared against source, including the reconstructed fonts.
Guard the release size before POST; never omit required runtime assets without reconstructing and
checking them. The measurements support keeping this panel's release archive below 100 MiB, not
treating every Broken pipe as proof of a size limit.

## OPS-655 — Uppercase QR encoding also changes the route prefix; replay the scanner text unchanged in end-to-end tests

`측정 2026-10-26 · Astro 7.3.3 standalone Node · qrcode-generator 1.4.4 · Brave on busan.mac`

**증상:** With an Astro standalone route /q/[token], a QR optimized using url.toUpperCase() encoded
/Q/ABCDE. Decoding succeeded, but opening that exact URL returned 404. Opening the lowercase route
worked. Lowercasing only params.token in the endpoint cannot help because the uppercase prefix
does not match the route. The old browser helper called decodedUrl.toLowerCase() before navigation,
so it passed while masking the actual scanner path failure.

**해결:** Treat OPS-646's uppercase/alphanumeric optimization as requiring matching routing support
for the entire QR path, not just a case-insensitive token. A dedicated GET/HEAD /Q/[token] redirect
to the lowercase /q/[token] route preserved the compact QR and restored the phone hand-off.
Limit normalization to the known QR path; do not lowercase arbitrary application paths or signed
query values. The corrected browser check opened the exact decoded QR string, reached the
intended phone page and observed the computer's opened state. Decoding alone, or replaying a
modified URL, is not an end-to-end scan check.


## OPS-656 — A classic script under Astro public/ can pollute application TypeScript globals when tsconfig includes **/*

`측정 2026-10-26 · Astro 7.3.3 · @astrojs/check 0.9.9 · TypeScript 5.9.3 · macOS busan.mac`

**증상:** a standalone design prototype in `public/reports/` passed browser checks and `astro build`, but `astro check` then reported 109 errors in unchanged application scripts. A prototype's top-level `form()` (returns HTML text), `$` and `$$` became ambient declarations because it was a classic JavaScript file and the project's strict tsconfig included `**/*`. Existing code calling `form('passport')` was inferred as a string: `Expected 0 arguments, but got 1`, `Property 'addEventListener' does not exist on type 'string'`, and `Argument of type 'string' is not assignable to parameter of type 'HTMLFormElement'`. Being a static public asset did not exclude it from the checker's input.

**해결:** give the independent browser file module scope with `export {};` and load it using `<script type="module" src="…"></script>`. Changing only that prototype script and its five HTML entry points restored the 733-file check to 0 errors and 0 warnings; all 115 interaction checks still passed. Check newly added public JavaScript for ambient names before changing unrelated application code or suppressing the diagnostics.

## OPS-657 — `wrangler dev` with `"ai": { "binding": "AI", "remote": true }` will not start over ssh: it needs a remote proxy session; a copy of the config without the `ai` line runs everything else locally

`측정 2026-10-25 · wrangler 4.135.0 · Workers + D1 local · busan.mac over ssh, wrangler logged in to several accounts`

**증상:** `npx wrangler dev --port N --local-upstream 127.0.0.1:N` exits before serving with `Failed to start the remote proxy session. Error reloading remote server: More than one account available but unable to select one in non-interactive mode.` Setting `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` only changes the error to `A request to the Cloudflare API (/accounts/<id>/workers/subdomain/edge-preview) failed.` Every page then answers nothing (curl `000`), so a browser test fails at its first `goto`. Workers AI exists only remotely, so a `remote: true` AI binding makes `wrangler dev` open a remote proxy even when no request uses it. Same cause as OPS-457 (astro), different tool.

**해결:** on the test host only, write a copy without the AI line and point dev at it: `grep -v '"ai": {' wrangler.jsonc > wrangler.qa.jsonc; npx wrangler dev -c wrangler.qa.jsonc ...`. D1 `--local` state is shared with the normal config (same `.wrangler` directory), so `wrangler d1 execute ... -c wrangler.qa.jsonc --local` seeds the same database. `env.AI` is absent there; code paths that call it must be off or mocked. Do not commit the copy.


## OPS-658 — Playwright isVisible() passes for a fixed control translated entirely below the viewport

`측정 2026-10-27 · Playwright 1.64.1 · Brave headless on busan.mac · CSS individual translate`

**증상:** A fixed QR stamp had `is-tuck` after an IntersectionObserver saw the footer. At a 1440×900 viewport,
`locator.isVisible()` returned true while boundingBox was x=-55.245, y=910.538, width=121.772,
height=151.462: every pixel was below the screen. A DOM-presence/visibility regression therefore missed a
customer-visible disappearance. Focusing it added `is-big` without clearing `is-tuck`; aria-expanded was
true while the enlarged stamp remained clipped (x=-45.2, y=814.32, height=247.68).

**해결:** For a fixed floating control, intersect its bounding rectangle with the viewport and hit-test visible
pixels using document.elementFromPoint; opening it must also fit the complete QR inside the viewport.
Recompute footer and expanded state together instead of waiting for another footer observer event. The
regression now checks the visible peek, hover, Escape, keyboard focus over the footer, return to top,
and 320–1440 CSS-pixel resizes. Measured artifact: cuckoo-rental-america commit 63fc123,
docs/qa/stamp-recovery-20261027/diagnosis.json; tests/stamp-recovery-browser.mjs.


## OPS-659 — QR short links use the displayed hostname: excluding an alias from uppercase-route repair leaves that alias broken

`측정 2026-10-27 · Astro 7.3.3 · Brave / Playwright 1.64.1 on busan.mac`

**증상:** QR generation used location.origin, but both the stamp repair and /Q/ middleware were guarded by an
exact cuckoo2.mnori.com allowlist. The owner actually used 888.cuckoorental.com, served by the same service.
On that hostname /ko had reliableStamp:false; /Q/7DY16 returned 404 (Cloudflare DYNAMIC), while /q/7dy16
returned 200 after an expired-token redirect. A passing literal-QR test on the canonical hostname did not
exercise the owner's alias.

**해결:** Give stamp routing/display its own hostname scope, including the real alias, without broadening chat,
report or administrator permissions. Run the browser using the actual hostname even in isolated QA
(Chromium --host-resolver-rules with the isolated server port); decode and open the QR unchanged on that
hostname, then check the exact destination, repeat scans, and post-install visibility. Test GET and HEAD
uppercase redirects for each host/service pair and preserve opaque query text. Measured fix:
cuckoo-rental-america 4fe3464, tests/stamp-888-browser.mjs and tests/stamp-domain.test.ts.


## OPS-660 — Astro dev's error overlay can block unrelated Playwright clicks after a background D1 API error; migrate every exercised local binding and restart the isolated dev server

`측정 2026-10-27 · Astro 7.3.3 · Wrangler 4.x · Playwright 1.63.0 · Brave on busan.mac`

**증상:** a signed-in local page returned 200 and exposed the expected article links, but a browser test timed out after 150 seconds at `locator.click`. The trace said `<vite-error-overlay dir="ltr"></vite-error-overlay> intercepts pointer events`. The isolated D1 state had no regional schema at first (`D1_ERROR: no such table: region_records: SQLITE_ERROR`); after MEMBERS migrations, background beta feedback requests still hit another unmigrated binding. A page can render normally while this dev overlay intercepts every click. Reading the page DOM or counting its links does not prove that it is clickable.

**해결:** apply the project migrations with `wrangler d1 migrations apply <binding> --local` inside the isolated directory for each binding the page and background scripts exercise (here MEMBERS, BETA, COUPONS and ANALYTICS), then restart only that directory's dev server to clear prior overlay state. Keep local state isolated and never add `--remote` for these fixtures. The same automatic-turn desktop/mobile tests then passed in 33.8s / 11.6s without forced clicks or overlay removal.


## OPS-661 — HTML design reports tested through a plain static server can pass locally while every production preview iframe is blocked by the private wrapper's X-Frame-Options

`측정 2026-10-27 · Astro 7.3.3 · Wrangler 4.135.0 · Brave on busan.mac · Cloudflare Workers private asset wrapper`

**증상:** a 24-page static report passed 120 local viewport/theme cases and its HTML/CSS/JS matched production. In authenticated production, the report and preview HTML carried `X-Frame-Options: DENY`; all 16 same-origin preview iframes became `chrome-error` frames. Brave logged 16 framing errors. The local Python static server did not send the production wrapper's headers, so it could not expose the failure. Being on the same origin does not override DENY.

**해결:** retain the private boundary and render the report's preview areas as verified browser captures linking to standalone interactive prototype pages. Verify the production response headers and actual image/frame content in a signed-in browser, in addition to file hashes and local viewport checks. If embedded frames are required in another project, exercise its real production header policy before choosing that presentation structure.

## OPS-662 — Chromium now has DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission, and Playwright's orientation override sends nulls until the sensor permissions are granted

`측정 2026-10-27 · Brave 1.98 (Chromium 156) · playwright-core on busan.mac · mobile emulation (isMobile, hasTouch)`

**증상:** a page that listened for `deviceorientation` only when `typeof DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission !== "function"` (the usual "iOS asks, Android does not" test) never listened in Brave: `typeof DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission` is `"function"` there too. Separately, `DeviceOrientation.setDeviceOrientationOverride({ alpha, beta, gamma })` over CDP delivered events whose `beta` and `gamma` were `null`.

**해결:** do not use the presence of `requestPermission` to tell iOS from Android. Add the listener unconditionally (iOS sends no readings until permission is granted, so it costs nothing) and call `requestPermission()` from a tap only while no reading has arrived. In Playwright, call `context.grantPermissions(['accelerometer', 'gyroscope', 'magnetometer'])` before the override; then `beta`/`gamma` arrive as set.

## OPS-663 — CDP touch emulation does not reproduce the real-phone "scroll that first pushes" bug on touch-driven canvases

`측정 2026-10-27 · Brave 1.98 (Chromium 156) · Input.dispatchTouchEvent and Input.synthesizeScrollGesture, 390×844 mobile emulation, CPU throttle 4×`

**증상:** on real phones, a vertical swipe that starts on a canvas with `touch-action: pan-y` delivers a few `pointermove` events before `pointercancel`, and a physics toy that pushes objects on `pointermove` visibly nudges them while the page scrolls. In emulation, a 220 px vertical `dispatchTouchEvent` drag starting on the canvas scrolled the page 205 px and moved 0 objects, both before and after the fix; a sideways drag moved 18–24. Frame timings under 4× throttling on an M4 Pro (p95 18.5 ms) also did not show the jank owners saw on their phones.

**해결:** treat emulation as unable to prove or disprove this class of bug. Fix it from the event model (ignore touch moves until about 10 px of movement shows a mostly sideways direction; drop the pointer on `pointercancel` at once) and confirm on a real device (`adb` with Chrome remote debugging, or Safari Web Inspector on an iPhone).

## OPS-664 — Play Console payout bank verification: the deposit-amount field is under the developer account's payments profile, not pay.google.com

`측정 2026-10-27 · Play Console web (ko UI), organization account with a separate business payments profile · Google Payments embedded pages`

**증상:** a Korean bank account added as the payout method shows 「확인 대기중」 and Play Console warns
`결제하거나 대금을 받으려면 은행 계좌 •••• NNN의 인증을 완료하세요.` Opening `pay.google.com/gp/w/u/0/home/paymentmethods`
in the same signed-in browser showed `결제 수단이 아직 없으신가요?`: it opens the Google account's personal
payments profile, not the business profile linked to the developer account.

**사실:**
- The business profile is reached at `play.google.com/console/u/0/developers/<developer id>/paymentssettings`
  (계정 관리 → 「결제 프로필 페이지 보기」). Its content sits in iframes from `payments.google.com`
  (`embedded_landing_page`, then `payment_methods`, then `instrumentmanager` for the dialog); Playwright
  must search `page.frames()`, the top page text has only the warning.
- 결제 수단 관리 → the account card's 「확인」 opens 「은행 입금액 확인」, which names the day Google sent the
  test deposit (`…에 10월 26일경에 입금된 GOOGLE 입금액을 입력하세요.`) and has one ₩ field.
  The account had been added on 2026-10-26, so the deposit went out the same day.
- The same page carries the 15% service-fee tier offer, which needs an account group and acceptance of
  the fee terms; it is not applied automatically.

**해결:** read the amount from the bank statement, open the dialog through the developer account's
`paymentssettings` page and enter it there. Do not guess amounts.


## OPS-665 — glab fails every command with "parsing time … as \"02 Jan 06 15:04 MST\"" after something rewrote its OAuth expiry in ISO format

`측정 2026-10-27 · glab 1.82.0 · macOS, ~/Library/Application Support/glab-cli/config.yml`

**증상:** every `glab` command, including `glab ci list`, printed `Failed to initialize auth source: parsing time "2026-10-27T09:23:46.000Z" as "02 Jan 06 15:04 MST": cannot parse "26-10-27T09:23:46.000Z" as " "` and exited. The config's `oauth2_expiry_date` held an ISO 8601 timestamp; glab 1.82 reads only the RFC 822 form it writes itself.

**해결:** back up the config and rewrite that one value in glab's own form, e.g. `oauth2_expiry_date: 27 Oct 26 09:23 UTC`. glab then sees the token as expired, refreshes it with the stored refresh token and works (`glab ci list` and `glab api` answered at once). Do not print the token values while editing.

## OPS-666 — Next.js 16 `RouteContext` fails a CI that runs `tsc --noEmit` before any `next build` or `next typegen`

`측정 2026-10-27 · Next.js 16.3.2 · GitLab CI verify job (npm run typecheck = tsc --noEmit, then build)`

**증상:** a route handler typed `ctx: RouteContext<"/api/qr/[token]">`, as the Next 16 docs show, passed `tsc` locally (where `next dev`/`next build` had generated `.next/types`) and failed CI with `error TS2304: Cannot find name 'RouteContext'`: the global type exists only after Next has generated its types.

**해결:** type the context by hand, `ctx: { params: Promise<{ token: string }> }`, or run `next typegen` before `tsc` in CI. To reproduce locally, delete `.next/types` and `.next/dev/types` before `tsc --noEmit`.

## OPS-667 — A small element with a width transition, painted in a big layer, checkerboards the scroll on Android Chrome; its own layer stops it

`측정 2026-10-27 · Pixel 7 Pro (120 Hz), Chrome over adb remote debugging · cc PipelineReporter in a CDP trace, real swipes with adb shell input swipe`

**증상:** on a page whose first screen holds a speech capsule that animates its `width` (a layout transition) as each line arrives, three fling-scrolls during the entrance showed 33–59 frames with `checkerboarded_needs_raster` (blank tiles) in `PipelineReporter` (`args.frame_reporter`). Hiding parts of the page with injected `visibility: hidden` isolated it: hiding the canvas animation halved it, but hiding only the capsule, or disabling only its width transition, brought it to 0–1. CDP emulation on a desktop could not show any of this.

**해결:** give the animating element its own compositing layer (`will-change: transform` on its small absolutely positioned container): 0 checkerboarded frames in the same test, with the animation unchanged. To find such causes, count `PipelineReporter` begin events whose `scroll_state` is not `SCROLL_NONE`, by `state` and `checkerboarded_needs_raster`, across CSS variants injected with `page.addStyleTag`. On Android 14+, `dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --latency` returns nothing for Chrome's BLAST SurfaceView, so use the trace.

## OPS-668 — Google account photos: real ones (`lh3…/a-/…`) carry no CORS header, so a canvas cannot read them; accounts without a picture get a generated letter image

`측정 2026-10-27 · lh3.googleusercontent.com · Firebase Auth user.photoURL · Brave 156 · nginx 1.28 · blabla`

**증상:** a web game drew the signed-in account's `photoURL` into a canvas (`img.crossOrigin='anonymous'`) to hand the pixels to the engine. It worked in tests with `https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/default-user=s96-c` (answers `access-control-allow-origin: *`) and failed in production: the real photo URL (`/a-/ALV-Uj…=s96-c`) answers 200 `image/png` with only `access-control-expose-headers`, no `access-control-allow-origin`, so the browser logs `Access to image … has been blocked by CORS policy` and `fetch()` fails the same way. A second surprise: an account with no picture still has a `photoURL`; the image is Google's generated initial (white letter on one flat colour), so "show the photo instead of a letter" shows a letter again.

- The size suffix can be rewritten (`=s160-c`, `=s400-c`); the path without it is the photo id.
- A generated initial is recognisable in the page: draw it at 32×32 and every pixel is a blend between the corner colour and white (per-channel `(p-bg)/(255-bg)` within 0.12 of each other). Measured: the generated "W" true; Google's default silhouette, a game screenshot and an app icon false.

**해결:** relay the photo through the site's own origin and read it there. nginx: `location ~ "^/photo/(a-?/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,2048}=s[0-9]{2,3}-c)$" { resolver 127.0.0.11 ipv6=off; proxy_pass https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/$1; proxy_ssl_server_name on; proxy_set_header Host lh3.googleusercontent.com; proxy_set_header Cookie ""; proxy_hide_header Set-Cookie; expires 1d; }` (a variable in `proxy_pass` needs a `resolver`; `127.0.0.11` is Docker's DNS). Check the config before deploying in a throwaway container on the compose network (`docker run --rm --network <app>_default -v conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro nginx:1.28-alpine nginx -t`), because a static `proxy_pass http://<service>` elsewhere in the file only resolves there. Treat a generated initial like a missing photo.

## OPS-669 — SpacetimeDB 2.8: a view's `Vec` order is lost over HTTP SQL, a view needs `<table>__view` in scope for tables of another module, and owner `UPDATE` is a usable test lever

`측정 2026-10-27 · SpacetimeDB 2.8.0 standalone · Rust module · spacetime CLI sql · blabla weekly league`

**증상:** three things while adding a leaderboard view.

- `SELECT * FROM my_league` over `/v1/database/<db>/sql` returned the view's rows in a different order from the `Vec` the view built (rank 2 first). A test that read `rows[0]` as first place passed once and failed the next run. Return an explicit `rank` column and sort on the client.
- In a view (`ViewContext`), `ctx.db.player_directory()` for a table declared in a sibling module failed with `E0599 no method named player_directory found for struct LocalReadOnly`; `use crate::admin::player_directory as _;` (the reducer trait) is not enough. The compiler's hint is right: `use crate::admin::player_directory__view as _;`.
- `spacetime sql --server http://127.0.0.1:<port> <db> "UPDATE league_clock SET week = 2964, day = 20753 WHERE id = 0"` works for the database owner (the CLI identity that published), commits like a reducer, and pushes the change to subscribers. That is enough to make a scheduled reducer see "next Monday" in a test without a clock hook in the module. Updating a column does not rename a string primary key built from it; delete such rows afterwards or later inserts with the same key hit the old row.

**해결:** sort view output by a column, import the `__view` trait for cross-module tables in views, and use owner SQL `UPDATE`/`INSERT`/`DELETE` on a private local database to stage time-based states.

## OPS-670 — Cloudflare's 4 h browser TTL on unversioned page scripts: a new release ran the previous `auth.js` until each script URL carried a content hash

`측정 2026-10-27 · Cloudflare free plan, zone browser cache TTL 4시간 · nginx `expires -1` origin · Brave 156 persistent profile · blabla`

**증상:** after a deploy that changed `auth.js`, `curl` got the new file (`cf-cache-status: REVALIDATED`) but a Brave profile that had loaded the site an hour earlier kept running the old one: the response it had cached said `cache-control: max-age=14400` although nginx sends `no-cache` (OPS-375). The new engine build called a function the old script did not have.

**해결:** keep `index.html` uncached (Cloudflare leaves HTML `DYNAMIC`) and write every page script and stylesheet into it as `name.js?v=<sha256 prefix of the file>` at build time. The next load of the page fetched `auth.js?v=c539d7ae8d` and the fix was live in the same profile at once.


## OPS-671 — Forwarding an SSH agent to the test host does not load the repository host's controller-side IdentityFile; use a short-lived transport agent with that registered key

`측정 2026-10-27 · Git 2.54.0 · macOS OpenSSH · GitLab over agent forwarding to busan.mac`

**증상:** `ssh -A busan.mac` followed by `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` answered `git@gitlab.com: Permission denied (publickey).` Adding `-o AddKeysToAgent=yes` to the test-host connection did not fix it. The controller's `ssh -G gitlab.com` named a different `IdentityFile` from the key used to reach the test host; that GitLab identity was not loaded into the forwarded agent. This was not loss of repository access.

**해결:** inspect the repository host's SSH config before changing credentials. For a task-scoped transport, run `ssh-agent sh -c 'ssh-add -q <configured-key> && ssh -A <test-host> <remote-git-command>'`; Git itself still runs on the test host, and the private key remains on the controller. This successfully read the GitLab main ref and pushed the owner's explicitly approved fast-forward. The temporary agent exits with its command, without changing the user's existing agent or GitLab credentials.

## OPS-672 — Playwright `page.route` stops seeing a page's reloads once its service worker controls the page; a mocked server-rendered list silently reverts

`측정 2026-10-27 · Playwright 1.63.0 · Brave 1.98 (Chromium 156) · astro dev · a site that registers /sw.js`

**증상:** a test fixture rewrote the HTML of `/la/stories?tab=tips` through `page.route` so the page embedded test rows. The first `page.goto` got the rewritten document; the `page.reload()` right after it got the server's original HTML (`DOC 200 … []` in a `page.on('response')` log), and the test failed on `toHaveCount(1)` with the list empty. The response headers were `Cache-Control: private, no-store` with no ETag, so it was not the HTTP cache. The page had registered its service worker during the first visit; from then on the worker fetched navigations itself, and Playwright's page routes do not see requests a service worker makes.

**해결:** `use: { serviceWorkers: 'block' }` in `playwright.config.ts` (or per context) for suites that mock pages or APIs with `page.route`; test the worker itself in a separate project that allows it. In one suite this alone turned five "flaky after reload" story-room tests green.

## OPS-673 — Android: Chrome's own notification permission off makes every site tab report `Notification.permission === 'denied'`, but an installed WebAPK of the site has its own permission and can still ask

`측정 2026-10-27 · Pixel 7 Pro (Android 17) · Chrome 156.0.8078.47 · site WebAPK org.chromium.webapk.*_v2`

**증상:** on a test phone, a site's "알림 받기" switch in a Chrome tab showed the browser-blocked state; `Notification.permission` was `denied` without the site ever having asked. `adb shell dumpsys package com.android.chrome | grep POST_NOTIFICATIONS` showed `granted=false, flags=[USER_SET|USER_FIXED…]`: the phone's owner had turned off notifications for Chrome itself. The same site's installed app (a WebAPK, started with `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d <url> <webapk package>`) reported `default`, and pressing the switch there showed Android's own prompt titled with the app's name ("교민센터 뉴저지에서 알림을 보내도록 허용하시겠습니까?"). After 허용, a Web Push arrived as a notification of the WebAPK package (`dumpsys notification --noredact | grep <package>`), even with the app closed.

**해결:** when a site's notification test fails on a real Android phone, check both packages' `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` first: `dumpsys package com.android.chrome` and each `org.chromium.webapk.*` (find the site's by the `Authority: "<host>"` line in `dumpsys package <pkg>`). Test push in the WebAPK if Chrome's is user-fixed off; do not flip the owner's Chrome permission. Afterwards restore the WebAPK with `pm revoke <pkg> android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS` and `pm clear-permission-flags <pkg> android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS user-set user-fixed` if it was unset before (verified the same day: the flags read back as before). Signing in to the site inside the WebAPK works: the Google account chooser opens as a sheet listing the device accounts, and the app returns signed in.

## OPS-674 — `sqlite3` CLI errors repeat the failing SQL text: a secret interpolated into a query is printed when the query fails

`측정 2026-10-27 · SQLite 3.45 CLI (Ubuntu 24.04) and macOS /usr/bin/sqlite3`

**증상:** a check meant to print only a count, `sqlite3 data.db "select count(*) from t where listRule like \"%$KEY%\" or authRule like \"%$KEY%\""`, failed on a missing column and answered `Error: in prepare, no such column: authRule` followed by the statement around the error position, with a caret line: about 56 of the key's 64 hex characters were in the output. A `sed` meant to mask quoted values in a printed rule (`s/"[^"]{20,}"/"<KEY>"/g`) also leaked the key, because the rule's escaped quotes shifted the match.

**해결:** never put a secret in SQL text, a command line or a masking regex whose failure prints its input. Read the secret inside a small script from a file and print only derived numbers (counts, `sha256` prefixes); compare values by hash. If a secret was printed anyway, treat it as exposed and rotate it, including a not-yet-deployed replacement.

## OPS-675 — Chrome on Android paints an installed web app's (WebAPK) navigation bar with the manifest `theme_color`; `viewport-fit=cover` does not draw the page behind it

`측정 2026-10-27 · Pixel 7 Pro (Android 17, gesture navigation) · Chrome 156.0.8078.47 · site WebAPK, display: standalone`

**증상:** with the phone in dark theme, an installed site app showed a white band with a grey gesture handle under its dark bottom tab bar (bottom rows of a `screencap` were `(255,255,255)`). The manifest had `theme_color: "#ffffff"`. Adding `viewport-fit=cover` to the page changed nothing in the app: `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` measured 0 inside it (a `position:fixed; height: env(...)` probe), and the band stayed white. The status bar at the top does follow the page's `<meta name="theme-color">`; the bottom bar does not. Chrome's own edge-to-edge guidance (Chrome 135+) is about browser tabs.

**해결:** for the installed app, choose the manifest `theme_color` as the colour you want under the bottom bar; there is one value for both themes, so pick the theme most users run. Keep `viewport-fit=cover` with `env(safe-area-inset-*)` padding for tabs and iOS. Chrome applies a changed `theme_color` only when it next checks the app's manifest (about daily) or after a reinstall. Playwright can emulate insets with CDP `Emulation.setSafeAreaInsetsOverride` (`{ insets: { bottom: 34 } }`), which works in Brave 1.98 / Chromium 156.

## OPS-676 — Rebuilding Astro output under an existing Wrangler dev server can leave built scripts and images answering 404; restart the isolated server after the build

`측정 2026-10-27 · Astro 7.3.3 · Wrangler 4.125.0 · Brave on busan.mac`

**증상:** an isolated `wrangler dev` served a built Astro application from `dist/server/wrangler.json`. After `npm run build` replaced the output while that process remained running, the HTML still answered 200, but hashed `/_astro/*.js`, images and even the public favicon answered `404 Not Found`. No page JavaScript exception was raised because the modules never loaded; a test waiting for client initialization timed out. Authentication was not the explanation: the public favicon also failed. The same build worked after restarting only that task's Wrangler process.

**해결:** complete the build, restart the owned Wrangler dev process with the same isolated config and persistence directory, and wait for a known static asset to answer 200 before running browser checks. When a document renders but its client controls never initialize, inspect failed script/image requests as well as `pageerror`. Do not stop another session's server or alter the product to hide the test-host failure.

## OPS-677 — With DOM and Cloudflare Workers types together, append(svg) can select the HTML content signature; appendChild(svg) stays DOM-typed

`측정 2026-10-27 · Astro 7.3.3 · TypeScript DOM + @cloudflare/workers-types`

**증상:** a browser module created a span with `document.createElement('span')`, then moved an existing SVG into it with `icon.append(svg)`. The browser worked, but `astro check` failed with `Argument of type 'SVGSVGElement' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string | Response | ReadableStream<any>'`. The project combined Astro's strict DOM configuration with `types: ['@cloudflare/workers-types']`; the reported content signature is the Workers HTML-rewriting API, rather than a DOM node parameter.

**해결:** use `icon.appendChild(svg)` for this single DOM-node insertion. In this configuration it kept strict checking, passed `astro check` with 0 errors, and the exact released build's browser check still opened the composer on the first tap. The rest of the application also passed 594 tests.

## OPS-678 — Forcing an installed Android web app (WebAPK) to pick up a new manifest: `chrome://webapks` → Update, relaunch, then close the task; it takes the manifest of whatever page is open, HTTP cache included

`측정 2026-10-27 · Pixel 7 Pro (Android 17) · Chrome 156.0.8078.47 · site WebAPK, display: standalone`

**증상:** after changing `theme_color` and `name`, the installed app kept the old values for hours (`dumpsys package <webapk>` showed `versionCode=1`, the old `lastUpdateTime`). `chrome://webapks` cannot be opened by intent or CDP `/json/new`; typed into a new tab's address bar it opens. Its `Update <app>` button raises a JS `alert` (a CDP `Runtime.evaluate` that clicks it hangs until the alert is dismissed on the screen), and the status turns `Pending`, not installed.

What made it apply, measured end to end:
1. Press `Update <app>` (tap with `adb shell input tap`; dismiss the alert with a tap on 확인/OK). Requests within a minute of the previous update are ignored.
2. Launch the app (`adb shell monkey -p <webapk package> -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1`). If the name or icon changed, Chrome shows "이름 및 아이콘 업데이트 검토" (old → new, with 앱 제거 / 확인) on top of the page; 확인 is needed.
3. Close the app's task. Pressing Home or Back is not enough; `adb shell am stack remove <taskId>` (task id from `dumpsys activity recents`, the `Task{… #<id> … A=…:<webapk package>}` line) is. The new APK was installed within about 1 minute (`versionCode` 1 → 2 → 3).

Chrome builds the update from the manifest linked by **the page open at launch**, not from the manifest URL it was installed with, when the manifest `id` matches. A signed-out launch landed on `/` whose `/manifest.webmanifest` (same computed id `/`) replaced the region manifest: `chrome://webapks` then showed `Manifest URL: …/manifest.webmanifest`. That file was served `cache-control: private, max-age=86400`, and the phone's HTTP cache returned the day-old copy, so the app got the old `theme_color` although the server already sent the new one.

**해결:** keep every manifest that shares an `id` identical in name, icons and colours, and serve manifests `no-store` (the region manifests were; the root one was not).
